Jubarte is an in-process Rust Word-document engine for comparison, inspection, edit plans, tracked-change resolution, Markdown conversion, legacy DOC import, validation, scrubbing and PDF/PNG rendering. Native CLI, PyO3/Python and wasm-bindgen/Node/browser surfaces call the shared engine (src/lib.rs:7-35; jubarte-python/Cargo.toml:35-39; jubarte-wasm/Cargo.toml:18-32). A separately installed Python MCP server brokers document tools over stdio under one directory capability; the Gemini extension starts this server with workspacePath as its root (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:67-108,373-381; gemini-extension.json:5-9). Native CLI self-update is a distinct optional network-and-executable-replacement workflow. Tag releases, local registry publication, CI and external Jules review/remediation are conditional maintainer workflows, not document-runtime capabilities.
Jubarte is a local Rust Word-document toolkit exposed through Rust byte APIs, PyO3 Python, WASM/Node, native and language CLIs, and an optional Python MCP server over stdio. Confidential document contents, comments, authorship, embedded media and metadata; inspection text, rendered documents and reports disclose selected document data to their caller (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:131-150,194-218,245-255).

Integrity of source documents and exact edit targets. V1 plans can carry an optional source SHA-256; V2 plans require source.sha256 and refuse mismatches (src/edit.rs:2081-2089; src/edit/v2_apply.rs:84-93).

Host files accessible to the native or Python process; MCP grants a persistent directory capability for document input and generated output, whereas ordinary CLI paths use ambient local authority (src/publication.rs:146-205; jubarte-python/src/lib.rs:1244-1278).

Process memory, CPU, raster memory and availability while parsing, comparing and rendering untrusted documents. Admission limits differ by operation and do not establish comprehensive process resource isolation (src/admission.rs:63-99; src/convert/mod.rs:602-630; SECURITY.md:71-74).

Native executable installation integrity: the updater installs a platform-specific GitHub release binary after checksum verification and an optional compiled-key signature policy (src/update.rs:25-48,198-210,245-257).

Release publication authority and signing material: GitHub release write permission, optional ZIPSIGN_PRIVATE_KEY, local Cargo/npm registry credentials, optional NPM_OTP and UV_PUBLISH_TOKEN (.github/workflows/release.yml:230-263,278-307,356-369; scripts/release.sh:919-959,1063-1069).

Confidential document text, comments, revisions, embedded media/fonts and metadata; emitted Markdown, snapshots, patches, reports, PDFs and PNGs can contain that content. MCP reads return document content; edit/render writes named artifacts (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:131-150,185-217,234-255).

Integrity of source snapshots and authorized clean/tracked output. V1 plans optionally bind source_sha256; V2 requires matching source.sha256. Native CLI rechecks named source against preparation bytes (src/edit.rs:99-106,2073-2105; src/edit/v2_apply.rs:84-99; src/bin/jubarte.rs:1642-1655).

Host CPU, memory and filesystem authority exercised by parsers, image/font decoders and publication. Default admission permits 64 MiB compressed/per part, 256 MiB total inflated, 10,000 entries and depth 256; comparison permits 512 MiB compressed/per part and 2 GiB total (src/admission.rs:63-99).

MCP root document/output files; native host fonts, user font folders and font-index.tsv are separately authorized resources (src/publication.rs:146-199; src/convert/font.rs:2281-2315,2637-2652,3100-3106).

Installed native executable and package integrity. Updater currently trusts release-adjacent SHA256SUMS.txt; compiled signing keys are empty and first-signed-release is None (src/update.rs:25-48,198-210,245-257).

Distinct publication credentials: CI ZIPSIGN_PRIVATE_KEY, release-job GITHUB_TOKEN, operator Cargo credentials, npm login/NPM_OTP and UV_PUBLISH_TOKEN (.github/workflows/release.yml:234-235,261-290,356-369; scripts/release.sh:374-380,919,934-956,1069).

Confidential document contents, comments, authors, metadata, embedded media and source snapshots; transformed DOCX/PDF/PNG/Markdown and diagnostic output may retain or reveal this information. Sources: src/lib.rs:15-29; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:131-135,354-368.

Integrity of source documents, explicitly selected output files, edit reports and tracked-change provenance. Optional source_sha256 guards an edit against stale source bytes; it is not authentication or authorization. Sources: src/edit.rs:2081-2094; SECURITY.md:76-85.

Availability and memory/CPU capacity of the consuming process or browser runtime. Default inspection/edit admission permits 64 MiB compressed input, 10,000 entries, 64 MiB per part and 256 MiB total inflation; compare admission permits 512 MiB compressed/per part and 2 GiB inflation. Both retain depth 256 and XML tag-policy budgets. Sources: src/admission.rs:63-99; src/inspect.rs:604-620; src/edit.rs:2094; src/document_comparer.rs:4922-4927; src/xmllinq/parse.rs:48-65.

MCP's operator-granted directory capability and the files under that directory. The root defaults to the launch working directory or the resolved --root argument. Sources: jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:67-108,373-381; src/publication.rs:146-199.

Host font files and the persistent font index, which can affect rendered output. Native user-font locations are JUBARTE_FONT_DIR when nonempty, otherwise HOME/Library/Application Support/jubarte/fonts on macOS, XDG_DATA_HOME/jubarte/fonts or HOME/.local/share/jubarte/fonts on Linux, and APPDATA/jubarte/fonts on Windows. The default index is font-index.tsv in the parent of the selected font directory, not inside fonts/. JUBARTE_FONT_INDEX overrides that complete filename; empty or off disables persistence. Sources: src/convert/font.rs:2633-2652,3090-3107,3154-3165,3182-3229.

Integrity of the installed native executable and of release archives/checksums. Current compiled updater policy has no trusted release keys and no first signed release, so it checks SHA256SUMS.txt without requiring signatures. Sources: src/update.rs:25-48,198-210,245-257; docs/SELF_UPDATE.md:59-80.

Conditional CI credentials and publication capabilities: release signing key reference ZIPSIGN_PRIVATE_KEY; release job GITHUB_TOKEN with contents:write; JULES_API_KEY and workflow-specific GitHub write permissions for external review agents. Sources: .github/workflows/release.yml:230-265,278-307,356-369; .github/workflows/jules-review.yml:18-50; .github/workflows/jules-el-conejo-review.yml:44-54,260-324.

Confidential source document bytes, text, tracked changes, comments, embedded media and other preserved package parts; generated clean/redline DOCX, PDF/PNG, Markdown diffs and reports contain document-derived information (src/lib.rs:15-30; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:185-218,234-255).

Host filesystem read/write authority: ambient caller-selected CLI/Node paths are different capabilities from the MCP server's held OutputRoot directory. OutputRoot confines relative reads and publication to its directory capability; publish_paths deliberately uses ambient local authority (src/publication.rs:146-226; jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:52-78,106-111).

Integrity of edit targets and resulting review artifacts. Legacy plans optionally bind source_sha256; v2 plans require a structured source hash. These are document-consistency controls, not caller authentication (src/edit.rs:97-106,2081-2088; src/edit/v2.rs:506-531).

Availability and memory/CPU of the embedding native process, Python interpreter, or WASM instance when processing attacker-influenced packages, XML, images, fonts or edit plans. Default admission permits 64 MiB compressed input, 10,000 entries, 64 MiB per part, 256 MiB total inflated bytes and XML depth 256; comparison/WmlDocument uses 512 MiB compressed/per-part and 2 GiB total inflated bytes (src/admission.rs:42-98; src/wml_document.rs:50-57).

Native renderer's host font files and mutable per-user font-index.tsv, including cached face source paths and filesystem metadata. Font-cache writes use ambient filesystem operations and are not mediated by OutputRoot (src/convert/font.rs:2633-2652,3090-3107,3154-3171,3182-3229).

Installed native CLI executable and release provenance. Current updater trust keys are empty and its first-signed-release threshold is unset, so deployed source enforces checksum-only installation unless these constants change (src/update.rs:25-48,198-210,245-257).

Conditional CI secrets and publication capabilities: ZIPSIGN_PRIVATE_KEY is delivered to the signing step, decoded into temporary runner files and used to sign dist/jubarte archives; the release step receives GITHUB_TOKEN as GH_TOKEN and creates release assets (.github/workflows/release.yml:261-309,356-369). Jules review receives JULES_API_KEY and GITHUB_TOKEN with separately declared review permissions (.github/workflows/jules-review.yml:17-50).
trustBoundaries: Document author -> Rust parsing/rendering -> caller process. admission bounds compressed bytes, entry counts, per-part/total inflation and selected XML depth/tag policy; downstream XML, numeric layout, images/fonts and legacy fields require their own effective controls (src/admission.rs:442-580,788-827; src/convert/mod.rs:769-798).

Python/Node/native CLI callers choose ambient local input/output paths; these callers already possess operator file authority. MCP clients instead provide relative document/output names beneath --root, default current working directory; build_server resolves that root once and _OutputRoot retains native cap_std::Dir authority for actual I/O (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:67-112,373-381; jubarte-python/src/lib.rs:1244-1279; src/publication.rs:146-200).

MCP/native rendering -> ambient font resources: JUBARTE_FONT_DIR overrides the platform user font directory; macOS ~/Library/Application Support/jubarte/fonts, Unix $XDG_DATA_HOME/jubarte/fonts or ~/.local/share/jubarte/fonts, Windows %APPDATA%/jubarte/fonts. Fonts are read by conversion outside the document root (src/convert/font.rs:2637-2652).

Rendering -> persistent font index: JUBARTE_FONT_INDEX selects a path; empty/off disables it; default parent(user_font_dir)/font-index.tsv. FONT_INDEX loads that path and save merges and writes path.with_extension(tsv.<pid>.tmp), then renames it to the index (src/convert/font.rs:3100-3107,3213-3229). This is component ambient authority, distinct from tool document/output confinement.

Explicit self-update -> fixed jandira-tech/jubarte-redlines GitHub release and SHA256SUMS.txt -> extracted platform executable -> installed binary. TLS/checksum verification, optional compiled version-gated signing policy, and lstat regular-file hook enforce distinct steps (src/update.rs:25-48,198-257,274-285,299-321; Cargo.toml:137-148).

Privileged release workflows: release.yml optionally signs with secret-store ZIPSIGN_PRIVATE_KEY, computes SHA256SUMS.txt and publishes GitHub assets. Operator scripts/release.sh:976-1012 can recover workflow artifacts into dist/release, compute checksums and create a release without that signing step.

Caller-supplied DOCX/ZIP/XML/media/fonts cross into the host engine. Admission counts actual inflation, checks package identity, names and XML limits; production archive opening rejects header/extent/special-entry defects. Low-level permissive parse_xdocument does not apply input policy: callers of raw XML APIs must select checked parsing or prevalidate. The deliberate debug archive reader is an inspection exception (src/admission.rs:13-28,439-566; src/opc/archive.rs:20-51; src/xmllinq/parse.rs:21-36,98-135; SECURITY.md:132-139).

Legacy DOC is a separate OLE/FIB/piece-table parser, not a ZIP-admission path. It converts the supported main story to Markdown/DOCX and explicitly excludes encrypted/obfuscated and older Word formats (src/legacy_doc.rs:13-50).

Edit-plan author transfers requested mutations and optionally source identity to the engine. Schema version and a supplied source_sha256 are checked; the v1 source guard is optional, not an authorization or mandatory freshness credential (src/edit.rs:97-106,2072-2094). Filesystem publication is a separate boundary from in-memory edit acceptance.

Native CLI uses ambient caller-selected output paths. publish_paths holds each parent directory, stages into parent/.jubarte-<uuid>.partial/bytes, uses Unix staging mode 0700, and commits per file; OutputRoot additionally validates portable relative names and confines capability-relative I/O. Multi-file publication is explicitly not atomic across the set, and errors record already committed files (src/publication.rs:83-143,146-225,228-273,420-505). Python and npm general-output helpers instead directly call Path.write_bytes/fs.writeFileSync; native publication controls cannot be assumed for those helpers (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/__main__.py:101-113,126-132; jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:76-79,106-110).

MCP caller gains document read/write operations only within the operator-selected root. Python resolve-based checks are early diagnostics; native cap-std OutputRoot owns the actual read/write confinement. overwrite is caller-controlled, false by default; annotations are hints, not per-tool authorization. stdio possession is the transport access boundary; no distinct users/tenants are established by this adapter (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:54-55,67-108,152-160,373-381; src/publication.rs:146-199).

Native Markdown image references cross from document content into local reads. Effective resource root is --resource-path or the Markdown file's parent, falling back to current directory. Percent-decoded targets must canonically remain under that root and actual reads use its held OutputRoot capability; URL schemes are refused. The library's image callback is separately supplied by the embedding caller, while Python/npm CLI reject resource_path support (src/bin/jubarte.rs:2811-2870,2936-2943,3365-3400; src/markdown/mod.rs:196-198; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/__main__.py:1057-1064; jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:724-727).

Native/Python rendering may read installed fonts and update the ambient per-user/configured index even when invoked through MCP. MCP's document-path capability is not a whole-process filesystem sandbox. Browser/WASM uses embedded/bundled faces rather than installed fonts; its byte APIs do not expose native OutputRoot publication (src/convert/font.rs:2258-2285,2633-2652,3095-3107,3182-3229; README.md:901-920; Cargo.toml:149-152).

Self-update crosses from GitHub release service/assets into executable replacement. Noninteractive operation requires --check or --yes; a terminal otherwise confirms replacement. Default selection installs newer versions; explicit --version permits downgrade. Unix archive member is jubarte-<version>-<target>/jubarte, Windows member ends jubarte.exe; an extracted regular-file verification hook runs before the delegated swap. Current release keys are empty, so signature support is compiled but not enforcing (src/update.rs:91-124,144-160,186-257,307-320).

Tag-triggered release builders have contents:read; the separate release job has contents:write. Archives/wheels are downloaded into dist, optional signing rewrites archives before SHA256SUMS.txt generation, then gh publishes dist/* to the tag. The signing private key is step-scoped and decoded into a temporary directory removed by EXIT trap (.github/workflows/release.yml:15-21,51-89,230-285,297-307,317-322,356-369).

Local scripts/release.sh uses the operator's separate registry credentials, validates tool/auth availability, verifies the tagged engine stamp and prompts for the exact version unless YES bypass applies. It also executes an external app checkout's scripts/release-engine.sh selected by JUBARTE_APP_DIR or jubarte-app; that external implementation and its downstream authority are absent from this repository (scripts/release.sh:374-389,870-899,919,934-956,1069).

Ordinary PR CI crosses into self-hosted execution with contents:read and persist-credentials:false; those settings govern GitHub-token persistence/permissions, not runner filesystem isolation. Jules review and companion remediation are independent grants: reviewer action receives PR/check-write GitHub token and Jules key, with enable_approve:false; remediation permits only configured trusted author/dispatcher/event combinations, then requests AUTO_CREATE_PR with require_plan_approval:false and starting_branch equal to mutable PR head_ref. The static analysis checkout is bound to head_sha, but the external session input is a branch name (.github/workflows/ci.yml:13-46; .github/workflows/jules-review.yml:20-50; .github/workflows/jules-el-conejo-review.yml:74-102,261-272,320-324).

Gemini extension startup passes --from jubarte-redlines[mcp] without a version pin to uvx; package resolution is host/package-manager authority before MCP opens workspacePath as root (gemini-extension.json:5-9).

Untrusted document suppliers cross into in-process ZIP/XML/media parsing. Admission applies configured byte/count/depth budgets and bounded inflated reads; shared archive opening applies zip_defects before use. Direct unchecked archive opening is retained for diagnostic inspection: src/admission.rs:439; src/admission.rs:531; src/opc/archive.rs:20; src/opc/archive.rs:42.

Public checked XML parsing validates before DOM construction; permissive parse_xdocument remains a different API whose caller must establish appropriate trust/admission. Tag defaults include 1,024 attributes, 1,024-byte qualified attribute names, 64 MiB attribute values and 128 MiB start tags: src/xmllinq/parse.rs:49; src/xmllinq/parse.rs:119; src/xmllinq/parse.rs:134.

MCP caller arguments cross into host document reads and publication. Python resolves paths for early diagnostics, while native _OutputRoot performs capability-relative read/publish using the directory held by publication::OutputRoot. Tool annotations are hints to the host, not an approval or per-tool authorization mechanism: jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:72; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:75; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:84; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:101; jubarte-python/src/lib.rs:1254; jubarte-python/src/lib.rs:1260; jubarte-python/src/lib.rs:1265; docs/adoption/mcp.md:39.

Native CLI and Python CLI callers already possess ambient local path authority. CLI publication uses publish_paths; Python CLI reads caller-specified paths. Their authority must not be conflated with the MCP root capability: src/publication.rs:211; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/__main__.py:61; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/__main__.py:73.

Rendering crosses from document-requested font families into ambient platform/configured font resources and cache writes. JUBARTE_FONT_DIR controls the font folder; JUBARTE_FONT_INDEX independently overrides or disables the index; absent override, the index is parent(font-folder)/font-index.tsv. These operations use std::fs rather than MCP OutputRoot: src/convert/font.rs:2637; src/convert/font.rs:3100; src/convert/font.rs:3165; src/convert/font.rs:3213.

Explicit updater crosses from GitHub release authority into installed executable replacement. It selects a platform-specific archive/member, requests SHA256SUMS.txt verification and checks the extracted binary is a regular file. Signature verification is conditional, and this source has RELEASE_KEYS=[] and FIRST_SIGNED_RELEASE=None: src/update.rs:25; src/update.rs:44; src/update.rs:48; src/update.rs:91; src/update.rs:104; src/update.rs:198; src/update.rs:245; src/update.rs:308.

Tag-triggered CI builds cross into a privileged release job with contents:write. Only the signing step receives ZIPSIGN_PRIVATE_KEY, which is decoded into ephemeral runner files; the publication step receives GITHUB_TOKEN and uploads dist/* to the current repository release: .github/workflows/release.yml:15; .github/workflows/release.yml:20; .github/workflows/release.yml:230; .github/workflows/release.yml:234; .github/workflows/release.yml:263; .github/workflows/release.yml:278; .github/workflows/release.yml:285; .github/workflows/release.yml:358; .github/workflows/release.yml:364.

npm edit plan recording has its own basename/PID partial-file publication path (jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:408-425,442-445). It uses ambient Node filesystem authority and does not inherit native Rust private-staging controls. Intentional resolution of the caller-selected plan symlink is distinct from an attacker-selected staging symlink.

Redaction and metadata scrub cross from document-retained parts into an asserted outgoing privacy postcondition. BOM UTF-16 auxiliary XML is admitted/preserved (src/admission.rs:764-780; src/opc/mod.rs:368-376,659-664), while leak checking must interpret that same representation (src/scrub.rs:467-475; src/edit.rs:4727-4747). Property discovery must follow package relationship targets rather than only fixed conventional paths (src/scrub.rs:39-43,357-384).

Untrusted package bytes cross into ZIP/OPC/XML parsing and rendering. Admission prechecks budgets, checks duplicate entries and shared ZIP structural defects, and bounds actual inflated reads rather than trusting declared sizes (src/admission.rs:439-470,531-535). The shared checked ZIP opener rejects defects; debug is an intentional unchecked diagnostic exception (src/opc/archive.rs:15-19,34-51). Checked XML APIs and raw permissive DOM APIs are separate caller contracts, explicitly distinguished by SECURITY.md:51-65.

Untrusted legacy DOC is a separate OLE/FIB/piece-table parsing path, subsequently converted into Markdown/DOCX; it is not covered merely by identifying DOCX ZIP admission (src/legacy_doc.rs:13-50). Embedded fonts, image decoders and layout are additional native parser surfaces identified by Cargo.toml:107-110.

Native CLI operators select ambient input/output paths. src/bin/jubarte.rs:261-273 invokes publication::publish_paths, whose root=None backend opens output parents with ambient authority (src/publication.rs:203-225,431-446). Outputs stage beside their destination in .jubarte-<UUID>.partial/bytes, with Unix staging directory mode 0700 and exclusive creation (src/publication.rs:472-505). Publication stages all files first but commits per file; failures can leave named committed outputs, and Windows directory synchronization is intentionally a no-op (src/publication.rs:100-130,168-174,387-405). This is not an all-files transaction.

Python and Node CLI callers retain ambient local filesystem authority. Python's _read_side consumes caller paths and _write calls Path.write_bytes; Node's read and write helpers call fs.readFileSync/writeFileSync (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/__main__.py:73-83,126-133; jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:52-56,106-111). Native staged-publication properties cannot be assumed for these helpers.

The MCP operator grants a directory root once; a connected stdio client can invoke all registered read/write tools within that grant. --root defaults to current working directory, is expanded/resolved, and must be a directory; no HTTP listener or application authentication is configured in this entrypoint (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:373-381). Python containment checks are early diagnostics; actual reads and publications use _native._OutputRoot, backed by cap_std directory authority and portable relative-write validation (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:69-108; jubarte-python/src/lib.rs:1244-1278; src/publication.rs:153-199,228-273,431-463). overwrite is a per-call replacement capability, defaulting false. ToolAnnotations are metadata, not a separate authorization layer (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:54-55,153-160).

CLI Markdown image targets cross into local filesystem reads only through a selected resource root: explicit --resource-path wins, otherwise the Markdown file's parent, otherwise '.' (src/bin/jubarte.rs:2937-2943). The loader canonicalizes and holds that directory capability, applies image policy and reads relative to the capability; URLs are not fetched by this loader (src/bin/jubarte.rs:2851-2877). This capability is separate from output publication authority.

Native renderer font discovery is ambient OS-account access, independent of MCP's document/output root. JUBARTE_FONT_DIR overrides per-user locations; absent it, Windows uses APPDATA/jubarte/fonts, macOS HOME/Library/Application Support/jubarte/fonts, and other native platforms XDG_DATA_HOME/jubarte/fonts or HOME/.local/share/jubarte/fonts (src/convert/font.rs:2633-2652). Native discovery also examines named system/Word font directories and HOME/Library/Group Containers/UBF8T346G9.Office/FontCache/4/CloudFonts/<family>; the document-supplied family must be a single normal path component for that derived cloud directory (src/convert/font.rs:2225-2236,2281-2309).

Browser/Node WASM callers pass byte arrays and JSON options into the engine. The bindings disable default engine features, omit native publication on wasm32 and support comparison-budget overrides; the binding explicitly warns that its 2 GiB inflated default can exceed practical WASM heap capacity (jubarte-wasm/Cargo.toml:18-23; src/lib.rs:163-165; jubarte-wasm/src/lib.rs:63-97). Hosting applications own admission tuning, upload authorization, origin policy, worker isolation and persistence.

Explicit jubarte self-update crosses from GitHub release metadata/assets into executable replacement. Repo is jandira-tech/jubarte-redlines; the chosen archive member is jubarte-<version>-<platform>/jubarte[.exe]; SHA256SUMS.txt is configured; extracted binary must lstat as a regular file (src/update.rs:25-27,91-109,198-210,299-321). Without --check/--yes, noninteractive runs stop before lookup; installation requires confirmation unless --yes; explicitly selected versions may downgrade (src/update.rs:120-125,144-160,234-247). Current RELEASE_KEYS=[] and FIRST_SIGNED_RELEASE=None mean signature enforcement is inactive (src/update.rs:44-48,274-285).

Tag-driven GitHub release automation builds platform archives/wheels with read-only job permissions, then a separate contents:write job signs when configured, computes checksums and publishes dist/* to the triggering tag's release (.github/workflows/release.yml:15-21,51-89,230-275,295-321,356-369). The signing secret is scoped to the signing step, decoded into RUNNER_TEMP/zipsign.<random>/keyN and removed by an EXIT trap; the signing tool and runner are recipients of this authority (.github/workflows/release.yml:261-307).

The local release script separately publishes the Rust package, both npm packages and PyPI artifacts. Typed version confirmation precedes pushing unless YES is set, then each registry operation uses its own tool/account authority (scripts/release.sh:877-919,929-959,1063-1069). The script calls a downstream app checkout, but that application's implementation is absent from this repository and is not included as inspected architecture (scripts/release.sh:141-175).

PR automation crosses repository-controlled PR source, descriptions and tool output into external actions and agent sessions. The normal review workflow excludes fork/Dependabot PRs and grants contents:read, pull-requests:write and checks:write; companion remediation additionally gates session creation on TRUSTED_USERS=['arthrod'] and selected events, uses AUTO_CREATE_PR and require_plan_approval=false (.github/workflows/jules-review.yml:19-50; .github/workflows/jules-el-conejo-review.yml:35-52,259-272,320-324). External action internals, Jules integration permissions and runtime restrictions are not present here.

CI/docs workflows execute checked-out repository code on self-hosted runners for pull_request events. Workflow token permissions are contents:read and checkout disables persisted credentials, but host filesystem, network, persistent-state isolation and runner admission controls are external deployment controls (.github/workflows/ci.yml:13-40,72-99; .github/workflows/docs.yml:42-86,98-99).

Validated audit refinements: package admission's extension-based selection does not cover relationship-resolved notes with non-XML suffixes (src/admission.rs:533-570; src/document_comparer.rs:6318-6328,6461-6479). Admission also ignores DTD while the raw DOM disagrees on declaration boundaries (src/admission.rs:798-820; src/xmllinq/parse.rs:539-547,660-662). These are findings, not assertions that the intended policy is fully enforced.

Untrusted DOCX/ZIP/XML bytes cross into package admission and then DOM/document operations. Opened::open admits using default limits, normalizes Strict packages and opens/parses within those limits. General rendering calls admit_package before package/DOM construction. The common archive opener rejects reported structural defects, while the deliberately unchecked opener supports triage and admission's own typed checks (src/inspect.rs:604-622; src/convert/mod.rs:769-798; src/opc/archive.rs:15-51).

Raw XML library callers choose between checked and permissive APIs. try_parse_xdocument_with_limits validates before constructing the DOM; parse_xdocument explicitly requires a prior gate and does not enforce input policy itself. Shared defaults include 1,024 element attributes, 1,024 attribute-name bytes, 64 MiB attribute values and 128 MiB start tags (src/xmllinq/parse.rs:25-36,48-57,91-98,119-135).

Edit requests cross from caller-authored plans to document mutations. V1 checks a supplied source hash, refuses blank authors and signed/macro-bearing inputs; V2 requires the exact source hash and resolves scope/context before operations. These are document-consistency controls, not user authentication or authorization (src/edit.rs:2072-2105; src/edit/v2_apply.rs:84-110). Dry run and application share in-memory preparation; filesystem publication remains a separate host operation (src/edit/prepared.rs:5-13,157-186).

JUBARTE_FONT_INDEX overrides the index path; empty/off disables it; otherwise the default is user_font_dir().parent()/font-index.tsv. Effective default font directories are macOS $HOME/Library/Application Support/jubarte/fonts, Linux $XDG_DATA_HOME/jubarte/fonts else $HOME/.local/share/jubarte/fonts, Windows $APPDATA/jubarte/fonts. The default index is one directory above, font-index.tsv. Windows system font roots use WINDIR else SystemRoot else C:\Windows, plus LOCALAPPDATA/Microsoft/Windows/Fonts; Office cloud cache is $HOME/Library/Group Containers/UBF8T346G9.Office/FontCache/4/CloudFonts.

JS host to WASM: compare accepts borrowed document bytes plus JSON limit overrides and returns bytes/errors. Browser/Node package entrypoints are separate generated loaders; native publication is cfg-excluded on wasm32. Node CLI filesystem authority belongs to its JS adapter, not to the WASM byte API (jubarte-wasm/src/lib.rs:65-98; jubarte-wasm/npm/package.json:34-75; src/lib.rs:163-165; jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:16-21,52-55,106-111).

Operator to updater to release infrastructure: only explicit self-update enters this flow. Fixed repository jandira-tech/jubarte-redlines, target-specific asset and SHA256SUMS.txt feed self_update; --check does not install; confirmation or --yes precedes installation. RELEASE_KEYS is empty and FIRST_SIGNED_RELEASE is None, so this checkout enforces checksum-only updates. A regular-file verification hook rejects extracted symlink/nonregular binaries before swap (src/update.rs:25-48,186-210,223-257,307-321). Windows enables ZIP extraction while other shipped targets use tar.gz (Cargo.toml:144-155; docs/SELF_UPDATE.md:25-36). Archive assets are jubarte-<version>-<target>.tar.gz or .zip, containing jubarte-<version>-<target>/jubarte[.exe]; the independent architecture reviewer inspected self_update 1.3.1 common builder lines1106-1108 and found the install destination defaults to std::env::current_exe(). No actual deployed executable path was queried.

Maintainer/tag authority to public distribution: v* tags trigger release builds; build jobs have contents:read and release job contents:write. Optional ZIPSIGN_PRIVATE_KEY is provided to the signing step, decoded under RUNNER_TEMP/zipsign.<random>/keyN and removed by trap; signed archives precede checksum generation. GH_TOKEN references GITHUB_TOKEN for gh release create, publishing dist/* to the tagged repository release. The maintainer script separately publishes crates.io jubarte-redlines, npm jubarte-wasm and jubarte-redlines, and PyPI jubarte-redlines using operator-held credentials (.github/workflows/release.yml:15-21,230-308,317-321,356-369; scripts/release.sh:886-899,919,935-954,1069).

Legacy DOC logical mapping and field-state boundaries are distinct from ZIP/XML policy: the convert branch materializes DOCX only after legacy decoding, and public legacy read directly expands pieces and parses field state (src/bin/jubarte.rs:3125-3144; src/legacy_doc.rs:180-215,1084-1109,1181-1221,1591-1620). Public scrub::leaks performs bounded ZIP reads but invokes raw XML DOM construction separately (src/scrub.rs:403-469,527-530). These are source-backed availability scenarios retained as findings, without assuming remote deployment.

Untrusted package bytes cross into the shared engine through admission and OPC parsing. Default agent inspection/editing limits are 64 MiB compressed, 64 MiB per part, 256 MiB total inflated, 10,000 entries and XML depth 256; comparison and rendering use 512 MiB compressed/per part and 2 GiB total inflated, with the same entry/depth defaults. Explicit InputLimitOverrides replace individual base fields and reject unknown keys (src/admission.rs:63-108,137-163; src/inspect.rs:606-615; src/convert/mod.rs:769-778; src/document_comparer.rs:4927).

ZIP metadata crosses a parser-consistency boundary before normal package processing. Admission checks defects explicitly; the shared normal opener rejects divergent headers, overlapping extents and special entry types. Reads remain in memory rather than extracting document entries to the host filesystem. The debug diagnostic opener intentionally bypasses those structural refusals to inspect rejected packages (src/admission.rs:439-470,516-554; src/opc/archive.rs:15-51).

Checked XML and permissive DOM parsing are distinct capabilities. Checked APIs apply well-formedness, tag and namespace policy; parse_xdocument deliberately does not enforce input policy, so direct library callers must validate first. Tag defaults include 1,024 attributes, 1,024-byte attribute names, 64 MiB attribute values and 128 MiB start tags; other namespace limits also exist (src/xmllinq/parse.rs:44-65,84-114).

Edit requests cross from caller intent into document mutation. V1 hashes are optional, V2 source hashes mandatory; exact target resolution and shared preparation are separate from filesystem publication. Source hash agreement is a consistency guard, not caller authentication (src/edit.rs:2081-2094; src/edit/v2_apply.rs:74-93; src/edit/prepared.rs:185-230).

MCP clients invoke document tools through stdio, not an evidenced network listener. --root defaults to startup cwd; the expanded resolved root is opened once as a native OutputRoot. Input paths receive an early containment diagnostic, while actual reads and writes use the held cap-std directory capability. Explicit tool overwrite flags authorize replacing existing outputs; tool annotations are hints rather than an independent authorization mechanism (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:54-55,67-108,373-381; jubarte-python/src/lib.rs:1244-1278; src/publication.rs:146-199).

MCP output locations are root/out_dir/clean.docx, redline.docx, patch.diff, report.json and optional redline.pdf/redline-page-NN.png for editing; rendering uses root/out_dir/page-NN.png and optional render.pdf. OutputRoot validates portable relative paths, stages all files before committing, and commits atomically per file, not as one atomic set (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:161-218,229-255; src/publication.rs:100-143,168-199,228-245).

Native CLI filesystem publication is explicitly ambient: it opens and holds each selected parent directory and stages outputs. Python CLI and npm CLI have their own host filesystem adapters that read user paths and perform direct writes; those adapters must not inherit MCP confinement or native staged-publication guarantees by implication (src/publication.rs:203-225; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/__main__.py:73-89,101-133; jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:52-78,106-110).

Native rendering has an independent ambient font-reading capability. Document font names select installed-font searches; JUBARTE_FONT_DIR overrides platform user font directories. macOS/Unix defaults derive HOME and XDG_DATA_HOME; Windows uses APPDATA for Jubarte fonts and WINDIR/SystemRoot plus LOCALAPPDATA for installed fonts. macOS cloud fonts derive HOME/Library/Group Containers/UBF8T346G9.Office/FontCache/4/CloudFonts/<family>; the direct family component is checked. Font bytes feed shaping and output generation (src/convert/font.rs:2225-2236,2241-2255,2281-2315,2633-2652,2831-2862).

Browser WASM accepts byte inputs and returns byte/text results; host filesystem publication is excluded from wasm32, while the Node CLI itself supplies ambient Node filesystem operations. WASM uses the same Rust engine with default features disabled and cli enabled, and its release profile aborts on panic (src/lib.rs:163-165; jubarte-wasm/Cargo.toml:18-35,64-69; jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:16-21,52-78,106-110).

Self-update crosses from GitHub release assets into replacement of the running executable. The repository is fixed to jandira-tech/jubarte-redlines, sums asset to SHA256SUMS.txt, and binary archive member to jubarte-<version>-<platform>/jubarte[.exe]. It refuses noninteractive install without --yes or --check, checks the selected version, and verifies an extracted regular file. RELEASE_KEYS is currently empty and FIRST_SIGNED_RELEASE is None, so present builds consume checksum-only updates; Windows ZIP and Unix tar extraction are delegated to self_update (src/update.rs:25-48,91-108,120-125,198-210,240-285,299-320).

Maintainer publication is separate from runtime document handling. Tag pushes v* trigger release builds with read-only contents permission; only the final release job has contents:write. Optional signing keys are decoded under RUNNER_TEMP/zipsign.<random>/keyN with exit cleanup and passed to zipsign; release assets and SHA256SUMS.txt are uploaded using a job GITHUB_TOKEN supplied as GH_TOKEN. The local release script separately publishes to crates.io, npm and PyPI, with an explicit version confirmation unless --yes (.github/workflows/release.yml:15-25,51-55,230-307,317-321,356-369; scripts/release.sh:875-899,919-959,1063-1069).

Native rendering also persists a font index outside the MCP document/output capability. JUBARTE_FONT_INDEX overrides the location (empty/off disables it); otherwise the consumer reads/writes user_font_dir().parent()/font-index.tsv, with temporary extension tsv.<pid>.tmp. Defaults are $HOME/Library/Application Support/jubarte/font-index.tsv on macOS, $XDG_DATA_HOME/jubarte/font-index.tsv or $HOME/.local/share/jubarte/font-index.tsv on Linux, and %APPDATA%\jubarte\font-index.tsv on Windows. With custom JUBARTE_FONT_DIR, the index is in that directory's parent. Recipients are the renderer, subsequent renderer processes and local readers permitted by host ACLs. Controls are trusted environment/configuration, delimiter filtering, cached length/mtime checks and write-then-rename; this is ambient std::fs authority, not OutputRoot confinement (src/convert/font.rs:2637-2652,3090-3107,3154-3229,3264-3275).

Untrusted DOCX crosses ZIP/OPC admission: pre-index budgets, ZIP structural/canonical-name checks, encryption/compression refusal, bounded inflation and XML policy (src/admission.rs:439-569). OPC independently checks archive defects, bounded reads and case-insensitive duplicates (src/opc/archive.rs:34-51; src/opc/mod.rs:282-350,497-524). Rendering admits before normalization/layout (src/convert/mod.rs:769-798).

Raw XML parse_xdocument intentionally skips input policy; try_parse_xdocument_with_limits validates first. Callers of raw API own prior admission (src/xmllinq/parse.rs:88-135). Tag defaults are 1,024 attributes, 1,024-byte names, 64 MiB values and 128 MiB tags (src/xmllinq/parse.rs:48-65).

Edit plans cross into mutation using schema/source checks, exact anchors and preparation gates; author labels are not authenticated identities. V1 rejects macro-bearing/signed packages and checks optional source hash; V2 rejects mismatching source hash before operation resolution (src/edit.rs:97-108,2073-2105; src/edit/v2_apply.rs:84-111).

Native CLI uses ambient operator filesystem authority. publish_paths holds parents, stages/verifies bytes and installs via overwrite rename or no-clobber hard link, atomic per file rather than per set (src/publication.rs:168-174,203-225,419-505,534-570). Python/Node ordinary CLI path writes have different controls (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/__main__.py:101-133; jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:76-80,106-111).

MCP client arguments cross a server-granted directory capability. Startup resolves --root once; diagnostics precede capability-relative actual reads/writes. Portable relative-name checks, overwrite opt-in and output-symlink refusal apply (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:67-108,373-381; jubarte-python/src/lib.rs:1244-1278; src/publication.rs:146-199,228-273,431-463). All connected stdio clients receive registered tools; annotations are hints rather than per-user authorization (mcp_server.py:54-55,126-159,258-277, relative to jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines).

Native Markdown image loading separately grants --resource-path, otherwise Markdown parent or '.'. Percent decoding precedes scheme/containment checks and capability reads; operator chooses trusted root (src/bin/jubarte.rs:2811-2877,2936-2943). Python/Node reject resource_path; byte conversion defaults to no image callback (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/__main__.py:1057-1064; jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:724-727; src/markdown/mod.rs:159-198,226).

Native font discovery reads system/Word, macOS Office CloudFonts/<family>, and configured/per-user fonts. Cloud family must be a single normal component. Index-named files are read after length/mtime checks; ambient cache persistence is independent of MCP root (src/convert/mod.rs:806-857; src/convert/font.rs:2225-2236,2258-2315,2637-2652,2855-2862,3154-3188,3213-3227).
Maintainer debug intentionally uses open_archive_unchecked after budget preflight, reports defects and continues, unlike ordinary refusal paths (src/debug.rs:206-222; src/opc/archive.rs:15-19).

Native updater downloads fixed repository/platform release assets, checks adjacent checksum and extracted regular-file type, and requires terminal confirmation or --yes; --check does not install. Empty signing keys disable required signatures (src/update.rs:25-48,91-108,120-125,198-257,299-320).

Tag CI separates read-only build from contents:write release. Signing-step secret is decoded below RUNNER_TEMP/zipsign.<random>/keyN and cleaned on exit. Separate GitHub token publishes dist/*; operator script independently publishes Cargo, npm engine/CLI and PyPI (.github/workflows/release.yml:15-21,54-55,230-290,303-321,356-369; scripts/release.sh:875-919,934-956,1039-1069).

Contributor pull_request jobs check out contributor code onto self-hosted runners also selected by main pushes; their local action configures a private mbx cache endpoint and documents persistent checkout/store use (.github/workflows/ci.yml:13-16,34-48,72-99; .github/actions/mbx/action.yml:8-12,20-38). External approval and runner isolation controls remain unknown.

Legacy DOC crosses OLE/FIB/piece decoding then field-block processing before Markdown/DOCX generation; physical chain bounds do not establish logical story or field-work limits (src/legacy_doc.rs:180-215,1090-1225,1596-1619). Embedded WMF crosses binary record decoding to owned text and raster output; MAX_SIDE bounds only pixels (src/convert/metafile.rs:25-31,477-489,603-620,692-700).

Document supplier to engine process: supplied ZIP/XML/media bytes are untrusted. Admission checks container budgets, names, duplicate identities, encryption/compression and XML policy before higher-level processing; package opens independently apply ZIP header/extent/special-entry consistency checks and bounded package construction. No package extraction to host files is part of this processing. Inspection/edit use default limits; comparison and rendering use the roomier compare policy. Sources: src/admission.rs:13-28,439-495; src/opc/archive.rs:15-51; src/opc/mod.rs:275-284,497-523; src/inspect.rs:604-622; src/convert/mod.rs:769-778.

Unchecked XML to DOM is a separate library boundary: parse_xdocument is permissive and does not enforce policy. Untrusted XML must pass validate_xml/try_parse_xdocument or admission with active limits first. This is not a schema-validity guarantee. Sources: src/xmllinq/parse.rs:19-36,84-90; SECURITY.md:51-69.

Edit-plan author to document transformation: plans select anchored operations and may carry a SHA-256 source guard. A guard mismatch returns STALE_SOURCE; omitting the optional guard is supported. This binds requested edits to bytes when present, not to a user identity or externally approved publication. Sources: src/edit.rs:106,2074-2094; SECURITY.md:76-85.

Native CLI to host filesystem: CLI publication deliberately grants ambient access to caller-selected paths. It uses held parent directory handles, staging and per-file atomic replacement; the complete file set is not atomic. Existing-file replacement requires overwrite/force, and rooted publication has stricter symlink policy than ambient publication. Sources: src/bin/jubarte.rs:261-273; src/publication.rs:168-174,203-225,419-480.

Python CLI and Node CLI are separate filesystem consumers, not automatically protected by native CLI publication. Python Document.read uses Path.read_bytes, Python CLI _write uses Path.write_bytes, and Node CLI read/write use fs.readFileSync/fs.writeFileSync. They run with their host process's ambient filesystem authority. Sources: jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/document.py:141-145; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/__main__.py:116-133; jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:52-79,106-110.

MCP stdio caller to rooted document I/O: the operator chooses an existing resolved root; client paths get early containment diagnostics, but native OutputRoot/cap-std directory-relative reads and publication enforce the actual boundary. Publication validates relative export names, refuses output symlinks and enforces overwrite in the native backend. ToolAnnotations are hints, not the enforcing authorization. The server exposes stdio, without a repository-provided user/session/tenant authentication layer. Sources: jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:54-55,67-108,373-381; jubarte-python/src/lib.rs:1244-1276; src/publication.rs:146-199,228-240,431-463.

Markdown image references to native CLI filesystem access: --resource-path selects the trusted resource root; otherwise the Markdown file's parent, or '.', is used. URL schemes are refused after percent decoding; canonical containment and an opened OutputRoot capability confine the actual file read. Library image loaders remain caller-supplied capabilities and default to absent. Sources: src/bin/jubarte.rs:2835-2877,2936-2943; src/markdown/mod.rs:159-170.

Native renderer to host fonts is independent of MCP's document-root capability. The renderer searches configured user fonts, fixed macOS/Word directories, Windows system/user font directories and Word's HOME-relative cloud-font cache. Document font-family names must be a single normal component for direct cloud-folder derivation. Font-index entries can name face files; loading checks recorded metadata before reading them. Index persistence uses ordinary host filesystem operations and a sibling font-index.tsv.<pid>.tmp followed by rename. Sources: src/convert/font.rs:2181-2216,2225-2235,2263-2304,2633-2652,2814-2828,2855-2862,3098-3107,3154-3165,3213-3229.

Browser/WASM caller to byte APIs: wasm-bindgen passes bytes and explicit options into shared Rust operations; the WASM package omits self-update, and browser/WASM has no host publication dependency. Default comparison inflation allowance exceeds a 32-bit WASM heap, so the host must lower it for its workload. Node CLI filesystem access is host JavaScript authority outside this byte API. Sources: jubarte-wasm/Cargo.toml:18-32; jubarte-wasm/src/lib.rs:77-97; Cargo.toml:150-153; jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:52-79,106-110.

Operator to native self-updater to release publisher: explicit invocation, check/yes/interactive preflight and optional confirmation gate installation. Repository and binary/archive naming are fixed to jandira-tech/jubarte-redlines, jubarte-<version>-<target>/jubarte[.exe], with tar.gz for Unix targets and ZIP support on Windows. The self_update dependency owns retrieval, staging and executable replacement; the application supplies SHA256SUMS.txt verification and a post-extraction regular-file hook. Current signature policy is checksum-only. Sources: src/update.rs:25-48,91-108,120-124,186-257,307-320; Cargo.toml:137-148.

Tag publisher to release CI: v* tag pushes trigger builds; the release job receives contents:write separately from read-only build jobs. The signing secret, when present, is decoded under RUNNER_TEMP/zipsign.<random>/keyN and supplied to zipsign for dist/jubarte-*.tar.gz and dist/jubarte-*.zip. The publish step supplies GITHUB_TOKEN as GH_TOKEN to gh release create for github.repository and uploads dist/*. Signing is conditional and currently not required by compiled updater keys. Sources: .github/workflows/release.yml:15-21,51-55,230-307,317-322,356-369.

PR source to CI runner: main pushes and pull_request events run repository build/lint commands on self-hosted runners, with contents:read and checkout credential persistence disabled. Token scope does not define host isolation; runner lifecycle, filesystem/network isolation, secret residency and GitHub approval settings are not supplied by repository source. Sources: .github/workflows/ci.yml:13-48; .github/workflows/docs.yml:42-48,76-88.

PR review/remediation workflows to external agents are separate capabilities. Jules PR Review excludes forks and Dependabot, passes JULES_API_KEY plus GITHUB_TOKEN to a pinned external action, grants PR/check write permissions and disables approval. Jules el conejo separately resolves a same-repository PR, checks out the resolved head SHA, and allows only configured trusted actors/authors to start the external AUTO_CREATE_PR session; it passes JULES_API_KEY, starting_branch and require_plan_approval:false. The external action/service implementations and their actual repository-write authorization are absent from this checkout and were not fetched. Sources: .github/workflows/jules-review.yml:18-50; .github/workflows/jules-el-conejo-review.yml:35-54,65-102,260-324.

Document producer to shared Rust parser: caller-controlled DOCX/legacy DOC/XML/media enters package admission, OPC handling, DOM construction, editing and rendering. Admission enforces configurable archive and XML limits; WmlDocument first admits under the comparison budget before opening the package. Library unsafe Rust is forbidden, but dependency safety and process resource limits remain separate controls (src/admission.rs:42-98,399-448,486-543; src/wml_document.rs:50-57; src/lib.rs:85-87; SECURITY.md:38-74).

ZIP central/local metadata to OPC package identity: production open_archive wraps unchecked archive open and validates defects; admission runs the defect pass while preserving typed refusal. Debug inspection intentionally has a different acceptance mode and must not be treated as the production admission boundary (src/opc/archive.rs:20-44,339-364,388-484; src/admission.rs:439-448; SECURITY.md:111-136).

Raw XML caller to DOM: checked APIs are the intended policy boundary; infallible parse_xdocument deliberately does not enforce input policy. A caller invoking raw low-level APIs owns admission obligations rather than gaining protection solely by linking the crate (SECURITY.md:43-66; src/wml_document.rs:85-96).

Agent/client to MCP filesystem broker: startup resolves --root, defaulting to cwd, opens _native._OutputRoot once, and serves stdio. Tool paths receive early Python containment checks, but actual reads/publication use the native directory capability; annotation hints are descriptive metadata rather than independent authorization. Every connected caller receives the configured tool capabilities; no per-user ownership or tenant model is established by this source (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:54-55,67-108,373-381; src/publication.rs:146-200).

MCP edit intent to published artifacts: docx_edit resolves a plan in memory, constructs clean.docx, redline.docx, patch.diff and report.json under caller-selected out_dir inside root, optionally adds rendered artifacts, then calls the broker's publish operation. Invalid plans are reported before publication; actual filesystem publication is atomic per file, not across the output set, and errors identify already committed files (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:153-218; src/publication.rs:83-143,168-199). No human approval boundary is implemented or claimed here.

Local CLI caller to ambient host publication: native publish_paths grants explicit local path authority, while Node's wrapper directly reads/writes paths with fs and checks overwrite separately. These interfaces do not inherit MCP's root confinement merely because the engine/parser is shared (src/publication.rs:203-225; jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:52-78,106-111,137-153).

Document font family/native rendering to host font resources: installed_family_faces obtains the environment-derived user font folder and Word cloud-font root and scans known font directories. Cloud family names must be one normal path component; cached index entries can subsequently name font files directly. Persistent font-index loading/saving and font reads operate with ambient process authority (src/convert/font.rs:2225-2235,2258-2315,2633-2652,3090-3107,3154-3171,3182-3229). This boundary exists during native MCP rendering even when document paths are confined.

Local operator to executable update: self-update checks interactivity before network lookup, chooses one of five OS/architecture targets, obtains the project's GitHub release, requires explicit intent for downgrades and confirmation unless --yes, downloads the target with SHA256SUMS.txt verification, registers a regular-file extracted-binary hook and replaces the executable through self_update. Current source has no trusted signing key, so GitHub release-asset integrity remains part of the trust chain (src/update.rs:25-48,83-109,120-125,144-161,186-258,299-307).

Maintainer/tag authority to public release artifacts: v* pushes trigger builds; tag and Cargo version must match; binary jobs have contents:read; signing consumes a step-scoped private-key secret and checks archives against committed public keys when present. Release publication consumes a separate GitHub token. Actual repository protection, environment approvals and external registry/account configuration are not established by these workflow declarations (.github/workflows/release.yml:15-49,51-74,261-309,356-369).

Same-repository PR content to external Jules reviewer: the review workflow excludes fork/Dependabot PRs, performs no local checkout, delegates to a SHA-pinned external action, grants read content plus write PR/check permissions, and disables model approval. External action/Jules implementation is absent from inspected repository source, so its downstream session controls and secret handling remain unresolved (.github/workflows/jules-review.yml:17-50). The separate el-conejo workflow resolves a same-repository PR and checks out its exact head with persisted credentials disabled; it has its own author/dispatcher trust configuration and should not be collapsed into the first workflow's authority (.github/workflows/jules-el-conejo-review.yml:35-52,58-102).
attackerCapabilities: An attacker can author DOCX ZIP entries, relationship targets/types, XML structures and numeric attributes, embedded media/font bytes, legacy DOC character streams, Markdown and edit-plan values that a caller elects to process.

An MCP client can invoke registered tools over its existing stdio connection and request reads/writes within the granted root; overwrite=true explicitly permits replacement there. No remote listener or tenant model is established by the source (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:93-112,373-381).

Document control does not imply control of host environment variables, font directories/index, release assets, signing credentials, operator checkout or trusted MCP root. No new authority is inferred from already possessing those privileges.

A document supplier can control DOCX/ZIP/XML, embedded media/fonts, legacy DOC bytes and Markdown; it need not control host accounts or filesystem configuration. Denial-of-service and unintended host access boundaries are relevant for library callers even without a demonstrated public deployment.

An MCP client can invoke exposed document tools and choose relative paths, plans and overwrite within the operator-granted root. It does not thereby possess arbitrary host-path, network, release or registry authority. Directory contents visible to other MCP clients are not isolated per caller by this adapter (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:67-108,152-160).

A same-repository PR contributor can control reviewed source/diff and PR metadata and cause applicable CI/review workflows. Fork PR eligibility, GitHub workflow approval settings and self-hosted runner registration determine additional reachability; no assumption of repository-secret or runner-administrator control is needed or granted by this model.

A release-asset adversary would need authority over published release artifacts, beyond normal document input. Current checksum-only update trust means archive and matching checksum share the release service's authority; documentation acknowledges this limitation. Signing keys, registry credentials and repository-write tokens are separate capabilities (docs/SELF_UPDATE.md:59-80; src/update.rs:44-48).

External Jules actions receive explicitly configured credentials and repository context, but their internal authorization, remote session permissions and enforcement cannot be established from this repository's workflow declarations alone.

A document supplier can control input package structures, XML, media, embedded fonts and document content without already controlling the host filesystem, operator environment or release infrastructure: src/admission.rs:439; src/opc/archive.rs:42; src/xmllinq/parse.rs:134.

An MCP client can supply tool arguments, document paths, edit plans, output directories and explicit overwrite flags within the granted root; it does not thereby receive ambient CLI authority. The server is started on stdio, without a network listener: jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:75; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:152; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:373; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:381.

An actor able to replace release archives and their adjacent checksum file has meaningful influence over checksum-only updater installations. Such release-write authority is a separate prerequisite, not an ordinary document supplier capability: src/update.rs:44; src/update.rs:48; src/update.rs:245; docs/SELF_UPDATE.md:59.

The assigned validated findings additionally distinguish a less-trusted local writer of a plan/index staging parent from a document supplier. A deployment that exposes these through an HTTP/API service must provide authentication, authorization, quotas and isolation; those deployment controls are not established here (src/lib.rs:7-35; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:373-381; SECURITY.md:71-85).

Documentation says every MCP path/tool only touches files under --root and Python Document operations write no output files. Actual brokered document I/O uses OutputRoot, but rendering also reads ambient font directories and writes an ambient per-user font index. Therefore the broad root-only wording must not be interpreted as process-wide filesystem confinement (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:5-11,67-108,234-255; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/document.py:116-123; src/convert/font.rs:2633-2652,3090-3107,3182-3229).

Documentation says core operations use complete bytes with no temporary files. Native font-index persistence creates a sibling PID-suffixed .tmp file before renaming, and host publication deliberately creates staging. The byte-level document-processing statement and incidental host filesystem behavior must both remain visible; this architecture difference is not by itself a vulnerability (src/lib.rs:7-11; src/convert/font.rs:3221-3229; src/publication.rs:284-312).

Self-update documentation describes staged signing and correctly says empty embedded keys mean checksum-only operation. Actual RELEASE_KEYS=&[] and FIRST_SIGNED_RELEASE=None confirm that signing support is currently inactive in the updater. Whether GitHub's private signing secret exists is not inferable from source (docs/SELF_UPDATE.md:59-87; src/update.rs:44-48; .github/workflows/release.yml:261-275).

SECURITY.md describes rdocx-opc 0.2 and quick-xml 0.41 remediation. Current manifest instead uses oxml-opc 0.14.2, quick-xml 0.42 for checked admission and an explicitly aliased 0.41 for OPC error compatibility. Preserve this documentation/dependency-name discrepancy without inferring either an exploit or lack of patched behavior (SECURITY.md:89-97; Cargo.toml:102-117; src/opc/mod.rs:15-17,161-164).

Default and comparison admission budgets are materially different. WmlDocument admits under the roomier comparison budget, so a general statement that the default 64 MiB/256 MiB budget protects every public use would be inaccurate (src/admission.rs:25-27,63-98; src/wml_document.rs:50-57).

Output publication is atomic per file rather than transactional across an output set, and it reports partial commits. Python plan-level atomicity claims must not be generalized into rollback of successful filesystem commits (src/publication.rs:5-7,36-46,83-143,168-174; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:161-168,217).

Native font-cache locations depend on operator environment, cwd when overrides are relative, and platform. Actual runtime environment values, host ACLs, mounted directories, network filesystem behavior and externally imposed resource limits were not supplied and were not inspected (src/convert/font.rs:2633-2652,3098-3107,3213-3229).

External crate implementations, generated WASM correspondence to current Rust source, external GitHub/Jules services, account/branch protections and full privileged remediation workflow details were not completely inspected. These are explicit coverage limits, not findings.

Validation refined the architecture's expected resource controls: the pre-index EOCD count can differ from zip's selected record (src/admission.rs:399-407,444-455,590-602); tolerant XML admission and recursive DOM consume unquoted attributes differently (src/admission.rs:788-820; src/xmllinq/parse.rs:554-593,660-663). Thus archive entry count and admitted XML depth are intended controls with specific validated bypasses, not universal effective guarantees.

Logical and generated-output work requires separate limits: table spans, numbering ranges/labels, altChunk expansion, repeated relationship repair, legacy piece expansion, field-state scans, escaping and table padding contain independently validated resource issues. The ordinary byte/depth limits and recommended process isolation remain material mitigations with bounded coverage (src/convert/mod.rs:13601-13615,5518-5532,6015-6019,773-798; src/opc/mod.rs:99-125; src/legacy_doc.rs:511-527,575-598,1176-1227,1591-1621).

Privacy scrub's intended selected-category guarantee is narrower in implementation because it selects conventional part locations rather than all relationship-selected semantic parts. Alternate main paths are explicitly supported by admission; sanitization must account for those paths before sharing (src/scrub.rs:211-216,271-289,353-385; src/admission.rs:1754-1769; src/cli.rs:1553-1557).

The independent Node CLI plan recorder still follows predictable temporary paths despite native recording's secure publication. Conditional local shared-directory exposure is separate from normal ambient CLI path authority (jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:408-427; src/edit/record.rs:142-149,161-167).

findings.title: Rendering a small DOCX table can exhaust host memory
findings.summary: An untrusted DOCX author can set huge positive w:gridSpan, w:gridBefore or w:gridAfter counts in a small, shallow table. Rendering sums those counts into grid occupancy and directly sizes column, preference and merge vectors. Counts of 1000000000/1073741824 request about 4 GB/4 GiB for f32 columns; 4294967295 requests approximately 16 GiB before additional allocations, despite package admission.

severity.rationale: An untrusted document can deterministically drive huge allocations through a public parser boundary. This compromises availability of the rendering process; shared-service exposure is conditional and process memory limits constrain the blast radius.
severity.changeConditions: Enforce derived resource/output bounds before allocation; process-isolated callers limit blast radius.

confidence.rationale: Static source tracing establishes the unbounded usize parsing and direct vector allocation after admission, with no semantic span budget. No application code was executed.

rootCause.summary:
cell_span parses gridSpan as usize with only a minimum of one; row_grid_skip accepts arbitrary positive usize gridBefore/gridAfter and represents them as placeholder spans. table_block retains RawCell.colspan, sums row occupancy without checked bounds and uses it for vec!/resize; resolve_table_merges separately resizes its open vector to col+span. Neither per-span, aggregate-column nor derived-allocation budgets intervene.
The additional validated trace also identifies grid_skip_cell retaining the skipped count at src/convert/mod.rs:14379 and the column-preference allocation at :14263. A common repair must reject excessive effective columns before RawCell/grid-sized preference or merge work, including 32-bit WASM and checked cumulative arithmetic.
Table dimensions derived from attacker-controlled numeric XML are treated as allocation sizes without an upper grid width, checked cumulative accounting or fallible layout budget.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: Table column occupancy is derived directly from document-provided span and skip counts without a semantic ceiling or checked aggregate budget before Vec allocation.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): `cell_span` parses an attacker-controlled usize and only applies a minimum of one; row grid skips accept any positive usize. These counts become RawCell colspans. Table occupancy sums them and resizes or creates the f32 column vector. Merge resolution also resizes its per-column vector from the same unchecked span.
Assigned discovery-0017 additionally traces leading/trailing grid_skip_cell placeholders and stretch_stale_spans, which leaves oversized rows unchanged; gridSpan=2147483647 requests about 8 GiB for f32 columns.
Assigned discovery-0023 corroboration: The renderer parses attacker-authored table span attributes into `usize` and preserves them in raw cells, including synthetic cells for omitted columns. `table_block` sums the spans and allocates a column vector of that size; `resolve_table_merges` then allocates merge tracking to the same extent. XML byte, depth and attribute budgets do not restrict these numeric values. For example, a one-cell span of 1000000000 requests roughly 4 GB for columns alone despite requiring only ten digits in XML.

findings.remediation: Enforce practical per-span and total-column budgets for gridSpan, gridBefore and gridAfter before excessive RawCell, column, preference or merge allocation/work. Use checked occupancy sums and col+span arithmetic, apply the same budget to every derived table vector, and return a typed resource-limit refusal on excess. Propagate a caller-adjustable semantic column limit through all public rendering surfaces and charge later column/merge vectors to that same budget.

rootCause.summary:
cell_span parses gridSpan as usize with only a minimum of one; row_grid_skip accepts arbitrary positive usize gridBefore/gridAfter and represents them as placeholder spans. table_block retains RawCell.colspan, sums row occupancy without checked bounds and uses it for vec!/resize; resolve_table_merges separately resizes its open vector to col+span. Neither per-span, aggregate-column nor derived-allocation budgets intervene.
The additional validated trace also identifies grid_skip_cell retaining the skipped count at src/convert/mod.rs:14379 and the column-preference allocation at :14263. A common repair must reject excessive effective columns before RawCell/grid-sized preference or merge work, including 32-bit WASM and checked cumulative arithmetic.
Table dimensions derived from attacker-controlled numeric XML are treated as allocation sizes without an upper grid width, checked cumulative accounting or fallible layout budget.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: Table column occupancy is derived directly from document-provided span and skip counts without a semantic ceiling or checked aggregate budget before Vec allocation.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): `cell_span` parses an attacker-controlled usize and only applies a minimum of one; row grid skips accept any positive usize. These counts become RawCell colspans. Table occupancy sums them and resizes or creates the f32 column vector. Merge resolution also resizes its per-column vector from the same unchecked span.

previousFindings.remediation: Enforce practical per-span and total-column budgets for gridSpan, gridBefore and gridAfter before excessive RawCell, column, preference or merge allocation/work. Use checked occupancy sums and col+span arithmetic, apply the same budget to every derived table vector, and return a typed resource-limit refusal on excess.

validation.method: Preserved already-validated Standard evidence and attack paths; serial semantic remediation-subsumption reduction only, without code inspection, new validation, execution or attack-path analysis
validation.summary:
Both validated sources trace public with_layout admission through the span parsers to column-vector allocation and merge bookkeeping. A gridSpan of 1000000000 fits native and wasm32 usize and requests about 4 GB for f32 widths; the other source gives 1073741824, requiring 4 GiB before additional vectors. Tiny shallow XML satisfies byte/depth admission. No altChunk is required; malformed/negative fallback does not constrain a positive in-range value.
The newly assigned validated source gives gridSpan=4294967295: this positive value fits native and wasm32 usize and requests 4294967295 f32 entries (approximately 16 GiB). This is a source-derived allocation request, not a measured successful allocation. PNG MAX_PAGE_PIXELS is checked after layout, and PDF/render reports also invoke this table path.
Parent verified native table path independently of HTML import. gridSpan and gridBefore/After populate RawCell.colspan; table_block takes the maximum row sum and constructs/resizes columns before column_prefs/resolve_table_merges. Admission checks original syntax/bytes and has no table-dimension cap.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration (preserved Standard static assessment, not reducer verification): Confirmed render -> with_layout -> body table_block -> cell_span/row_grid_skip -> RawCell.colspan -> occupancy -> Vec allocation. Admission checks archive sizes, XML depth and tag widths, not these numeric layout counts.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): A one-cell table with gridSpan=4294967295 requests approximately 16GiB for the f32 column vector on a 64-bit host. Larger accepted usize values can trigger capacity overflow. `stretch_stale_spans` skips rows already occupying at least the declared grid and does not clamp them. `with_layout` admission bounds archive/XML bytes and structure, not these numeric counts.
Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed a one-cell table with gridSpan one billion requests about four billion bytes for an initial f32 vector alone. Row gridBefore/gridAfter reach the same occupancy mechanism through grid_skip_cell. This requires neither altChunk nor a large inflated XML part.

rootCause.summary:
cell_span parses gridSpan as usize with only a minimum of one; row_grid_skip accepts arbitrary positive usize gridBefore/gridAfter and represents them as placeholder spans. table_block retains RawCell.colspan, sums row occupancy without checked bounds and uses it for vec!/resize; resolve_table_merges separately resizes its open vector to col+span. Neither per-span, aggregate-column nor derived-allocation budgets intervene.
The additional validated trace also identifies grid_skip_cell retaining the skipped count at src/convert/mod.rs:14379 and the column-preference allocation at :14263. A common repair must reject excessive effective columns before RawCell/grid-sized preference or merge work, including 32-bit WASM and checked cumulative arithmetic.
Table dimensions derived from attacker-controlled numeric XML are treated as allocation sizes without an upper grid width, checked cumulative accounting or fallible layout budget.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: Table column occupancy is derived directly from document-provided span and skip counts without a semantic ceiling or checked aggregate budget before Vec allocation.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): `cell_span` parses an attacker-controlled usize and only applies a minimum of one; row grid skips accept any positive usize. These counts become RawCell colspans. Table occupancy sums them and resizes or creates the f32 column vector. Merge resolution also resizes its per-column vector from the same unchecked span.
Assigned discovery-0017 additionally traces leading/trailing grid_skip_cell placeholders and stretch_stale_spans, which leaves oversized rows unchanged; gridSpan=2147483647 requests about 8 GiB for f32 columns.

previousFindings.remediation: Enforce practical per-span and total-column budgets for gridSpan, gridBefore and gridAfter before excessive RawCell, column, preference or merge allocation/work. Use checked occupancy sums and col+span arithmetic, apply the same budget to every derived table vector, and return a typed resource-limit refusal on excess.

The security policy recommends process CPU/memory limits; these limit damage to a worker but do not reject the document.

validation.summary:
Both validated sources trace public with_layout admission through the span parsers to column-vector allocation and merge bookkeeping. A gridSpan of 1000000000 fits native and wasm32 usize and requests about 4 GB for f32 widths; the other source gives 1073741824, requiring 4 GiB before additional vectors. Tiny shallow XML satisfies byte/depth admission. No altChunk is required; malformed/negative fallback does not constrain a positive in-range value.
The newly assigned validated source gives gridSpan=4294967295: this positive value fits native and wasm32 usize and requests 4294967295 f32 entries (approximately 16 GiB). This is a source-derived allocation request, not a measured successful allocation. PNG MAX_PAGE_PIXELS is checked after layout, and PDF/render reports also invoke this table path.
Parent verified native table path independently of HTML import. gridSpan and gridBefore/After populate RawCell.colspan; table_block takes the maximum row sum and constructs/resizes columns before column_prefs/resolve_table_merges. Admission checks original syntax/bytes and has no table-dimension cap.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration (preserved Standard static assessment, not reducer verification): Confirmed render -> with_layout -> body table_block -> cell_span/row_grid_skip -> RawCell.colspan -> occupancy -> Vec allocation. Admission checks archive sizes, XML depth and tag widths, not these numeric layout counts.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): A one-cell table with gridSpan=4294967295 requests approximately 16GiB for the f32 column vector on a 64-bit host. Larger accepted usize values can trigger capacity overflow. `stretch_stale_spans` skips rows already occupying at least the declared grid and does not clamp them. `with_layout` admission bounds archive/XML bytes and structure, not these numeric counts.
Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed a one-cell table with gridSpan one billion requests about four billion bytes for an initial f32 vector alone. Row gridBefore/gridAfter reach the same occupancy mechanism through grid_skip_cell. This requires neither altChunk nor a large inflated XML part.
Assigned discovery-0017 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): The public rendering path admits and opens the document before table parsing. A positive 2147483647 fits usize on supported 32/64-bit targets. It is retained as `colspan`; the stale-span repair skips oversized rows. Occupancy reaches `vec![each; occupancy]` or `resize` without a maximum. Both row-skip fields independently feed the same sum via grid_skip_cell.
