rootCause.summary:
cell_span parses gridSpan as usize with only a minimum of one; row_grid_skip accepts arbitrary positive usize gridBefore/gridAfter and represents them as placeholder spans. table_block retains RawCell.colspan, sums row occupancy without checked bounds and uses it for vec!/resize; resolve_table_merges separately resizes its open vector to col+span. Neither per-span, aggregate-column nor derived-allocation budgets intervene.
The additional validated trace also identifies grid_skip_cell retaining the skipped count at src/convert/mod.rs:14379 and the column-preference allocation at :14263. A common repair must reject excessive effective columns before RawCell/grid-sized preference or merge work, including 32-bit WASM and checked cumulative arithmetic.
Table dimensions derived from attacker-controlled numeric XML are treated as allocation sizes without an upper grid width, checked cumulative accounting or fallible layout budget.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: Table column occupancy is derived directly from document-provided span and skip counts without a semantic ceiling or checked aggregate budget before Vec allocation.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): `cell_span` parses an attacker-controlled usize and only applies a minimum of one; row grid skips accept any positive usize. These counts become RawCell colspans. Table occupancy sums them and resizes or creates the f32 column vector. Merge resolution also resizes its per-column vector from the same unchecked span.
Assigned discovery-0017 additionally traces leading/trailing grid_skip_cell placeholders and stretch_stale_spans, which leaves oversized rows unchanged; gridSpan=2147483647 requests about 8 GiB for f32 columns.

previousFindings.remediation: Enforce practical per-span and total-column budgets for gridSpan, gridBefore and gridAfter before excessive RawCell, column, preference or merge allocation/work. Use checked occupancy sums and col+span arithmetic, apply the same budget to every derived table vector, and return a typed resource-limit refusal on excess. Propagate a caller-adjustable semantic column limit through all public rendering surfaces and charge later column/merge vectors to that same budget.

validation.summary:
Both validated sources trace public with_layout admission through the span parsers to column-vector allocation and merge bookkeeping. A gridSpan of 1000000000 fits native and wasm32 usize and requests about 4 GB for f32 widths; the other source gives 1073741824, requiring 4 GiB before additional vectors. Tiny shallow XML satisfies byte/depth admission. No altChunk is required; malformed/negative fallback does not constrain a positive in-range value.
The newly assigned validated source gives gridSpan=4294967295: this positive value fits native and wasm32 usize and requests 4294967295 f32 entries (approximately 16 GiB). This is a source-derived allocation request, not a measured successful allocation. PNG MAX_PAGE_PIXELS is checked after layout, and PDF/render reports also invoke this table path.
Parent verified native table path independently of HTML import. gridSpan and gridBefore/After populate RawCell.colspan; table_block takes the maximum row sum and constructs/resizes columns before column_prefs/resolve_table_merges. Admission checks original syntax/bytes and has no table-dimension cap.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration (preserved Standard static assessment, not reducer verification): Confirmed render -> with_layout -> body table_block -> cell_span/row_grid_skip -> RawCell.colspan -> occupancy -> Vec allocation. Admission checks archive sizes, XML depth and tag widths, not these numeric layout counts.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): A one-cell table with gridSpan=4294967295 requests approximately 16GiB for the f32 column vector on a 64-bit host. Larger accepted usize values can trigger capacity overflow. `stretch_stale_spans` skips rows already occupying at least the declared grid and does not clamp them. `with_layout` admission bounds archive/XML bytes and structure, not these numeric counts.
Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed a one-cell table with gridSpan one billion requests about four billion bytes for an initial f32 vector alone. Row gridBefore/gridAfter reach the same occupancy mechanism through grid_skip_cell. This requires neither altChunk nor a large inflated XML part.
Assigned discovery-0017 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): The public rendering path admits and opens the document before table parsing. A positive 2147483647 fits usize on supported 32/64-bit targets. It is retained as `colspan`; the stale-span repair skips oversized rows. Occupancy reaches `vec![each; occupancy]` or `resize` without a maximum. Both row-skip fields independently feed the same sum via grid_skip_cell.

findings.title: Processing renamed auxiliary XML bypasses XML depth limits
findings.summary: A DOCX author can put deeply nested auxiliary XML under a non-.xml/.rels suffix. Admission drains those bytes without XML policy, while rendering, revision listing, revision acceptance/rejection and comparison follow internal relationships and recursively build a DOM. Confirmed rendering parts include theme, styles, numbering, comments/commentsExtended, notes and headers/footers; get_revisions and comparison also parse renamed footnotes/endnotes. A small admitted package can terminate the native host or trap WASM. The assigned source additionally confirms eager relationship-selected fontTable parsing before font inspection, including renamed fontTable.bin. Comparison preprocessing also follows renamed styles and charts, alongside footnotes/endnotes. The assigned Standard source additionally identifies edit initialization's existing_comment_ids on relationship-selected comments before the later checked CommentFamily loader. Assigned discovery-0019 corroborates the same shared selector for styles, theme, numbering and fontTable under .bin names; its proof is limited to those four consumers, while earlier validated consumer paths remain retained.

severity.rationale: Untrusted document bytes cross a public parser boundary and can terminate the rendering process. External shared-service exposure is conditional; no code execution or file access is established.
severity.changeConditions: Effective per-document worker isolation limits impact; enforcing active XML policy on every consumed XML part removes this path.

confidence.rationale: Parent independently verified the extension-based admission gate, relationship-selected consumer and unchecked recursive parser. Runtime stack threshold was not tested.

rootCause.summary:
Admission chooses XML depth/tag checks by .xml/.rels filename and applies extension-independent checking only to the main part. Relationship-selected auxiliary consumers do not require XML suffixes or an enforcing content-type check: main_rel_part selects theme/styles/numbering, part_xml_by_rel_kind selects comments/notes, and header/footer relationship resolution loads bytes as XML. Their unchecked parse_xdocument calls reach recursive parse_element without a construction-depth bound. PartFs and Strict normalization add byte bounds but do not close this auxiliary XML-policy gap.
The assigned source further records the converter's comment-thread path: part_xml_by_rel_kind loads comments/commentsExtended, then unchecked parsing occurs at src/convert/mod.rs:7669-7675 and :7688-7689. This shares the missing extension-independent XML admission control; the separately checked src/comments.rs:467-468 CommentFamily::load is excluded.
Revision listing and comparison independently share the same extension-based policy gap: document_comparer::notes_part_names resolves internal footnotes/endnotes targets regardless of filename, and get_revisions (:6318-6328) and compare notes parse_part_root (:6676-6689) call unchecked parse_xdocument on those actual strings. A central active-limit XML-consumption boundary covering all these consumers subsumes every source; fixing renderer-only calls would leave revision/comparison paths reachable.
Admission infers XML coverage from a filename suffix, but consumers infer XML from relationship role. The consumer trusts admission for parts the gate never parsed.
The discovery-0009 rendering trace additionally specifies a normal Transitional package and disabled link styles, leaving selected styles.bin nesting unchanged through load_stylesheet; neither filename/content-type enforcement nor later auxiliary admission intervenes. Markdown Package::xml separately checks its XML and is excluded from this trace.
The revision_processor trace resolves headers, footers, endnotes, footnotes, comments and styles without extension constraints, then parses selected XML both during RevisionIds collection (:3785-3794) and process_part transforms (:3732-3748). The suffix admission gap precedes these independent operation paths.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): Admission trusts filename extensions to identify XML, but the consumer identifies auxiliary XML by relationship type and invokes recursive unchecked parsing.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): The policy gate classifies XML by archive filename, then checks only a renamed main document as a special case. Rendering instead selects header/footer parts by relationships and interprets their bytes as XML regardless of name. The downstream raw DOM parser relies on prior admission and recurses once per element, leaving renamed story parts outside the depth invariant. Comparison preprocessing repeats this boundary mismatch for relationship-selected styles, notes and charts.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): Admission gates XML depth/tag checks on `.xml`/`.rels` suffixes and only adds a main-part fallback. Comparator preprocessing instead trusts relationship types to identify notes, loads their text regardless of name and invokes unchecked recursive `parse_xdocument()`. Semantic XML consumers therefore receive unbounded nesting despite successful package admission.
The supplied discovery-0018 trace adds existing_comment_ids in edit initialization (src/edit.rs:2154-2158,5552-5563), reached before CommentFamily::load. The later checked loader therefore does not protect the earlier recursive parse. The assigned trace preserves main_rel_part's support for arbitrary internal target names and the main-part-only fallback check. It does not establish every mapped auxiliary consumer as vulnerable.
Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: The admission boundary decides XML policy by filename extension, while consumers decide what is XML by relationship semantics. Renamed auxiliary parts bypass admission and reach a recursive parser whose safety depends on that admission.

findings.remediation: Apply active InputLimits at a centralized checked XML access/parse boundary for every semantic XML consumer regardless of filename, or resolve/classify and admit XML through actual content-type/relationship use. Cover theme, styles, numbering, converter comments/commentsExtended, notes and headers/footers; include settings in regression coverage while retaining the source distinction that it was recommended rather than confirmed here. Preserve renamed-main checks, and enforce actual DOM construction depth or use iterative construction. Apply that same mandatory checked boundary to get_revisions and comparison notes parsing, including both footnotes and endnotes; propagate typed refusal under the active comparer InputLimits. Include pre_process_markup's relationship-selected notes at src/document_comparer.rs:4725-4750 and exposed Python get_revisions_json/WASM getRevisions; valid arbitrary part names remain supported. Include diagram and text-box relationship targets in regression coverage as proposed subcases, without promoting them to newly validated affected consumers. Cover revision_processor RevisionIds collection and process_part for all six selected auxiliary buckets (headers, footers, endnotes, footnotes, comments and styles), including public revision acceptance/rejection. Explicitly include the now-confirmed fontTable loader (src/convert/font_table.rs:66-78; src/convert/mod.rs:806) in the mandatory checked XML boundary; parsing must be bounded before any font root/entry inspection. Explicitly cover comparison defined_style_ids (src/document_comparer.rs:4684-4696), relationship-selected footnotes/endnotes (4724-4750) and chart preprocessing (4861-4878), all reached through admitted nonidentical comparison inputs (6555-6569,6607-6625). Apply the same mandatory XML boundary before edit initialization's existing_comment_ids scan, not only in the later checked CommentFamily loader; preserve the effective checks at inspect::parse_part_within and edit::load_stories.

validation.summary:
The validated styles-specific trace confirms a normal main document can select deeply nested styles.bin, without suffix/content-type enforcement or a later depth gate. The other validated trace confirms theme1.bin plus styles, numbering, comments, footnotes, endnotes and relationship-named headers/footers. Byte, inflation, CRC, ZIP/path checks and the nonstandard-main exception remain active; the malicious auxiliary payload alone bypasses XML policy. No external relationship or network fetch is needed.
The additional validated trace confirms converter commentsExtended as well as comments/notes/chrome consumers. A roughly 700 KiB part with 100000 nested elements fits byte limits; actual failing depth remains runtime-dependent and unmeasured. For a normal Transitional DOCX, normalization leaves the renamed part unchanged (src/strict_translation.rs:809-831); PartFs adds byte bounds rather than XML policy. This does not affect separately validated CommentFamily::load (src/comments.rs:467-468).
Verified public `get_revisions` input admission, internal relationship resolution without suffix restrictions, bounded ZIP loading that does not validate auxiliary XML, and the recursive parser sink. The comparison notes pipeline has the same missing check.
Parent verified suffix gate, main-only fallback, relationship resolver and get_revisions parser plus Python/WASM exposure. Deep notes.dat XML is parsed before note-definition processing. pre_process_markup independently follows and parses the same relationship-selected parts at4725-4750.
Assigned discovery-0008 corroboration: Independently verified Attacker DOCX styles relationship -> main_rel_part -> part_string(styles.bin) -> load_stylesheet -> Dom::parse_xdocument -> recursive parse_element.
Assigned discovery-0009 corroboration (preserved offline Standard validation): Confirmed that the main-only extension fallback in admission.rs:556-569 does not cover auxiliary parts; PartFs::read_package bounds inflated bytes but does not validate auxiliary XML. A Transitional DOCX with an internal styles relationship targeting a deeply nested .bin part reaches load_stylesheet's unchecked parser. No content-type extension requirement or later checked parse blocks this path.
Assigned discovery-0010 Standard corroboration (source validation, not reducer verification): Parent verified suffix classification/main exception, all six revision relationship buckets, RevisionIds/process_part parses and independent comparison notes parses. PartFs reads the selected bytes in memory without adding XML policy. A valid internal relationship/content type can name word/notes.dat; external relationships are excluded.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Parent traced admission.rs:533-569 classification/main exception, font_table.rs:66-78 loader, convert/mod.rs:806 and21310-21318 relationship selection, and parse.rs:660-663 recursive call. A normal main part plus fontTable target word/fontTable.bin containing100000 nested x tags stays within physical byte budgets and reaches recursion without depth policy.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Confirmed that a valid minimal main document and its shallow .rels can select a header.bin payload; default archive and byte budgets still allow many thousands of short nested tags. Strict-to-transitional conversion preserves non-XML parts (src/strict_translation.rs:809-831), and PartFs::open bounds bytes rather than applying XML depth (src/opc/mod.rs:282-350). The raw header parser therefore receives the unbounded nesting. Parent source review also confirms the same root gap in comparison preprocessing for footnotes/endnotes, styles and charts (src/document_comparer.rs:4685-4696,4724-4750,4861-4878), reached after admission and PartFs opening (6559-6568,6607-6625).
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Compared nonidentical packages are admitted, opened, then passed to pre_process_markup. An internal footnotes/endnotes relationship can name a safe `.bin` part with an XML content-type override; PartFs stores/returns it without adding an XML-depth check. The note parser runs before note-reference/shape handling, reaching recursive descent.
Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Parent traced admission, main-only exception, bounded OPC byte loading, renderer internal note/header targets and comparison's internal note preprocessing to unchecked recursive parse_element. Byte limits permit nesting far above the 256-depth limit. Strict translation likewise does not validate non-.xml auxiliary XML.

finding.title: Processing renamed XML parts bypasses depth admission and can abort the host
finding.summary: A document author can give an internal XML part a non-.xml/.rels filename and link it as a header/footer, style, footnote/endnote or chart. Admission skips its XML policy, but rendering or comparison recursively parses it and can exhaust the host stack.

severity.rationale: Attacker-supplied document bytes cross a public parser boundary and can terminate the rendering host with a small input; no remote service exposure is assumed. Process CPU/memory limits do not prevent a per-process stack-overflow abort.
severity.changeConditions: Isolated disposable conversion processes reduce the application-level impact; a shared conversion service would increase impact.

confidence.rationale: Static source trace establishes the filename-only gate, main-only fallback, relationship-selected bytes and unbounded recursive parser. No runtime exploit was executed.

codeEvidence.label: Caller-controlled package reaches layout
codeEvidence.explanation: `docx_to_pdf` and PNG/report paths share `with_layout`; the package is admitted and opened before header processing.

codeEvidence.label: Admission chooses policy by suffix
codeEvidence.explanation: The inflated part receives XML policy checks only when its name ends in .xml or .rels. An internal header.bin is counted in byte budgets but skipped by XML policy.

codeEvidence.label: Only the main document gets a second check
codeEvidence.explanation: The explicit fallback protects a renamed main part; it does not validate other relationship-selected XML consumers.

codeEvidence.label: Header reference selected from the document
codeEvidence.explanation: An attacker-controlled section reference selects a relationship ID passed to `load_chrome_part`.

codeEvidence.label: Arbitrary internal target read as XML
codeEvidence.explanation: The selected target bytes are decoded as UTF-8 and forwarded to `chrome_part_xml` without a policy check.

codeEvidence.label: Header/footer raw parser
codeEvidence.explanation: `chrome_part_xml` directly invokes the recursive infallible DOM parser on bytes skipped by the admission XML checks.

codeEvidence.label: Relationship controls target path
codeEvidence.explanation: The document relationship ID selects the package target without a filename-extension or content-type restriction.

codeEvidence.label: DOM nesting consumes call stack
codeEvidence.explanation: Each nested element recurses into `parse_element`; this path has no depth budget, so sufficiently deep XML exhausts the host stack.

codeEvidence.label: Comparison admits package bytes
codeEvidence.explanation: The modified input crosses admission before package processing.

codeEvidence.label: Comparison enters preprocessing
codeEvidence.explanation: Distinct admitted packages reach pre_process_markup, which loads relationship-selected auxiliary parts.

codeEvidence.label: Notes targets bypass suffix assumptions
codeEvidence.explanation: Internal footnotes/endnotes relationship targets are read and directly parsed regardless of filename.

codeEvidence.label: Styles target bypasses suffix assumptions
codeEvidence.explanation: The stylesheet selected by its relationship is passed to the raw parser without a per-part check.

codeEvidence.label: Charts bypass suffix assumptions
codeEvidence.explanation: Each internal chart target is selected by relationship type and its bytes enter raw DOM parsing irrespective of filename.

rootCause.summary: The policy gate classifies XML by archive filename, then checks only a renamed main document as a special case. Rendering instead selects header/footer parts by relationships and interprets their bytes as XML regardless of name. The downstream raw DOM parser relies on prior admission and recurses once per element, leaving renamed story parts outside the depth invariant. Comparison preprocessing repeats this boundary mismatch for relationship-selected styles, notes and charts.

finding.remediation: Enforce the active XML policy before parsing every XML relationship target irrespective of extension, or enumerate typed XML parts during admission. Make the raw DOM parser iterative or depth-bounded as defense in depth.

counterEvidence: Normal .xml/.rels parts receive XML checks, and renamed main documents are explicitly rechecked.
Raw parse_xdocument is documented as unchecked; the defect is its use behind a supposedly admitted package boundary, not the existence of that API.
External relationships are not needed; this exploit uses internal package bytes.
limitations: No application code or malicious input was executed; exact crash depth depends on platform and stack size.
validation.summary: Confirmed that a valid minimal main document and its shallow .rels can select a header.bin payload; default archive and byte budgets still allow many thousands of short nested tags. Strict-to-transitional conversion preserves non-XML parts (src/strict_translation.rs:809-831), and PartFs::open bounds bytes rather than applying XML depth (src/opc/mod.rs:282-350). The raw header parser therefore receives the unbounded nesting. Parent source review also confirms the same root gap in comparison preprocessing for footnotes/endnotes, styles and charts (src/document_comparer.rs:4685-4696,4724-4750,4861-4878), reached after admission and PartFs opening (6559-6568,6607-6625).

dataflow.summary: DOCX bytes -> with_layout -> admit -> suffix-based XML check skips header.bin -> internal relationship resolution -> chrome_part_xml -> recursive parse_element -> stack exhaustion

impact.rationale: Host-process availability; no confidentiality, arbitrary file write or code-execution claim.

likelihood.rationale: Default parser path accepts the internally linked renamed payload; deep nesting is directly attacker-controlled.

attackPath.summary: Supply a DOCX with an ordinary main part, a section headerReference, an internal header relationship targeting header.bin, and a deeply nested well-formed XML payload at that target; render via the public PDF/PNG APIs or their wrappers.

remediationTests: An internal header/footer target named .bin with nesting above max_xml_depth must return INVALID_XML before DOM construction.
Repeat with custom part names and raised/lowered InputLimits; ordinary shallow parts must remain supported.
Repeat renamed-part admission regressions for styles, footnotes, endnotes and chart relationships in comparison preprocessing.

originalCandidates.message: Confirmed candidate: admission scans XML policy only when archive entry lower.ends_with('.xml'|'.rels') (src/admission.rs:534-545), special-cases only main_part missing extension (558-569). An attacker can target word/header.bin and put deeply nested well-formed XML there, bypass max_xml_depth=256 and crash converter host via stack exhaustion. Investigating all entrypoint controls before final.

finding.summary: Admission selects XML policy by filename suffix, but the comparator resolves footnote/endnote XML by relationships regardless of suffix. A deeply nested notes part named `.bin` reaches the unchecked recursive DOM parser and can terminate the embedding process with stack exhaustion.

severity.rationale: A document producer can bypass an explicit parser depth control and deny availability during comparison; no code execution or disclosure is established.
severity.changeConditions: Process isolation reduces collateral impact; using checked XML APIs for every semantic XML consumer closes this path.

codeEvidence.explanation: An auxiliary part with another extension is counted as bytes but skips check_xml_depth and its tag policy; the subsequent fallback only checks the main document.

codeEvidence.label: Notes are located by relationship type
codeEvidence.explanation: The document supplier chooses an internal notes target such as word/notes.bin; no extension constraint is applied.

codeEvidence.label: Resolved notes use unchecked DOM parsing
codeEvidence.explanation: Both notes paths parse fetched text before validating semantic contents, without a checked XML gate carrying InputLimits.

codeEvidence.explanation: Unchecked parsing recursively handles nested elements without a depth counter, so a short but deeply nested XML payload can exhaust the process/instance stack.

rootCause.summary: Admission gates XML depth/tag checks on `.xml`/`.rels` suffixes and only adds a main-part fallback. Comparator preprocessing instead trusts relationship types to identify notes, loads their text regardless of name and invokes unchecked recursive `parse_xdocument()`. Semantic XML consumers therefore receive unbounded nesting despite successful package admission.

finding.remediation: Apply active XML limits at every semantic XML parse boundary, including relationship-resolved notes, or enumerate XML parts by content types and relationship consumers before parsing. Use checked DOM APIs in comparator preprocessing.

counterEvidence: `.xml`/`.rels` parts and the main document are depth/tag checked, and inspect has checked XML paths; those controls do not cover this relationship-resolved comparator path.
ZIP byte/entry/inflated limits still apply, but tens of thousands of nested tags fit comfortably within defaults.
The infallible raw DOM API is documented as unchecked; the report concerns its use after incomplete package admission, not the existence of that API.
limitations: No runtime stack-overflow reproduction; exact failing depth depends on host stack and target.

The note parser runs before note-reference/shape handling, reaching recursive descent.

rootCause.summary: Package admission recognizes XML by `.xml`/`.rels` suffix and separately checks only a nonstandard main-document name. OPC auxiliary relationships are allowed arbitrary internal target names. Conversion opens those selected parts as text and calls permissive parse_xdocument, whose nested-element branch recurses without a depth check. Renaming the target changes admission classification without changing its later XML interpretation.

finding.remediation: Identify all XML by supported relationship/content types during admission and validate every selected XML part under the active InputLimits immediately before DOM construction, regardless of filename. Prefer checked parser APIs at these boundaries.

counterEvidence: Conventional .xml/.rels parts are policy-checked.
A renamed main document is checked explicitly, so it is not the demonstrated bypass.
PartFs byte/inflation and ZIP consistency controls still apply.
SECURITY.md distinguishes infallible parser and recommends caller process limits; conversion itself advertises admission before parsing.
limitations: Crash depth depends on host stack/target; no dynamic reproduction.
Other auxiliary consumers were mapped but the retained proof names these four independently selected operations.
validation.summary: Verified styles, theme, numbering and font-table variants through the shared relationship selector, plus the original admission and DOM recursion. finding.title: Accepting or rejecting revisions can bypass XML depth limits
finding.summary: An attacker can name a revision-bearing auxiliary XML part with a non-XML suffix, such as `.bin`. Admission skips its XML policy, but revision processing follows the relationship and recursively parses it. Deep nesting can terminate the processor even though the high-level API admitted the package.

severity.rationale: An untrusted DOCX can exhaust the consumer stack through supported byte APIs despite default admission. Service-wide exposure remains conditional on downstream integration.

confidence.rationale: Parent verified the suffix gate, main-only exception, relationship-based selection and unconditional unchecked parse.

taxonomy.category: XML input policy bypass through inconsistent part classification

codeEvidence.label: XML policy selected by suffix for auxiliary parts
codeEvidence.explanation: Only .xml/.rels members receive XML checks; the additional suffix-independent check covers main_part alone.

codeEvidence.label: Revision byte APIs admit then process
codeEvidence.explanation: Both public byte facades admit the caller's package before accepting/rejecting revisions.

codeEvidence.label: Revision parts selected by relationship type
codeEvidence.explanation: Header/footer/notes/comments/styles relationships select arbitrary safe target names without requiring XML suffixes.

codeEvidence.label: Selected part reaches unchecked DOM
codeEvidence.explanation: Each relationship-selected part is parsed regardless of suffix without a consumer-side XML depth check.

codeEvidence.label: Resolution initializes ids for all selected parts
codeEvidence.explanation: Resolution unconditionally invokes RevisionIds::new before processing selected parts.

codeEvidence.label: Each child nests another stack frame
codeEvidence.explanation: Deep repeated elements recursively call parse_element without a depth counter until stack exhaustion.

rootCause.summary: `accept_revisions()` and `reject_revisions()` admit raw package bytes. Admission validates auxiliary XML by filename extension and only revisits the main document independently of its name. The revision processor instead selects headers/footers/notes/comments/styles by relationship type. `RevisionIds::new()` parses every selected target using the permissive DOM, so an XML target named .bin crosses into recursive parsing without the promised depth/tag check.

finding.remediation: Validate every part actually consumed as XML with the active limits independently of its filename. Add relationship/content-type-aware admission and enforce checked parsing at consumers so auxiliary names cannot bypass policy.

counterEvidence: Byte/inflation/ZIP consistency controls remain active.
Ordinary .xml auxiliary parts and any main part are checked.
Some other consumers, such as inspect/comments/audit, validate actual related XML before parsing.
limitations: No crafted document or application execution was performed; other auxiliary XML consumers were not exhaustively audited.
validation.summary: Parent confirmed ordinary bounded main/metadata parts can coexist with a safe .bin auxiliary target carrying deeply nested XML. PartFs retains its bytes without XML policy (src/opc/mod.rs:344-377); relationship selection ignores extension, and RevisionIds parses it before revisions are processed.

dataflow.summary: DOCX -> admission skips non-XML suffix -> PartFs retains target -> relationship-based revision selection -> RevisionIds::new -> recursive DOM parse.

reachability.summary: Both public accept_revisions/reject_revisions APIs expose the route with default admission enabled; no privileged limit overrides are needed.

attackPath.summary: Supply a DOCX with a normal main part and an internal header/footer/notes/comments/styles relationship to deeply nested XML stored as a .bin part; induce accept/reject revision processing.

remediationTests: Use non-.xml targets for each revision-bearing relationship and assert depth/tag violations are refused.
Cover custom main-part names, ordinary valid auxiliary targets, and preserved active limits.

originalCandidates.message: accept_revisions/reject_revisions admit input at document_comparer.rs:4961-4987, but admission validates XML by .xml/.rels extension with main-part special case (admission.rs:533-569). Related header/footer/notes/comments/styles .bin part retained raw by PartFs opc/mod.rs:348-377, then revision_bearing_parts selects relationship target by type without extension/content validation (revision_processor.rs:3689-3728). RevisionIds::new parse_xdocument:3785-3792 precedes process_part:3732-3740; deeply nested XML bypasses input depth/tag policy through high-level byte APIs. Static evidence only.

finding.title: Renamed auxiliary XML bypasses admission and reaches unbounded recursive parsing
finding.summary: Admission validates XML only for .xml/.rels names, plus a special case for the main document. Rendering and comparison later select auxiliary parts by relationship type/ID, regardless of extension, and pass them into the unchecked recursive DOM parser. An internal endnotes.bin, footnotes.bin or header.bin can therefore carry deeply nested XML beneath byte limits and terminate the native process through stack exhaustion.

severity.rationale: An untrusted document author can bypass the configured XML-depth boundary and terminate the processing host during ordinary compare/render operations. No remote deployment or confidentiality compromise is required or assumed.
severity.changeConditions: Bounded checked parsing at every consumed XML part removes the bypass; host process isolation limits availability blast radius.

confidence.rationale: Parent verified suffix-based admission, relationship-selected auxiliary reads, unchecked parser recursion, public renderer and comparer call paths, and the contrasting checked Markdown parser. No runtime exploit was executed.

rootCause.summary: Admission chooses XML depth/tag checks by .xml/.rels filename and applies extension-independent checking only to the main part. Relationship-selected auxiliary consumers do not require XML suffixes or an enforcing content-type check: main_rel_part selects theme/styles/numbering, part_xml_by_rel_kind selects comments/notes, and header/footer relationship resolution loads bytes as XML. Their unchecked parse_xdocument calls reach recursive parse_element without a construction-depth bound. rootCause.summary:
Admission chooses XML depth/tag checks by .xml/.rels filename and applies extension-independent checking only to the main part. Relationship-selected auxiliary consumers do not require XML suffixes or an enforcing content-type check: main_rel_part selects theme/styles/numbering, part_xml_by_rel_kind selects comments/notes, and header/footer relationship resolution loads bytes as XML. Their unchecked parse_xdocument calls reach recursive parse_element without a construction-depth bound. PartFs and Strict normalization add byte bounds but do not close this auxiliary XML-policy gap.
The assigned source further records the converter's comment-thread path: part_xml_by_rel_kind loads comments/commentsExtended, then unchecked parsing occurs at src/convert/mod.rs:7669-7675 and :7688-7689. This shares the missing extension-independent XML admission control; the separately checked src/comments.rs:467-468 CommentFamily::load is excluded.
Revision listing and comparison independently share the same extension-based policy gap: document_comparer::notes_part_names resolves internal footnotes/endnotes targets regardless of filename, and get_revisions (:6318-6328) and compare notes parse_part_root (:6676-6689) call unchecked parse_xdocument on those actual strings. A central active-limit XML-consumption boundary covering all these consumers subsumes every source; fixing renderer-only calls would leave revision/comparison paths reachable.
Admission infers XML coverage from a filename suffix, but consumers infer XML from relationship role. The consumer trusts admission for parts the gate never parsed.

Cover theme, styles, numbering, converter comments/commentsExtended, notes and headers/footers; include settings in regression coverage while retaining the source distinction that it was recommended rather than confirmed here. Preserve renamed-main checks, and enforce actual DOM construction depth or use iterative construction. Apply that same mandatory checked boundary to get_revisions and comparison notes parsing, including both footnotes and endnotes; propagate typed refusal under the active comparer InputLimits. Include pre_process_markup's relationship-selected notes at src/document_comparer.rs:4725-4750 and exposed Python get_revisions_json/WASM getRevisions; valid arbitrary part names remain supported.

validation.summary:
The validated styles-specific trace confirms a normal main document can select deeply nested styles.bin, without suffix/content-type enforcement or a later depth gate. The other validated trace confirms theme1.bin plus styles, numbering, comments, footnotes, endnotes and relationship-named headers/footers. Byte, inflation, CRC, ZIP/path checks and the nonstandard-main exception remain active; the malicious auxiliary payload alone bypasses XML policy. No external relationship or network fetch is needed.
The additional validated trace confirms converter commentsExtended as well as comments/notes/chrome consumers. A roughly 700 KiB part with 100000 nested elements fits byte limits; actual failing depth remains runtime-dependent and unmeasured. For a normal Transitional DOCX, normalization leaves the renamed part unchanged (src/strict_translation.rs:809-831); PartFs adds byte bounds rather than XML policy. This does not affect separately validated CommentFamily::load (src/comments.rs:467-468).
Verified public `get_revisions` input admission, internal relationship resolution without suffix restrictions, bounded ZIP loading that does not validate auxiliary XML, and the recursive parser sink. The comparison notes pipeline has the same missing check.
Parent verified suffix gate, main-only fallback, relationship resolver and get_revisions parser plus Python/WASM exposure. Deep notes.dat XML is parsed before note-definition processing. pre_process_markup independently follows and parses the same relationship-selected parts at4725-4750.

extensions.semanticReductionNotes:

The raw unchecked parser is documented trusted-only; the finding concerns its automatic invocation on incompletely admitted document content. dedup-0002 adds validated converter commentsExtended/thread parsing, the ~700 KiB/100000-nesting framing, normalization and fallback nuances, and the explicitly protected CommentFamily::load exclusion. dedup-0003 absorbs the same suffix-only auxiliary XML admission root issue and preserves the independent get_revisions and comparison notes entrypoints, notes_part_names resolution, both footnotes/endnotes, checked API exclusion and active-limit/refusal requirements. Existing malformed-attribute, DTD-literal and reference-template findings remain separate because correcting suffix classification alone does not fix them.
dedup-0004: Same suffix-based XML policy versus role-selected auxiliary consumer. The previous aggregate already covers get_revisions and compare notes as well as renderer consumers. Protected checked consumers and unusual main-part exception remain excluded.

Keep main-only admission and archive byte controls, internal-relationship prerequisite and untested stack threshold. rootCause.summary:
Admission chooses XML depth/tag checks by .xml/.rels filename and applies extension-independent checking only to the main part. Relationship-selected auxiliary consumers do not require XML suffixes or an enforcing content-type check: main_rel_part selects theme/styles/numbering, part_xml_by_rel_kind selects comments/notes, and header/footer relationship resolution loads bytes as XML. Their unchecked parse_xdocument calls reach recursive parse_element without a construction-depth bound. PartFs and Strict normalization add byte bounds but do not close this auxiliary XML-policy gap.
The assigned source further records the converter's comment-thread path: part_xml_by_rel_kind loads comments/commentsExtended, then unchecked parsing occurs at src/convert/mod.rs:7669-7675 and :7688-7689. This shares the missing extension-independent XML admission control; the separately checked src/comments.rs:467-468 CommentFamily::load is excluded.
Revision listing and comparison independently share the same extension-based policy gap: document_comparer::notes_part_names resolves internal footnotes/endnotes targets regardless of filename, and get_revisions (:6318-6328) and compare notes parse_part_root (:6676-6689) call unchecked parse_xdocument on those actual strings. A central active-limit XML-consumption boundary covering all these consumers subsumes every source; fixing renderer-only calls would leave revision/comparison paths reachable.
Admission infers XML coverage from a filename suffix, but consumers infer XML from relationship role. The consumer trusts admission for parts the gate never parsed.
The discovery-0009 rendering trace additionally specifies a normal Transitional package and disabled link styles, leaving selected styles.bin nesting unchanged through load_stylesheet; neither filename/content-type enforcement nor later auxiliary admission intervenes. Markdown Package::xml separately checks its XML and is excluded from this trace.
The revision_processor trace resolves headers, footers, endnotes, footnotes, comments and styles without extension constraints, then parses selected XML both during RevisionIds collection (:3785-3794) and process_part transforms (:3732-3748). The suffix admission gap precedes these independent operation paths.

previousFindings.remediation: Apply active InputLimits at a centralized checked XML access/parse boundary for every semantic XML consumer regardless of filename, or resolve/classify and admit XML through actual content-type/relationship use. Cover theme, styles, numbering, converter comments/commentsExtended, notes and headers/footers; include settings in regression coverage while retaining the source distinction that it was recommended rather than confirmed here. Preserve renamed-main checks, and enforce actual DOM construction depth or use iterative construction. Apply that same mandatory checked boundary to get_revisions and comparison notes parsing, including both footnotes and endnotes; propagate typed refusal under the active comparer InputLimits. Include pre_process_markup's relationship-selected notes at src/document_comparer.rs:4725-4750 and exposed Python get_revisions_json/WASM getRevisions; valid arbitrary part names remain supported. Include diagram and text-box relationship targets in regression coverage as proposed subcases, without promoting them to newly validated affected consumers. Cover revision_processor RevisionIds collection and process_part for all six selected auxiliary buckets (headers, footers, endnotes, footnotes, comments and styles), including public revision acceptance/rejection.

rootCause.summary:
Admission chooses XML depth/tag checks by .xml/.rels filename and applies extension-independent checking only to the main part. Relationship-selected auxiliary consumers do not require XML suffixes or an enforcing content-type check: main_rel_part selects theme/styles/numbering, part_xml_by_rel_kind selects comments/notes, and header/footer relationship resolution loads bytes as XML. Their unchecked parse_xdocument calls reach recursive parse_element without a construction-depth bound. PartFs and Strict normalization add byte bounds but do not close this auxiliary XML-policy gap.
The assigned source further records the converter's comment-thread path: part_xml_by_rel_kind loads comments/commentsExtended, then unchecked parsing occurs at src/convert/mod.rs:7669-7675 and :7688-7689. This shares the missing extension-independent XML admission control; the separately checked src/comments.rs:467-468 CommentFamily::load is excluded.
Revision listing and comparison independently share the same extension-based policy gap: document_comparer::notes_part_names resolves internal footnotes/endnotes targets regardless of filename, and get_revisions (:6318-6328) and compare notes parse_part_root (:6676-6689) call unchecked parse_xdocument on those actual strings. A central active-limit XML-consumption boundary covering all these consumers subsumes every source; fixing renderer-only calls would leave revision/comparison paths reachable.
Admission infers XML coverage from a filename suffix, but consumers infer XML from relationship role. The consumer trusts admission for parts the gate never parsed.
The discovery-0009 rendering trace additionally specifies a normal Transitional package and disabled link styles, leaving selected styles.bin nesting unchanged through load_stylesheet; neither filename/content-type enforcement nor later auxiliary admission intervenes. Markdown Package::xml separately checks its XML and is excluded from this trace.
The revision_processor trace resolves headers, footers, endnotes, footnotes, comments and styles without extension constraints, then parses selected XML both during RevisionIds collection (:3785-3794) and process_part transforms (:3732-3748). The suffix admission gap precedes these independent operation paths.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): Admission trusts filename extensions to identify XML, but the consumer identifies auxiliary XML by relationship type and invokes recursive unchecked parsing.

previousFindings.remediation: Apply active InputLimits at a centralized checked XML access/parse boundary for every semantic XML consumer regardless of filename, or resolve/classify and admit XML through actual content-type/relationship use. Cover theme, styles, numbering, converter comments/commentsExtended, notes and headers/footers; include settings in regression coverage while retaining the source distinction that it was recommended rather than confirmed here. Preserve renamed-main checks, and enforce actual DOM construction depth or use iterative construction. Apply that same mandatory checked boundary to get_revisions and comparison notes parsing, including both footnotes and endnotes; propagate typed refusal under the active comparer InputLimits. Include pre_process_markup's relationship-selected notes at src/document_comparer.rs:4725-4750 and exposed Python get_revisions_json/WASM getRevisions; valid arbitrary part names remain supported. Include diagram and text-box relationship targets in regression coverage as proposed subcases, without promoting them to newly validated affected consumers. Cover revision_processor RevisionIds collection and process_part for all six selected auxiliary buckets (headers, footers, endnotes, footnotes, comments and styles), including public revision acceptance/rejection. Explicitly include the now-confirmed fontTable loader (src/convert/font_table.rs:66-78; src/convert/mod.rs:806) in the mandatory checked XML boundary; parsing must be bounded before any font root/entry inspection.

rootCause.summary:
Admission chooses XML depth/tag checks by .xml/.rels filename and applies extension-independent checking only to the main part. Relationship-selected auxiliary consumers do not require XML suffixes or an enforcing content-type check: main_rel_part selects theme/styles/numbering, part_xml_by_rel_kind selects comments/notes, and header/footer relationship resolution loads bytes as XML. Their unchecked parse_xdocument calls reach recursive parse_element without a construction-depth bound. PartFs and Strict normalization add byte bounds but do not close this auxiliary XML-policy gap.
The assigned source further records the converter's comment-thread path: part_xml_by_rel_kind loads comments/commentsExtended, then unchecked parsing occurs at src/convert/mod.rs:7669-7675 and :7688-7689. This shares the missing extension-independent XML admission control; the separately checked src/comments.rs:467-468 CommentFamily::load is excluded.
Revision listing and comparison independently share the same extension-based policy gap: document_comparer::notes_part_names resolves internal footnotes/endnotes targets regardless of filename, and get_revisions (:6318-6328) and compare notes parse_part_root (:6676-6689) call unchecked parse_xdocument on those actual strings. A central active-limit XML-consumption boundary covering all these consumers subsumes every source; fixing renderer-only calls would leave revision/comparison paths reachable.
Admission infers XML coverage from a filename suffix, but consumers infer XML from relationship role. The consumer trusts admission for parts the gate never parsed.
The discovery-0009 rendering trace additionally specifies a normal Transitional package and disabled link styles, leaving selected styles.bin nesting unchanged through load_stylesheet; neither filename/content-type enforcement nor later auxiliary admission intervenes. Markdown Package::xml separately checks its XML and is excluded from this trace.
The revision_processor trace resolves headers, footers, endnotes, footnotes, comments and styles without extension constraints, then parses selected XML both during RevisionIds collection (:3785-3794) and process_part transforms (:3732-3748). The suffix admission gap precedes these independent operation paths.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): Admission trusts filename extensions to identify XML, but the consumer identifies auxiliary XML by relationship type and invokes recursive unchecked parsing.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): The policy gate classifies XML by archive filename, then checks only a renamed main document as a special case. Rendering instead selects header/footer parts by relationships and interprets their bytes as XML regardless of name. The downstream raw DOM parser relies on prior admission and recurses once per element, leaving renamed story parts outside the depth invariant. Comparison preprocessing repeats this boundary mismatch for relationship-selected styles, notes and charts.

previousFindings.remediation: Apply active InputLimits at a centralized checked XML access/parse boundary for every semantic XML consumer regardless of filename, or resolve/classify and admit XML through actual content-type/relationship use. Cover theme, styles, numbering, converter comments/commentsExtended, notes and headers/footers; include settings in regression coverage while retaining the source distinction that it was recommended rather than confirmed here. Preserve renamed-main checks, and enforce actual DOM construction depth or use iterative construction. Apply that same mandatory checked boundary to get_revisions and comparison notes parsing, including both footnotes and endnotes; propagate typed refusal under the active comparer InputLimits. Include pre_process_markup's relationship-selected notes at src/document_comparer.rs:4725-4750 and exposed Python get_revisions_json/WASM getRevisions; valid arbitrary part names remain supported. Include diagram and text-box relationship targets in regression coverage as proposed subcases, without promoting them to newly validated affected consumers. Cover revision_processor RevisionIds collection and process_part for all six selected auxiliary buckets (headers, footers, endnotes, footnotes, comments and styles), including public revision acceptance/rejection. Explicitly include the now-confirmed fontTable loader (src/convert/font_table.rs:66-78; src/convert/mod.rs:806) in the mandatory checked XML boundary; parsing must be bounded before any font root/entry inspection. Explicitly cover comparison defined_style_ids (src/document_comparer.rs:4684-4696), relationship-selected footnotes/endnotes (4724-4750) and chart preprocessing (4861-4878), all reached through admitted nonidentical comparison inputs (6555-6569,6607-6625).

validation.summary:
The validated styles-specific trace confirms a normal main document can select deeply nested styles.bin, without suffix/content-type enforcement or a later depth gate. The other validated trace confirms theme1.bin plus styles, numbering, comments, footnotes, endnotes and relationship-named headers/footers. Byte, inflation, CRC, ZIP/path checks and the nonstandard-main exception remain active; the malicious auxiliary payload alone bypasses XML policy. No external relationship or network fetch is needed.
The additional validated trace confirms converter commentsExtended as well as comments/notes/chrome consumers. A roughly 700 KiB part with 100000 nested elements fits byte limits; actual failing depth remains runtime-dependent and unmeasured. For a normal Transitional DOCX, normalization leaves the renamed part unchanged (src/strict_translation.rs:809-831); PartFs adds byte bounds rather than XML policy. This does not affect separately validated CommentFamily::load (src/comments.rs:467-468).
Verified public `get_revisions` input admission, internal relationship resolution without suffix restrictions, bounded ZIP loading that does not validate auxiliary XML, and the recursive parser sink. The comparison notes pipeline has the same missing check.
Parent verified suffix gate, main-only fallback, relationship resolver and get_revisions parser plus Python/WASM exposure. Deep notes.dat XML is parsed before note-definition processing. pre_process_markup independently follows and parses the same relationship-selected parts at4725-4750.
Assigned discovery-0008 corroboration: Independently verified Attacker DOCX styles relationship -> main_rel_part -> part_string(styles.bin) -> load_stylesheet -> Dom::parse_xdocument -> recursive parse_element.
Assigned discovery-0009 corroboration (preserved offline Standard validation): Confirmed that the main-only extension fallback in admission.rs:556-569 does not cover auxiliary parts; PartFs::read_package bounds inflated bytes but does not validate auxiliary XML. A Transitional DOCX with an internal styles relationship targeting a deeply nested .bin part reaches load_stylesheet's unchecked parser. No content-type extension requirement or later checked parse blocks this path.
Assigned discovery-0010 Standard corroboration (source validation, not reducer verification): Parent verified suffix classification/main exception, all six revision relationship buckets, RevisionIds/process_part parses and independent comparison notes parses. PartFs reads the selected bytes in memory without adding XML policy. A valid internal relationship/content type can name word/notes.dat; external relationships are excluded.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Parent traced admission.rs:533-569 classification/main exception, font_table.rs:66-78 loader, convert/mod.rs:806 and21310-21318 relationship selection, and parse.rs:660-663 recursive call. A normal main part plus fontTable target word/fontTable.bin containing100000 nested x tags stays within physical byte budgets and reaches recursion without depth policy.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Confirmed that a valid minimal main document and its shallow .rels can select a header.bin payload; default archive and byte budgets still allow many thousands of short nested tags. Strict-to-transitional conversion preserves non-XML parts (src/strict_translation.rs:809-831), and PartFs::open bounds bytes rather than applying XML depth (src/opc/mod.rs:282-350). The raw header parser therefore receives the unbounded nesting. Parent source review also confirms the same root gap in comparison preprocessing for footnotes/endnotes, styles and charts (src/document_comparer.rs:4685-4696,4724-4750,4861-4878), reached after admission and PartFs opening (6559-6568,6607-6625).

previousFindings.title: Processing renamed auxiliary XML bypasses XML depth limits
previousFindings.summary: A DOCX author can put deeply nested auxiliary XML under a non-.xml/.rels suffix. Admission drains those bytes without XML policy, while rendering, revision listing, revision acceptance/rejection and comparison follow internal relationships and recursively build a DOM. Confirmed rendering parts include theme, styles, numbering, comments/commentsExtended, notes and headers/footers; get_revisions and comparison also parse renamed footnotes/endnotes. A small admitted package can terminate the native host or trap WASM. The assigned source additionally confirms eager relationship-selected fontTable parsing before font inspection, including renamed fontTable.bin. Comparison preprocessing also follows renamed styles and charts, alongside footnotes/endnotes.

severity.rationale: Untrusted document bytes cross a public parser boundary and can terminate the rendering process. External shared-service exposure is conditional; no code execution or file access is established.
severity.changeConditions: Effective per-document worker isolation limits impact; enforcing active XML policy on every consumed XML part removes this path.

codeEvidence.label: Notes are located by relationship type
codeEvidence.explanation: The document supplier chooses an internal notes target such as word/notes.bin; no extension constraint is applied.

codeEvidence.label: Resolved notes use unchecked DOM parsing
codeEvidence.explanation: Both notes paths parse fetched text before validating semantic contents, without a checked XML gate carrying InputLimits.

codeEvidence.label: DOM descent consumes one stack frame per element
codeEvidence.explanation: Unchecked parsing recursively handles nested elements without a depth counter, so a short but deeply nested XML payload can exhaust the process/instance stack.

rootCause.summary:
Admission chooses XML depth/tag checks by .xml/.rels filename and applies extension-independent checking only to the main part. Relationship-selected auxiliary consumers do not require XML suffixes or an enforcing content-type check: main_rel_part selects theme/styles/numbering, part_xml_by_rel_kind selects comments/notes, and header/footer relationship resolution loads bytes as XML. Their unchecked parse_xdocument calls reach recursive parse_element without a construction-depth bound. PartFs and Strict normalization add byte bounds but do not close this auxiliary XML-policy gap.
The assigned source further records the converter's comment-thread path: part_xml_by_rel_kind loads comments/commentsExtended, then unchecked parsing occurs at src/convert/mod.rs:7669-7675 and :7688-7689. This shares the missing extension-independent XML admission control; the separately checked src/comments.rs:467-468 CommentFamily::load is excluded.
Revision listing and comparison independently share the same extension-based policy gap: document_comparer::notes_part_names resolves internal footnotes/endnotes targets regardless of filename, and get_revisions (:6318-6328) and compare notes parse_part_root (:6676-6689) call unchecked parse_xdocument on those actual strings. A central active-limit XML-consumption boundary covering all these consumers subsumes every source; fixing renderer-only calls would leave revision/comparison paths reachable.
Admission infers XML coverage from a filename suffix, but consumers infer XML from relationship role. The consumer trusts admission for parts the gate never parsed.
The discovery-0009 rendering trace additionally specifies a normal Transitional package and disabled link styles, leaving selected styles.bin nesting unchanged through load_stylesheet; neither filename/content-type enforcement nor later auxiliary admission intervenes. Markdown Package::xml separately checks its XML and is excluded from this trace.
The revision_processor trace resolves headers, footers, endnotes, footnotes, comments and styles without extension constraints, then parses selected XML both during RevisionIds collection (:3785-3794) and process_part transforms (:3732-3748). The suffix admission gap precedes these independent operation paths.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): Admission trusts filename extensions to identify XML, but the consumer identifies auxiliary XML by relationship type and invokes recursive unchecked parsing.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): The policy gate classifies XML by archive filename, then checks only a renamed main document as a special case. Rendering instead selects header/footer parts by relationships and interprets their bytes as XML regardless of name. The downstream raw DOM parser relies on prior admission and recurses once per element, leaving renamed story parts outside the depth invariant. Comparison preprocessing repeats this boundary mismatch for relationship-selected styles, notes and charts.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): Admission gates XML depth/tag checks on `.xml`/`.rels` suffixes and only adds a main-part fallback. Comparator preprocessing instead trusts relationship types to identify notes, loads their text regardless of name and invokes unchecked recursive `parse_xdocument()`. Semantic XML consumers therefore receive unbounded nesting despite successful package admission.

previousFindings.remediation: Apply active InputLimits at a centralized checked XML access/parse boundary for every semantic XML consumer regardless of filename, or resolve/classify and admit XML through actual content-type/relationship use. Cover theme, styles, numbering, converter comments/commentsExtended, notes and headers/footers; include settings in regression coverage while retaining the source distinction that it was recommended rather than confirmed here. Preserve renamed-main checks, and enforce actual DOM construction depth or use iterative construction. Apply that same mandatory checked boundary to get_revisions and comparison notes parsing, including both footnotes and endnotes; propagate typed refusal under the active comparer InputLimits. Include pre_process_markup's relationship-selected notes at src/document_comparer.rs:4725-4750 and exposed Python get_revisions_json/WASM getRevisions; valid arbitrary part names remain supported. Include diagram and text-box relationship targets in regression coverage as proposed subcases, without promoting them to newly validated affected consumers. Cover revision_processor RevisionIds collection and process_part for all six selected auxiliary buckets (headers, footers, endnotes, footnotes, comments and styles), including public revision acceptance/rejection. Explicitly include the now-confirmed fontTable loader (src/convert/font_table.rs:66-78; src/convert/mod.rs:806) in the mandatory checked XML boundary; parsing must be bounded before any font root/entry inspection. Explicitly cover comparison defined_style_ids (src/document_comparer.rs:4684-4696), relationship-selected footnotes/endnotes (4724-4750) and chart preprocessing (4861-4878), all reached through admitted nonidentical comparison inputs (6555-6569,6607-6625).

validation.summary:
The validated styles-specific trace confirms a normal main document can select deeply nested styles.bin, without suffix/content-type enforcement or a later depth gate. The other validated trace confirms theme1.bin plus styles, numbering, comments, footnotes, endnotes and relationship-named headers/footers. Byte, inflation, CRC, ZIP/path checks and the nonstandard-main exception remain active; the malicious auxiliary payload alone bypasses XML policy. No external relationship or network fetch is needed.
The additional validated trace confirms converter commentsExtended as well as comments/notes/chrome consumers. A roughly 700 KiB part with 100000 nested elements fits byte limits; actual failing depth remains runtime-dependent and unmeasured. For a normal Transitional DOCX, normalization leaves the renamed part unchanged (src/strict_translation.rs:809-831); PartFs adds byte bounds rather than XML policy. This does not affect separately validated CommentFamily::load (src/comments.rs:467-468).
Verified public `get_revisions` input admission, internal relationship resolution without suffix restrictions, bounded ZIP loading that does not validate auxiliary XML, and the recursive parser sink. The comparison notes pipeline has the same missing check.
Parent verified suffix gate, main-only fallback, relationship resolver and get_revisions parser plus Python/WASM exposure. Deep notes.dat XML is parsed before note-definition processing. pre_process_markup independently follows and parses the same relationship-selected parts at4725-4750.
Assigned discovery-0008 corroboration: Independently verified Attacker DOCX styles relationship -> main_rel_part -> part_string(styles.bin) -> load_stylesheet -> Dom::parse_xdocument -> recursive parse_element.
Assigned discovery-0009 corroboration (preserved offline Standard validation): Confirmed that the main-only extension fallback in admission.rs:556-569 does not cover auxiliary parts; PartFs::read_package bounds inflated bytes but does not validate auxiliary XML. A Transitional DOCX with an internal styles relationship targeting a deeply nested .bin part reaches load_stylesheet's unchecked parser. No content-type extension requirement or later checked parse blocks this path.
Assigned discovery-0010 Standard corroboration (source validation, not reducer verification): Parent verified suffix classification/main exception, all six revision relationship buckets, RevisionIds/process_part parses and independent comparison notes parses. PartFs reads the selected bytes in memory without adding XML policy. A valid internal relationship/content type can name word/notes.dat; external relationships are excluded.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Parent traced admission.rs:533-569 classification/main exception, font_table.rs:66-78 loader, convert/mod.rs:806 and21310-21318 relationship selection, and parse.rs:660-663 recursive call. A normal main part plus fontTable target word/fontTable.bin containing100000 nested x tags stays within physical byte budgets and reaches recursion without depth policy.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Confirmed that a valid minimal main document and its shallow .rels can select a header.bin payload; default archive and byte budgets still allow many thousands of short nested tags. Strict-to-transitional conversion preserves non-XML parts (src/strict_translation.rs:809-831), and PartFs::open bounds bytes rather than applying XML depth (src/opc/mod.rs:282-350). The raw header parser therefore receives the unbounded nesting. Parent source review also confirms the same root gap in comparison preprocessing for footnotes/endnotes, styles and charts (src/document_comparer.rs:4685-4696,4724-4750,4861-4878), reached after admission and PartFs opening (6559-6568,6607-6625).
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Compared nonidentical packages are admitted, opened, then passed to pre_process_markup. An internal footnotes/endnotes relationship can name a safe `.bin` part with an XML content-type override; PartFs stores/returns it without adding an XML-depth check. The note parser runs before note-reference/shape handling, reaching recursive descent.

previousFindings.title: Processing renamed auxiliary XML bypasses XML depth limits
previousFindings.summary: A DOCX author can put deeply nested auxiliary XML under a non-.xml/.rels suffix. Admission drains those bytes without XML policy, while rendering, revision listing, revision acceptance/rejection and comparison follow internal relationships and recursively build a DOM. Confirmed rendering parts include theme, styles, numbering, comments/commentsExtended, notes and headers/footers; get_revisions and comparison also parse renamed footnotes/endnotes. A small admitted package can terminate the native host or trap WASM. The assigned source additionally confirms eager relationship-selected fontTable parsing before font inspection, including renamed fontTable.bin. Comparison preprocessing also follows renamed styles and charts, alongside footnotes/endnotes. The assigned Standard source additionally identifies edit initialization's existing_comment_ids on relationship-selected comments before the later checked CommentFamily loader.

severity.rationale: Untrusted document bytes cross a public parser boundary and can terminate the rendering process. External shared-service exposure is conditional; no code execution or file access is established.
severity.changeConditions: Effective per-document worker isolation limits impact; enforcing active XML policy on every consumed XML part removes this path.

confidence.rationale: Parent independently verified the extension-based admission gate, relationship-selected consumer and unchecked recursive parser. Runtime stack threshold was not tested.

rootCause.summary:
Admission chooses XML depth/tag checks by .xml/.rels filename and applies extension-independent checking only to the main part. Relationship-selected auxiliary consumers do not require XML suffixes or an enforcing content-type check: main_rel_part selects theme/styles/numbering, part_xml_by_rel_kind selects comments/notes, and header/footer relationship resolution loads bytes as XML. Their unchecked parse_xdocument calls reach recursive parse_element without a construction-depth bound. PartFs and Strict normalization add byte bounds but do not close this auxiliary XML-policy gap.
The assigned source further records the converter's comment-thread path: part_xml_by_rel_kind loads comments/commentsExtended, then unchecked parsing occurs at src/convert/mod.rs:7669-7675 and :7688-7689. This shares the missing extension-independent XML admission control; the separately checked src/comments.rs:467-468 CommentFamily::load is excluded.
Revision listing and comparison independently share the same extension-based policy gap: document_comparer::notes_part_names resolves internal footnotes/endnotes targets regardless of filename, and get_revisions (:6318-6328) and compare notes parse_part_root (:6676-6689) call unchecked parse_xdocument on those actual strings. A central active-limit XML-consumption boundary covering all these consumers subsumes every source; fixing renderer-only calls would leave revision/comparison paths reachable.
Admission infers XML coverage from a filename suffix, but consumers infer XML from relationship role. The consumer trusts admission for parts the gate never parsed.
The discovery-0009 rendering trace additionally specifies a normal Transitional package and disabled link styles, leaving selected styles.bin nesting unchanged through load_stylesheet; neither filename/content-type enforcement nor later auxiliary admission intervenes. Markdown Package::xml separately checks its XML and is excluded from this trace.
The revision_processor trace resolves headers, footers, endnotes, footnotes, comments and styles without extension constraints, then parses selected XML both during RevisionIds collection (:3785-3794) and process_part transforms (:3732-3748). The suffix admission gap precedes these independent operation paths.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): Admission trusts filename extensions to identify XML, but the consumer identifies auxiliary XML by relationship type and invokes recursive unchecked parsing.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): The policy gate classifies XML by archive filename, then checks only a renamed main document as a special case. Rendering instead selects header/footer parts by relationships and interprets their bytes as XML regardless of name. The downstream raw DOM parser relies on prior admission and recurses once per element, leaving renamed story parts outside the depth invariant. Comparison preprocessing repeats this boundary mismatch for relationship-selected styles, notes and charts.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): Admission gates XML depth/tag checks on `.xml`/`.rels` suffixes and only adds a main-part fallback. Comparator preprocessing instead trusts relationship types to identify notes, loads their text regardless of name and invokes unchecked recursive `parse_xdocument()`. Semantic XML consumers therefore receive unbounded nesting despite successful package admission.
The supplied discovery-0018 trace adds existing_comment_ids in edit initialization (src/edit.rs:2154-2158,5552-5563), reached before CommentFamily::load. The later checked loader therefore does not protect the earlier recursive parse.

previousFindings.remediation: Apply active InputLimits at a centralized checked XML access/parse boundary for every semantic XML consumer regardless of filename, or resolve/classify and admit XML through actual content-type/relationship use. Cover theme, styles, numbering, converter comments/commentsExtended, notes and headers/footers; include settings in regression coverage while retaining the source distinction that it was recommended rather than confirmed here. Preserve renamed-main checks, and enforce actual DOM construction depth or use iterative construction. Apply that same mandatory checked boundary to get_revisions and comparison notes parsing, including both footnotes and endnotes; propagate typed refusal under the active comparer InputLimits. Include pre_process_markup's relationship-selected notes at src/document_comparer.rs:4725-4750 and exposed Python get_revisions_json/WASM getRevisions; valid arbitrary part names remain supported. Include diagram and text-box relationship targets in regression coverage as proposed subcases, without promoting them to newly validated affected consumers. Cover revision_processor RevisionIds collection and process_part for all six selected auxiliary buckets (headers, footers, endnotes, footnotes, comments and styles), including public revision acceptance/rejection. Explicitly include the now-confirmed fontTable loader (src/convert/font_table.rs:66-78; src/convert/mod.rs:806) in the mandatory checked XML boundary; parsing must be bounded before any font root/entry inspection. Explicitly cover comparison defined_style_ids (src/document_comparer.rs:4684-4696), relationship-selected footnotes/endnotes (4724-4750) and chart preprocessing (4861-4878), all reached through admitted nonidentical comparison inputs (6555-6569,6607-6625). Apply the same mandatory XML boundary before edit initialization's existing_comment_ids scan, not only in the later checked CommentFamily loader; preserve the effective checks at inspect::parse_part_within and edit::load_stories.
