validation.summary:
The validated styles-specific trace confirms a normal main document can select deeply nested styles.bin, without suffix/content-type enforcement or a later depth gate. The other validated trace confirms theme1.bin plus styles, numbering, comments, footnotes, endnotes and relationship-named headers/footers. Byte, inflation, CRC, ZIP/path checks and the nonstandard-main exception remain active; the malicious auxiliary payload alone bypasses XML policy. No external relationship or network fetch is needed.
The additional validated trace confirms converter commentsExtended as well as comments/notes/chrome consumers. A roughly 700 KiB part with 100000 nested elements fits byte limits; actual failing depth remains runtime-dependent and unmeasured. For a normal Transitional DOCX, normalization leaves the renamed part unchanged (src/strict_translation.rs:809-831); PartFs adds byte bounds rather than XML policy. This does not affect separately validated CommentFamily::load (src/comments.rs:467-468).
Verified public `get_revisions` input admission, internal relationship resolution without suffix restrictions, bounded ZIP loading that does not validate auxiliary XML, and the recursive parser sink. The comparison notes pipeline has the same missing check.
Parent verified suffix gate, main-only fallback, relationship resolver and get_revisions parser plus Python/WASM exposure. Deep notes.dat XML is parsed before note-definition processing. pre_process_markup independently follows and parses the same relationship-selected parts at4725-4750.
Assigned discovery-0008 corroboration: Independently verified Attacker DOCX styles relationship -> main_rel_part -> part_string(styles.bin) -> load_stylesheet -> Dom::parse_xdocument -> recursive parse_element.
Assigned discovery-0009 corroboration (preserved offline Standard validation): Confirmed that the main-only extension fallback in admission.rs:556-569 does not cover auxiliary parts; PartFs::read_package bounds inflated bytes but does not validate auxiliary XML. A Transitional DOCX with an internal styles relationship targeting a deeply nested .bin part reaches load_stylesheet's unchecked parser. No content-type extension requirement or later checked parse blocks this path.
Assigned discovery-0010 Standard corroboration (source validation, not reducer verification): Parent verified suffix classification/main exception, all six revision relationship buckets, RevisionIds/process_part parses and independent comparison notes parses. PartFs reads the selected bytes in memory without adding XML policy. A valid internal relationship/content type can name word/notes.dat; external relationships are excluded.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Parent traced admission.rs:533-569 classification/main exception, font_table.rs:66-78 loader, convert/mod.rs:806 and21310-21318 relationship selection, and parse.rs:660-663 recursive call. A normal main part plus fontTable target word/fontTable.bin containing100000 nested x tags stays within physical byte budgets and reaches recursion without depth policy.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Confirmed that a valid minimal main document and its shallow .rels can select a header.bin payload; default archive and byte budgets still allow many thousands of short nested tags. Strict-to-transitional conversion preserves non-XML parts (src/strict_translation.rs:809-831), and PartFs::open bounds bytes rather than applying XML depth (src/opc/mod.rs:282-350). The raw header parser therefore receives the unbounded nesting. Parent source review also confirms the same root gap in comparison preprocessing for footnotes/endnotes, styles and charts (src/document_comparer.rs:4685-4696,4724-4750,4861-4878), reached after admission and PartFs opening (6559-6568,6607-6625).
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Compared nonidentical packages are admitted, opened, then passed to pre_process_markup. An internal footnotes/endnotes relationship can name a safe `.bin` part with an XML content-type override; PartFs stores/returns it without adding an XML-depth check. The note parser runs before note-reference/shape handling, reaching recursive descent.

DOCX auxiliary bytes and internal relationship target -> suffix-only admission drains/counts bytes -> normalized bounded PartFs -> main_rel_part(theme/styles/numbering), part_xml_by_rel_kind(comments/notes), or header/footer target resolution -> unchecked auxiliary parse_xdocument -> unbounded recursive parse_element.

previousFindings.title: Processing renamed auxiliary XML bypasses XML depth limits
previousFindings.summary: A DOCX author can put deeply nested auxiliary XML under a non-.xml/.rels suffix. Admission drains those bytes without XML policy, while rendering, revision listing, revision acceptance/rejection and comparison follow internal relationships and recursively build a DOM. Confirmed rendering parts include theme, styles, numbering, comments/commentsExtended, notes and headers/footers; get_revisions and comparison also parse renamed footnotes/endnotes. A small admitted package can terminate the native host or trap WASM. The assigned source additionally confirms eager relationship-selected fontTable parsing before font inspection, including renamed fontTable.bin. Comparison preprocessing also follows renamed styles and charts, alongside footnotes/endnotes. The assigned Standard source additionally identifies edit initialization's existing_comment_ids on relationship-selected comments before the later checked CommentFamily loader. Assigned discovery-0019 corroborates the same shared selector for styles, theme, numbering and fontTable under .bin names; its proof is limited to those four consumers, while earlier validated consumer paths remain retained.

severity.changeConditions: Effective per-document worker isolation limits impact; enforcing active XML policy on every consumed XML part removes this path.

rootCause.summary:
Admission chooses XML depth/tag checks by .xml/.rels filename and applies extension-independent checking only to the main part. Relationship-selected auxiliary consumers do not require XML suffixes or an enforcing content-type check: main_rel_part selects theme/styles/numbering, part_xml_by_rel_kind selects comments/notes, and header/footer relationship resolution loads bytes as XML. Their unchecked parse_xdocument calls reach recursive parse_element without a construction-depth bound. PartFs and Strict normalization add byte bounds but do not close this auxiliary XML-policy gap.
The assigned source further records the converter's comment-thread path: part_xml_by_rel_kind loads comments/commentsExtended, then unchecked parsing occurs at src/convert/mod.rs:7669-7675 and :7688-7689. This shares the missing extension-independent XML admission control; the separately checked src/comments.rs:467-468 CommentFamily::load is excluded.
Revision listing and comparison independently share the same extension-based policy gap: document_comparer::notes_part_names resolves internal footnotes/endnotes targets regardless of filename, and get_revisions (:6318-6328) and compare notes parse_part_root (:6676-6689) call unchecked parse_xdocument on those actual strings. A central active-limit XML-consumption boundary covering all these consumers subsumes every source; fixing renderer-only calls would leave revision/comparison paths reachable.
Admission infers XML coverage from a filename suffix, but consumers infer XML from relationship role. The consumer trusts admission for parts the gate never parsed.
The discovery-0009 rendering trace additionally specifies a normal Transitional package and disabled link styles, leaving selected styles.bin nesting unchanged through load_stylesheet; neither filename/content-type enforcement nor later auxiliary admission intervenes. Markdown Package::xml separately checks its XML and is excluded from this trace.
The revision_processor trace resolves headers, footers, endnotes, footnotes, comments and styles without extension constraints, then parses selected XML both during RevisionIds collection (:3785-3794) and process_part transforms (:3732-3748). The suffix admission gap precedes these independent operation paths.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): Admission trusts filename extensions to identify XML, but the consumer identifies auxiliary XML by relationship type and invokes recursive unchecked parsing.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): The policy gate classifies XML by archive filename, then checks only a renamed main document as a special case. Rendering instead selects header/footer parts by relationships and interprets their bytes as XML regardless of name. The downstream raw DOM parser relies on prior admission and recurses once per element, leaving renamed story parts outside the depth invariant. Comparison preprocessing repeats this boundary mismatch for relationship-selected styles, notes and charts.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): Admission gates XML depth/tag checks on `.xml`/`.rels` suffixes and only adds a main-part fallback. Comparator preprocessing instead trusts relationship types to identify notes, loads their text regardless of name and invokes unchecked recursive `parse_xdocument()`. Semantic XML consumers therefore receive unbounded nesting despite successful package admission.
The supplied discovery-0018 trace adds existing_comment_ids in edit initialization (src/edit.rs:2154-2158,5552-5563), reached before CommentFamily::load. The later checked loader therefore does not protect the earlier recursive parse. The assigned trace preserves main_rel_part's support for arbitrary internal target names and the main-part-only fallback check. It does not establish every mapped auxiliary consumer as vulnerable.

previousFindings.remediation: Apply active InputLimits at a centralized checked XML access/parse boundary for every semantic XML consumer regardless of filename, or resolve/classify and admit XML through actual content-type/relationship use. Cover theme, styles, numbering, converter comments/commentsExtended, notes and headers/footers; include settings in regression coverage while retaining the source distinction that it was recommended rather than confirmed here. Preserve renamed-main checks, and enforce actual DOM construction depth or use iterative construction. Apply that same mandatory checked boundary to get_revisions and comparison notes parsing, including both footnotes and endnotes; propagate typed refusal under the active comparer InputLimits. Include pre_process_markup's relationship-selected notes at src/document_comparer.rs:4725-4750 and exposed Python get_revisions_json/WASM getRevisions; valid arbitrary part names remain supported. Include diagram and text-box relationship targets in regression coverage as proposed subcases, without promoting them to newly validated affected consumers. Cover revision_processor RevisionIds collection and process_part for all six selected auxiliary buckets (headers, footers, endnotes, footnotes, comments and styles), including public revision acceptance/rejection. Explicitly include the now-confirmed fontTable loader (src/convert/font_table.rs:66-78; src/convert/mod.rs:806) in the mandatory checked XML boundary; parsing must be bounded before any font root/entry inspection. Explicitly cover comparison defined_style_ids (src/document_comparer.rs:4684-4696), relationship-selected footnotes/endnotes (4724-4750) and chart preprocessing (4861-4878), all reached through admitted nonidentical comparison inputs (6555-6569,6607-6625). Apply the same mandatory XML boundary before edit initialization's existing_comment_ids scan, not only in the later checked CommentFamily loader; preserve the effective checks at inspect::parse_part_within and edit::load_stories.

validation.summary:
The validated styles-specific trace confirms a normal main document can select deeply nested styles.bin, without suffix/content-type enforcement or a later depth gate. The other validated trace confirms theme1.bin plus styles, numbering, comments, footnotes, endnotes and relationship-named headers/footers. Byte, inflation, CRC, ZIP/path checks and the nonstandard-main exception remain active; the malicious auxiliary payload alone bypasses XML policy. No external relationship or network fetch is needed.
The additional validated trace confirms converter commentsExtended as well as comments/notes/chrome consumers. A roughly 700 KiB part with 100000 nested elements fits byte limits; actual failing depth remains runtime-dependent and unmeasured. For a normal Transitional DOCX, normalization leaves the renamed part unchanged (src/strict_translation.rs:809-831); PartFs adds byte bounds rather than XML policy. This does not affect separately validated CommentFamily::load (src/comments.rs:467-468).
Verified public `get_revisions` input admission, internal relationship resolution without suffix restrictions, bounded ZIP loading that does not validate auxiliary XML, and the recursive parser sink. The comparison notes pipeline has the same missing check.
Parent verified suffix gate, main-only fallback, relationship resolver and get_revisions parser plus Python/WASM exposure. Deep notes.dat XML is parsed before note-definition processing. pre_process_markup independently follows and parses the same relationship-selected parts at4725-4750.
Assigned discovery-0008 corroboration: Independently verified Attacker DOCX styles relationship -> main_rel_part -> part_string(styles.bin) -> load_stylesheet -> Dom::parse_xdocument -> recursive parse_element.
Assigned discovery-0009 corroboration (preserved offline Standard validation): Confirmed that the main-only extension fallback in admission.rs:556-569 does not cover auxiliary parts; PartFs::read_package bounds inflated bytes but does not validate auxiliary XML. A Transitional DOCX with an internal styles relationship targeting a deeply nested .bin part reaches load_stylesheet's unchecked parser. No content-type extension requirement or later checked parse blocks this path.
Assigned discovery-0010 Standard corroboration (source validation, not reducer verification): Parent verified suffix classification/main exception, all six revision relationship buckets, RevisionIds/process_part parses and independent comparison notes parses. PartFs reads the selected bytes in memory without adding XML policy. A valid internal relationship/content type can name word/notes.dat; external relationships are excluded.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Parent traced admission.rs:533-569 classification/main exception, font_table.rs:66-78 loader, convert/mod.rs:806 and21310-21318 relationship selection, and parse.rs:660-663 recursive call. A normal main part plus fontTable target word/fontTable.bin containing100000 nested x tags stays within physical byte budgets and reaches recursion without depth policy.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Confirmed that a valid minimal main document and its shallow .rels can select a header.bin payload; default archive and byte budgets still allow many thousands of short nested tags. Strict-to-transitional conversion preserves non-XML parts (src/strict_translation.rs:809-831), and PartFs::open bounds bytes rather than applying XML depth (src/opc/mod.rs:282-350). The raw header parser therefore receives the unbounded nesting. Parent source review also confirms the same root gap in comparison preprocessing for footnotes/endnotes, styles and charts (src/document_comparer.rs:4685-4696,4724-4750,4861-4878), reached after admission and PartFs opening (6559-6568,6607-6625).
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Compared nonidentical packages are admitted, opened, then passed to pre_process_markup. An internal footnotes/endnotes relationship can name a safe `.bin` part with an XML content-type override; PartFs stores/returns it without adding an XML-depth check. The note parser runs before note-reference/shape handling, reaching recursive descent.

controls: Normal .xml auxiliary parts and an unusually named main part receive depth checks. PartFs also bounds archive inflation. Neither control checks the nesting of the non-XML-named auxiliary part before recursive parsing. The raw parser is documented as unchecked; the issue is its use on an admitted package path.

dataflow.summary: Admission checks XML depth and tag policy only for entry names ending in .xml or .rels, with an additional special case for the main document part. The converter resolves the fontTable relationship to an arbitrary package part name and passes its text to the infallible recursive DOM parser. An auxiliary fontTable.bin therefore bypasses the admission scan while remaining a reachable XML consumer. Matching auxiliary relationship targets control names for theme/styles/comments/notes/header/footer and chart data. A .bin target bypasses extension admission; the corresponding caller parses it before semantic use. Edit constructs comment IDs before its checked CommentFamily load.

impact.rationale: A valid small main document and a fontTable relationship targeting a deeply nested fontTable.bin can cause recursive parse_element calls until stack overflow, terminating a native embedding process or failing a WASM instance. The advertised 256-element admission depth does not apply to that part.

likelihood.rationale: Compact attacker-selected values/content reach the sink without extra privileges; no deployment-specific authentication bypass is required.

extensions.semanticReductionNotes:
Both reports concern the same extension-based admission gap; a complete extension-independent XML-consumption policy must cover every listed auxiliary part. The raw unchecked parser is documented trusted-only; the finding concerns its automatic invocation on incompletely admitted document content. The malformed-main-XML parser differential and Markdown reference-admission omission remain separate findings because correcting auxiliary part selection alone does not repair them.
dedup-0002 adds validated converter commentsExtended/thread parsing, the ~700 KiB/100000-nesting framing, normalization and fallback nuances, and the explicitly protected CommentFamily::load exclusion. Settings remains a regression recommendation, not a newly established vulnerable consumer. DTD-literal and unquoted-attribute parser disagreements remain independently actionable: extension-independent auxiliary selection alone does not fix either.
dedup-0003 absorbs the same suffix-only auxiliary XML admission root issue and preserves the independent get_revisions and comparison notes entrypoints, notes_part_names resolution, both footnotes/endnotes, checked API exclusion and active-limit/refusal requirements. A complete centralized XML-consumption fix must cover every listed consumer; renderer-only patching is insufficient. Existing malformed-attribute, DTD-literal and reference-template findings remain separate because correcting suffix classification alone does not fix them.
dedup-0004: Same suffix-based XML policy versus role-selected auxiliary consumer. The previous aggregate already covers get_revisions and compare notes as well as renderer consumers. Preserve assigned pre_process_markup:4725-4750, footnotes/endnotes, notes.dat, Python get_revisions_json and WASM getRevisions anchors; the retained mandatory active-limit semantic XML boundary subsumes them. Protected checked consumers and unusual main-part exception remain excluded.
dedup-0006: Same styles.bin -> load_stylesheet -> unchecked recursive DOM instance, covered by the retained extension-independent active XML-consumption boundary. Keep main-only admission and archive byte controls, internal-relationship prerequisite and untested stack threshold. New fontTable/settings regression suggestions are not newly confirmed affected consumers; prior confirmed consumers and exclusions remain intact.
dedup-0007: Same suffix-only auxiliary admission versus internal relationship-selected XML at the retained styles/header/footer/notes consumers. The existing mandatory active-limit XML-consumption boundary subsumes this source, including rendering, and retains the independent revision/comparison paths. dedup-0008: The same suffix-only XML admission versus relationship-selected auxiliary XML. dedup-0012: Same filename-selected XML admission gap and relationship-selected raw parsing. Central active-limit checking for every semantic XML target subsumes headers/footers and comparison styles/notes/charts. previousFindings.title: Processing renamed auxiliary XML bypasses XML depth limits
previousFindings.summary: A DOCX author can put deeply nested auxiliary XML under a non-.xml/.rels suffix. Admission drains those bytes without XML policy, while rendering, revision listing, revision acceptance/rejection and comparison follow internal relationships and recursively build a DOM. Confirmed rendering parts include theme, styles, numbering, comments/commentsExtended, notes and headers/footers; get_revisions and comparison also parse renamed footnotes/endnotes. A small admitted package can terminate the native host or trap WASM. The assigned source additionally confirms eager relationship-selected fontTable parsing before font inspection, including renamed fontTable.bin. Comparison preprocessing also follows renamed styles and charts, alongside footnotes/endnotes. The assigned Standard source additionally identifies edit initialization's existing_comment_ids on relationship-selected comments before the later checked CommentFamily loader. Assigned discovery-0019 corroborates the same shared selector for styles, theme, numbering and fontTable under .bin names; its proof is limited to those four consumers, while earlier validated consumer paths remain retained.

severity.rationale: Untrusted document bytes cross a public parser boundary and can terminate the rendering process. External shared-service exposure is conditional; no code execution or file access is established.
severity.changeConditions: Effective per-document worker isolation limits impact; enforcing active XML policy on every consumed XML part removes this path.

confidence.rationale: Parent independently verified the extension-based admission gate, relationship-selected consumer and unchecked recursive parser. Runtime stack threshold was not tested.

rootCause.summary:
Admission chooses XML depth/tag checks by .xml/.rels filename and applies extension-independent checking only to the main part. Relationship-selected auxiliary consumers do not require XML suffixes or an enforcing content-type check: main_rel_part selects theme/styles/numbering, part_xml_by_rel_kind selects comments/notes, and header/footer relationship resolution loads bytes as XML. Their unchecked parse_xdocument calls reach recursive parse_element without a construction-depth bound. PartFs and Strict normalization add byte bounds but do not close this auxiliary XML-policy gap.
The assigned source further records the converter's comment-thread path: part_xml_by_rel_kind loads comments/commentsExtended, then unchecked parsing occurs at src/convert/mod.rs:7669-7675 and :7688-7689. This shares the missing extension-independent XML admission control; the separately checked src/comments.rs:467-468 CommentFamily::load is excluded.
Revision listing and comparison independently share the same extension-based policy gap: document_comparer::notes_part_names resolves internal footnotes/endnotes targets regardless of filename, and get_revisions (:6318-6328) and compare notes parse_part_root (:6676-6689) call unchecked parse_xdocument on those actual strings. A central active-limit XML-consumption boundary covering all these consumers subsumes every source; fixing renderer-only calls would leave revision/comparison paths reachable.
Admission infers XML coverage from a filename suffix, but consumers infer XML from relationship role. The consumer trusts admission for parts the gate never parsed.
The discovery-0009 rendering trace additionally specifies a normal Transitional package and disabled link styles, leaving selected styles.bin nesting unchanged through load_stylesheet; neither filename/content-type enforcement nor later auxiliary admission intervenes. Markdown Package::xml separately checks its XML and is excluded from this trace.
The revision_processor trace resolves headers, footers, endnotes, footnotes, comments and styles without extension constraints, then parses selected XML both during RevisionIds collection (:3785-3794) and process_part transforms (:3732-3748). The suffix admission gap precedes these independent operation paths.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): Admission trusts filename extensions to identify XML, but the consumer identifies auxiliary XML by relationship type and invokes recursive unchecked parsing.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): The policy gate classifies XML by archive filename, then checks only a renamed main document as a special case. Rendering instead selects header/footer parts by relationships and interprets their bytes as XML regardless of name. The downstream raw DOM parser relies on prior admission and recurses once per element, leaving renamed story parts outside the depth invariant. Comparison preprocessing repeats this boundary mismatch for relationship-selected styles, notes and charts.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): Admission gates XML depth/tag checks on `.xml`/`.rels` suffixes and only adds a main-part fallback. Comparator preprocessing instead trusts relationship types to identify notes, loads their text regardless of name and invokes unchecked recursive `parse_xdocument()`. Semantic XML consumers therefore receive unbounded nesting despite successful package admission.
The supplied discovery-0018 trace adds existing_comment_ids in edit initialization (src/edit.rs:2154-2158,5552-5563), reached before CommentFamily::load. The later checked loader therefore does not protect the earlier recursive parse. The assigned trace preserves main_rel_part's support for arbitrary internal target names and the main-part-only fallback check. It does not establish every mapped auxiliary consumer as vulnerable.

previousFindings.remediation: Apply active InputLimits at a centralized checked XML access/parse boundary for every semantic XML consumer regardless of filename, or resolve/classify and admit XML through actual content-type/relationship use. Cover theme, styles, numbering, converter comments/commentsExtended, notes and headers/footers; include settings in regression coverage while retaining the source distinction that it was recommended rather than confirmed here. Preserve renamed-main checks, and enforce actual DOM construction depth or use iterative construction. Apply that same mandatory checked boundary to get_revisions and comparison notes parsing, including both footnotes and endnotes; propagate typed refusal under the active comparer InputLimits. Include pre_process_markup's relationship-selected notes at src/document_comparer.rs:4725-4750 and exposed Python get_revisions_json/WASM getRevisions; valid arbitrary part names remain supported. Include diagram and text-box relationship targets in regression coverage as proposed subcases, without promoting them to newly validated affected consumers. Cover revision_processor RevisionIds collection and process_part for all six selected auxiliary buckets (headers, footers, endnotes, footnotes, comments and styles), including public revision acceptance/rejection. Explicitly include the now-confirmed fontTable loader (src/convert/font_table.rs:66-78; src/convert/mod.rs:806) in the mandatory checked XML boundary; parsing must be bounded before any font root/entry inspection. Explicitly cover comparison defined_style_ids (src/document_comparer.rs:4684-4696), relationship-selected footnotes/endnotes (4724-4750) and chart preprocessing (4861-4878), all reached through admitted nonidentical comparison inputs (6555-6569,6607-6625). Apply the same mandatory XML boundary before edit initialization's existing_comment_ids scan, not only in the later checked CommentFamily loader; preserve the effective checks at inspect::parse_part_within and edit::load_stories.

The other validated trace confirms theme1.bin plus styles, numbering, comments, footnotes, endnotes and relationship-named headers/footers. Byte, inflation, CRC, ZIP/path checks and the nonstandard-main exception remain active; the malicious auxiliary payload alone bypasses XML policy. No external relationship or network fetch is needed.
The additional validated trace confirms converter commentsExtended as well as comments/notes/chrome consumers. For a normal Transitional DOCX, normalization leaves the renamed part unchanged (src/strict_translation.rs:809-831); PartFs adds byte bounds rather than XML policy. This does not affect separately validated CommentFamily::load (src/comments.rs:467-468).

Parent verified suffix gate, main-only fallback, relationship resolver and get_revisions parser plus Python/WASM exposure. Deep notes.dat XML is parsed before note-definition processing. pre_process_markup independently follows and parses the same relationship-selected parts at4725-4750.

Assigned discovery-0009 corroboration (preserved offline Standard validation): Confirmed that the main-only extension fallback in admission.rs:556-569 does not cover auxiliary parts; PartFs::read_package bounds inflated bytes but does not validate auxiliary XML. A Transitional DOCX with an internal styles relationship targeting a deeply nested .bin part reaches load_stylesheet's unchecked parser. No content-type extension requirement or later checked parse blocks this path.
Assigned discovery-0010 Standard corroboration (source validation, not reducer verification): Parent verified suffix classification/main exception, all six revision relationship buckets, RevisionIds/process_part parses and independent comparison notes parses. Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Parent traced admission.rs:533-569 classification/main exception, font_table.rs:66-78 loader, convert/mod.rs:806 and21310-21318 relationship selection, and parse.rs:660-663 recursive call. Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Confirmed that a valid minimal main document and its shallow .rels can select a header.bin payload; default archive and byte budgets still allow many thousands of short nested tags. Strict-to-transitional conversion preserves non-XML parts (src/strict_translation.rs:809-831), and PartFs::open bounds bytes rather than applying XML depth (src/opc/mod.rs:282-350). The raw header parser therefore receives the unbounded nesting. The note parser runs before note-reference/shape handling, reaching recursive descent.

previousFindings.title: Processing renamed auxiliary XML bypasses XML depth limits
previousFindings.summary: A DOCX author can put deeply nested auxiliary XML under a non-.xml/.rels suffix. Admission drains those bytes without XML policy, while rendering, revision listing, revision acceptance/rejection and comparison follow internal relationships and recursively build a DOM. Confirmed rendering parts include theme, styles, numbering, comments/commentsExtended, notes and headers/footers; get_revisions and comparison also parse renamed footnotes/endnotes. A small admitted package can terminate the native host or trap WASM. The assigned source additionally confirms eager relationship-selected fontTable parsing before font inspection, including renamed fontTable.bin. Comparison preprocessing also follows renamed styles and charts, alongside footnotes/endnotes. The assigned Standard source additionally identifies edit initialization's existing_comment_ids on relationship-selected comments before the later checked CommentFamily loader. Assigned discovery-0019 corroborates the same shared selector for styles, theme, numbering and fontTable under .bin names; its proof is limited to those four consumers, while earlier validated consumer paths remain retained.

severity.rationale: Untrusted document bytes cross a public parser boundary and can terminate the rendering process. External shared-service exposure is conditional; no code execution or file access is established.
severity.changeConditions: Effective per-document worker isolation limits impact; enforcing active XML policy on every consumed XML part removes this path.

confidence.rationale: Parent independently verified the extension-based admission gate, relationship-selected consumer and unchecked recursive parser. Runtime stack threshold was not tested.

rootCause.summary:
Admission chooses XML depth/tag checks by .xml/.rels filename and applies extension-independent checking only to the main part. Relationship-selected auxiliary consumers do not require XML suffixes or an enforcing content-type check: main_rel_part selects theme/styles/numbering, part_xml_by_rel_kind selects comments/notes, and header/footer relationship resolution loads bytes as XML. Their unchecked parse_xdocument calls reach recursive parse_element without a construction-depth bound. PartFs and Strict normalization add byte bounds but do not close this auxiliary XML-policy gap.
The assigned source further records the converter's comment-thread path: part_xml_by_rel_kind loads comments/commentsExtended, then unchecked parsing occurs at src/convert/mod.rs:7669-7675 and :7688-7689. This shares the missing extension-independent XML admission control; the separately checked src/comments.rs:467-468 CommentFamily::load is excluded.
Revision listing and comparison independently share the same extension-based policy gap: document_comparer::notes_part_names resolves internal footnotes/endnotes targets regardless of filename, and get_revisions (:6318-6328) and compare notes parse_part_root (:6676-6689) call unchecked parse_xdocument on those actual strings. A central active-limit XML-consumption boundary covering all these consumers subsumes every source; fixing renderer-only calls would leave revision/comparison paths reachable.
Admission infers XML coverage from a filename suffix, but consumers infer XML from relationship role. The consumer trusts admission for parts the gate never parsed.
The discovery-0009 rendering trace additionally specifies a normal Transitional package and disabled link styles, leaving selected styles.bin nesting unchanged through load_stylesheet; neither filename/content-type enforcement nor later auxiliary admission intervenes. Markdown Package::xml separately checks its XML and is excluded from this trace.
The revision_processor trace resolves headers, footers, endnotes, footnotes, comments and styles without extension constraints, then parses selected XML both during RevisionIds collection (:3785-3794) and process_part transforms (:3732-3748). The suffix admission gap precedes these independent operation paths.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): Admission trusts filename extensions to identify XML, but the consumer identifies auxiliary XML by relationship type and invokes recursive unchecked parsing.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): The policy gate classifies XML by archive filename, then checks only a renamed main document as a special case. Rendering instead selects header/footer parts by relationships and interprets their bytes as XML regardless of name. The downstream raw DOM parser relies on prior admission and recurses once per element, leaving renamed story parts outside the depth invariant. Comparison preprocessing repeats this boundary mismatch for relationship-selected styles, notes and charts.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): Admission gates XML depth/tag checks on `.xml`/`.rels` suffixes and only adds a main-part fallback. Comparator preprocessing instead trusts relationship types to identify notes, loads their text regardless of name and invokes unchecked recursive `parse_xdocument()`. Semantic XML consumers therefore receive unbounded nesting despite successful package admission.
The supplied discovery-0018 trace adds existing_comment_ids in edit initialization (src/edit.rs:2154-2158,5552-5563), reached before CommentFamily::load. The later checked loader therefore does not protect the earlier recursive parse. The assigned trace preserves main_rel_part's support for arbitrary internal target names and the main-part-only fallback check. It does not establish every mapped auxiliary consumer as vulnerable.
Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: The admission boundary decides XML policy by filename extension, while consumers decide what is XML by relationship semantics. Renamed auxiliary parts bypass admission and reach a recursive parser whose safety depends on that admission.

Cover theme, styles, numbering, converter comments/commentsExtended, notes and headers/footers; include settings in regression coverage while retaining the source distinction that it was recommended rather than confirmed here. Preserve renamed-main checks, and enforce actual DOM construction depth or use iterative construction. Apply that same mandatory checked boundary to get_revisions and comparison notes parsing, including both footnotes and endnotes; propagate typed refusal under the active comparer InputLimits. Include pre_process_markup's relationship-selected notes at src/document_comparer.rs:4725-4750 and exposed Python get_revisions_json/WASM getRevisions; valid arbitrary part names remain supported. Include diagram and text-box relationship targets in regression coverage as proposed subcases, without promoting them to newly validated affected consumers. Cover revision_processor RevisionIds collection and process_part for all six selected auxiliary buckets (headers, footers, endnotes, footnotes, comments and styles), including public revision acceptance/rejection. Explicitly include the now-confirmed fontTable loader (src/convert/font_table.rs:66-78; src/convert/mod.rs:806) in the mandatory checked XML boundary; parsing must be bounded before any font root/entry inspection. Explicitly cover comparison defined_style_ids (src/document_comparer.rs:4684-4696), relationship-selected footnotes/endnotes (4724-4750) and chart preprocessing (4861-4878), all reached through admitted nonidentical comparison inputs (6555-6569,6607-6625). Cover both get_revisions and compare with the same relationship-selected deep part.

Retain valid nonstandard part names and ordinary depth-boundary behavior.

Cover fontTable, settings, themes and story relationship consumers under renamed auxiliary parts and explicit raised limits.
Render a package with a styles relationship to deeply nested styles.bin and assert INVALID_XML before DOM construction.
Cover header/footer, notes, diagram and text-box relationship targets with nonstandard extensions and active depth/tag budgets.
Verify valid nonstandard auxiliary filenames continue to render.
Add deterministic regression inputs for the source-supported differential and assert a typed bounded refusal.
Verify ordinary compatible documents still process under unchanged limits.

Repeat with custom part names and raised/lowered InputLimits; ordinary shallow parts must remain supported.

Custom-named auxiliary XML also honors attribute/tag budgets under active InputLimits.
Ordinary valid custom-named notes continue to compare.
Use relationship-routed auxiliary XML with a non-XML extension exceeding the configured depth; require INVALID_XML before DOM construction.

Keep the renamed-main-part check and ordinary valid nonstandard auxiliary names supported.
Use non-.xml targets for each revision-bearing relationship and assert depth/tag violations are refused.
Cover custom main-part names, ordinary valid auxiliary targets, and preserved active limits.

extensions.semanticReductionNotes:
Both reports concern the same extension-based admission gap; a complete extension-independent XML-consumption policy must cover every listed auxiliary part. The raw unchecked parser is documented trusted-only; the finding concerns its automatic invocation on incompletely admitted document content. The malformed-main-XML parser differential and Markdown reference-admission omission remain separate findings because correcting auxiliary part selection alone does not repair them.
dedup-0002 adds validated converter commentsExtended/thread parsing, the ~700 KiB/100000-nesting framing, normalization and fallback nuances, and the explicitly protected CommentFamily::load exclusion. Settings remains a regression recommendation, not a newly established vulnerable consumer. DTD-literal and unquoted-attribute parser disagreements remain independently actionable: extension-independent auxiliary selection alone does not fix either.
dedup-0003 absorbs the same suffix-only auxiliary XML admission root issue and preserves the independent get_revisions and comparison notes entrypoints, notes_part_names resolution, both footnotes/endnotes, checked API exclusion and active-limit/refusal requirements. A complete centralized XML-consumption fix must cover every listed consumer; renderer-only patching is insufficient. Existing malformed-attribute, DTD-literal and reference-template findings remain separate because correcting suffix classification alone does not fix them.
dedup-0004: Same suffix-based XML policy versus role-selected auxiliary consumer. The previous aggregate already covers get_revisions and compare notes as well as renderer consumers. Preserve assigned pre_process_markup:4725-4750, footnotes/endnotes, notes.dat, Python get_revisions_json and WASM getRevisions anchors; the retained mandatory active-limit semantic XML boundary subsumes them. Protected checked consumers and unusual main-part exception remain excluded.
dedup-0006: Same styles.bin -> load_stylesheet -> unchecked recursive DOM instance, covered by the retained extension-independent active XML-consumption boundary. Keep main-only admission and archive byte controls, internal-relationship prerequisite and untested stack threshold. New fontTable/settings regression suggestions are not newly confirmed affected consumers; prior confirmed consumers and exclusions remain intact.
dedup-0007: Same suffix-only auxiliary admission versus internal relationship-selected XML at the retained styles/header/footer/notes consumers. The existing mandatory active-limit XML-consumption boundary subsumes this source, including rendering, and retains the independent revision/comparison paths. Preserve Transitional styles.bin with link styles disabled, main-only exception, byte/count budgets, and the separately checked Markdown Package::xml exclusion. Diagram and text-box regression cases are recommendations from this source, not newly confirmed vulnerable consumers.
dedup-0008: The same suffix-only XML admission versus relationship-selected auxiliary XML. The retained mandatory active-limit XML boundary must now explicitly cover revision_processor's all-six auxiliary buckets, RevisionIds collection and process_part transforms as well as comparison/render/get_revisions. dedup-0011: Same suffix-based admission versus semantic relationship-selected auxiliary parser. dedup-0012: Same filename-selected XML admission gap and relationship-selected raw parsing. dedup-0014: Same filename-selected admission versus relationship-selected footnotes/endnotes mismatch. dedup-0017: Same filename-based auxiliary XML admission gap before relationship-selected unchecked DOM parsing. dedup-0018: The retained mandatory active-limit XML boundary explicitly covers revision acceptance/rejection, RevisionIds collection and all six relationship-selected auxiliary buckets. findings.summary:
Malformed unquoted attributes can make tolerant package admission observe shallow XML while the permissive DOM constructs deeply nested elements without a depth guard. Repeated sibling

tags are one framing; a=x followed by b="x>..." can expose attribute-contained tags as another. Rendering is the earlier affected route; WmlDocument::from_bytes followed by lazy main_document is the newly supplied route. Strict checked inspection rejects the malformed attribute form. A further supplied shallow sibling framing, x>, makes the DOM swallow the closing tag as attribute text and treat following siblings as descendants.

severity.rationale: A small attacker-authored document can cause unbounded parser recursion in the host process through a public parser boundary. Impact is availability loss; shared service use and process isolation determine wider impact.

confidence.rationale: Independent source review confirmed both product parser paths and cached quick-xml 0.42.0 tokenization: final /> is stripped into an Empty event and HTML attributes accept the remaining unquoted slash.

rootCause.summary:
The admission gate allows HTML-style unquoted attributes, while the downstream parser assumes any first character after `=` opens a quoted value. For `

` admission sees an empty tag with an unquoted slash value. DOM parsing consumes both slashes as delimiters, sees an ordinary closing `>` and recursively nests following siblings. Thus reader depth is not the depth of the representation actually constructed. Assigned discovery-0023 corroboration: Admission uses quick-xml's event scanner and HTML attribute iterator, which treats `a=x b="x>..."` as one unquoted and one quoted attribute. Literal `` strings within b remain attribute content, so admission sees a shallow document. The DOM parser instead treats the first x after a= as a quote delimiter and consumes through b's first x. It then treats the next `>` as the root-tag end, exposing the hidden `` strings as elements. Recursive child parsing has no independent depth limit, so a roughly 300 KiB attribute containing 100,000 `` strings can cause 100,000 recursive calls despite an admitted depth of one. Assigned discovery-0025 adds repeated x> siblings within normal namespace-qualified document/body wrappers. Tolerant admission observes bounded event depth; the DOM takes x as an opening delimiter and consumes the closing tag until the next x, after which following siblings recurse. WmlDocument::from_bytes -> main_document reaches this consumer; strict checked XML/inspect rejection and direct raw-parser caller obligations are retained.

findings.remediation: Make tolerant attribute tokenization identical between admission and DOM construction or refuse unsupported unquoted values, and enforce a real construction-depth limit or use an iterative DOM parser.

Recursive child parsing has no independent depth limit, so a roughly 300 KiB attribute containing 100,000 `` strings can cause 100,000 recursive calls despite an admitted depth of one.

rootCause.summary:
The public legacy reader decodes WordDocument and 0Table/1Table pieces into StoryChar, preserving field delimiters, then calls Story::blocks with no field-work/depth budget. blocks retains enclosing code/result states in Vec<bool> and recomputes fields.iter().any for each character, including begin/separator/end controls. Repeated begin+separator sets prior frames false, defeating short-circuiting; balanced ends scan shrinking false stacks and displayed results scan all enclosing frames. No O(1) active-code count is maintained.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: Story::blocks recomputes whether any field is in its code phase by scanning all nested field flags on each character, with no nesting/work limit or constant-time aggregate state.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `Story::blocks()` evaluates `fields.iter().any()` for every character. Field begin pushes true and separator sets the top flag false. Nesting fields inside enclosing result phases leaves all older flags false, so each subsequent character scans increasingly many frames.
Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Story::blocks computes whether any enclosing field is in code by rescanning an unbounded Vec<bool> for each input character, rather than maintaining bounded constant-time state.

findings.remediation: Maintain an O(1) active-code-frame count, updating it correctly on begin, separator and end while preserving suppression under any code ancestor. Enforce explicit field-nesting and processing-work budgets for balanced and malformed legacy field streams before excessive work. Keep legacy diagnostic probes cheap and bounded, or enforce the same field/work budgets before invoking the full reader solely for a refusal hint.

validation.summary:
Both validated source traces establish public legacy read/CLI conversion -> main_text -> Story::blocks without a field-depth budget. N begin/separator pairs incur O(N²) Boolean visits; balanced closing controls and result text add scans. At depth 100000, roughly 300 KiB of balanced delimiters requires billions of Boolean examinations. The additional native read_document refusal path invokes legacy_doc::read to decide whether to print a DOC conversion hint, so refusal is not an early protection.
Assigned discovery-0008 corroboration: Independently verified Unencrypted DOC -> legacy_doc::read -> main_text -> Story::blocks -> fields.iter().any on each character; BEGIN pushes true, SEPARATOR changes top to false, END pops.
Assigned discovery-0010 Standard corroboration (source validation, not reducer verification): Parent read main_text control decoding and Story::blocks. Each0x13 pushes true;0x14 makes the newest entry false. Repeating this pair leaves all ancestors false and causes scans summing1+2+...+N; balanced0x15 closes also scan before popping. Physical CFB bounds do not constrain this later work.
Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): For [0x13,0x14] repeated N times followed by N 0x15 markers, the stack grows then shrinks while mostly/all false. Sum of traversed depths is quadratic; N=100000 uses 300000 physical text bytes and tens of billions of predicate checks.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration (preserved Standard static assessment, not reducer verification): Verified public read decodes piece-table text to StoryChar values and calls Story::blocks; compressed and UTF-16 decoders preserve field control characters. Each start/separator pair grows an all-false stack, so iter().any scans a progressively larger prefix. No field-depth cap intervenes in the inspected path.
Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed compressed text retains begin/separator/end codes 0x13/0x14/0x15. Repeated begin+separator pairs model nested fields in their result phase; every all-false prefix is rescanned before later input. Public legacy read invokes this function on the complete decoded story.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Verified the character loop and state transitions; no field-depth budget or cached active-code count exists. Early exit for a true outer code flag is avoided by opening each child after the enclosing separator. Closing the fields still produces a supported parser path; no recursion is required for this CPU attack.

finding.title: Reading or converting nested legacy DOC fields can monopolize the processing thread
finding.summary: An attacker-authored Word 97–2003 document can repeatedly begin fields and enter their result sections. Each input character scans the full stack of result frames, producing quadratic CPU work for a small story and blocking conversion.

severity.rationale: Small untrusted document input can cause disproportionate CPU consumption through public legacy conversion APIs. This affects host availability; shared-server exposure is not assumed and process CPU limits constrain impact.

confidence.rationale: Independent static trace confirms preserved field control characters, an unbounded stack, and a full scan before each character. The operation count follows directly from the loop; no runtime timing claim is made.

rootCause.summary:
The public legacy reader decodes WordDocument and 0Table/1Table pieces into StoryChar, preserving field delimiters, then calls Story::blocks with no field-work/depth budget. blocks retains enclosing code/result states in Vec<bool> and recomputes fields.iter().any for each character, including begin/separator/end controls. Repeated begin+separator sets prior frames false, defeating short-circuiting; balanced ends scan shrinking false stacks and displayed results scan all enclosing frames. No O(1) active-code count is maintained.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: Story::blocks recomputes whether any field is in its code phase by scanning all nested field flags on each character, with no nesting/work limit or constant-time aggregate state.

previousFindings.remediation: Maintain an O(1) active-code-frame count, updating it correctly on begin, separator and end while preserving suppression under any code ancestor. Enforce explicit field-nesting and processing-work budgets for balanced and malformed legacy field streams before excessive work.

validation.summary:
Both validated source traces establish public legacy read/CLI conversion -> main_text -> Story::blocks without a field-depth budget. N begin/separator pairs incur O(N²) Boolean visits; balanced closing controls and result text add scans. At depth 100000, roughly 300 KiB of balanced delimiters requires billions of Boolean examinations. The additional native read_document refusal path invokes legacy_doc::read to decide whether to print a DOC conversion hint, so refusal is not an early protection.
Assigned discovery-0008 corroboration: Independently verified Unencrypted DOC -> legacy_doc::read -> main_text -> Story::blocks -> fields.iter().any on each character; BEGIN pushes true, SEPARATOR changes top to false, END pops.
Assigned discovery-0010 Standard corroboration (source validation, not reducer verification): Parent read main_text control decoding and Story::blocks. Each0x13 pushes true;0x14 makes the newest entry false. Repeating this pair leaves all ancestors false and causes scans summing1+2+...+N; balanced0x15 closes also scan before popping. Physical CFB bounds do not constrain this later work.
Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): For [0x13,0x14] repeated N times followed by N 0x15 markers, the stack grows then shrinks while mostly/all false. Sum of traversed depths is quadratic; N=100000 uses 300000 physical text bytes and tens of billions of predicate checks.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration (preserved Standard static assessment, not reducer verification): Verified public read decodes piece-table text to StoryChar values and calls Story::blocks; compressed and UTF-16 decoders preserve field control characters. Each start/separator pair grows an all-false stack, so iter().any scans a progressively larger prefix. No field-depth cap intervenes in the inspected path.

rootCause.summary:
The public legacy reader decodes WordDocument and 0Table/1Table pieces into StoryChar, preserving field delimiters, then calls Story::blocks with no field-work/depth budget. blocks retains enclosing code/result states in Vec<bool> and recomputes fields.iter().any for each character, including begin/separator/end controls. Repeated begin+separator sets prior frames false, defeating short-circuiting; balanced ends scan shrinking false stacks and displayed results scan all enclosing frames. No O(1) active-code count is maintained.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: Story::blocks recomputes whether any field is in its code phase by scanning all nested field flags on each character, with no nesting/work limit or constant-time aggregate state.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `Story::blocks()` evaluates `fields.iter().any()` for every character. Field begin pushes true and separator sets the top flag false. Nesting fields inside enclosing result phases leaves all older flags false, so each subsequent character scans increasingly many frames.

rootCause.summary:
The public legacy reader decodes WordDocument and 0Table/1Table pieces into StoryChar, preserving field delimiters, then calls Story::blocks with no field-work/depth budget. blocks retains enclosing code/result states in Vec<bool> and recomputes fields.iter().any for each character, including begin/separator/end controls. Repeated begin+separator sets prior frames false, defeating short-circuiting; balanced ends scan shrinking false stacks and displayed results scan all enclosing frames. No O(1) active-code count is maintained.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: Story::blocks recomputes whether any field is in its code phase by scanning all nested field flags on each character, with no nesting/work limit or constant-time aggregate state.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `Story::blocks()` evaluates `fields.iter().any()` for every character. Field begin pushes true and separator sets the top flag false. Nesting fields inside enclosing result phases leaves all older flags false, so each subsequent character scans increasingly many frames.

validation.summary:
Both validated source traces establish public legacy read/CLI conversion -> main_text -> Story::blocks without a field-depth budget. N begin/separator pairs incur O(N²) Boolean visits; balanced closing controls and result text add scans. At depth 100000, roughly 300 KiB of balanced delimiters requires billions of Boolean examinations. The additional native read_document refusal path invokes legacy_doc::read to decide whether to print a DOC conversion hint, so refusal is not an early protection.
Assigned discovery-0008 corroboration: Independently verified Unencrypted DOC -> legacy_doc::read -> main_text -> Story::blocks -> fields.iter().any on each character; BEGIN pushes true, SEPARATOR changes top to false, END pops.
Assigned discovery-0010 Standard corroboration (source validation, not reducer verification): Parent read main_text control decoding and Story::blocks. Each0x13 pushes true;0x14 makes the newest entry false. Repeating this pair leaves all ancestors false and causes scans summing1+2+...+N; balanced0x15 closes also scan before popping. Physical CFB bounds do not constrain this later work.
Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): For [0x13,0x14] repeated N times followed by N 0x15 markers, the stack grows then shrinks while mostly/all false. Sum of traversed depths is quadratic; N=100000 uses 300000 physical text bytes and tens of billions of predicate checks.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration (preserved Standard static assessment, not reducer verification): Verified public read decodes piece-table text to StoryChar values and calls Story::blocks; compressed and UTF-16 decoders preserve field control characters. Each start/separator pair grows an all-false stack, so iter().any scans a progressively larger prefix. No field-depth cap intervenes in the inspected path.
Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed compressed text retains begin/separator/end codes 0x13/0x14/0x15. Repeated begin+separator pairs model nested fields in their result phase; every all-false prefix is rescanned before later input. Public legacy read invokes this function on the complete decoded story.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Verified the character loop and state transitions; no field-depth budget or cached active-code count exists. Early exit for a true outer code flag is avoided by opening each child after the enclosing separator. Closing the fields still produces a supported parser path; no recursion is required for this CPU attack.

rootCause.summary:
The public legacy reader decodes WordDocument and 0Table/1Table pieces into StoryChar, preserving field delimiters, then calls Story::blocks with no field-work/depth budget. blocks retains enclosing code/result states in Vec<bool> and recomputes fields.iter().any for each character, including begin/separator/end controls. Repeated begin+separator sets prior frames false, defeating short-circuiting; balanced ends scan shrinking false stacks and displayed results scan all enclosing frames. No O(1) active-code count is maintained.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: Story::blocks recomputes whether any field is in its code phase by scanning all nested field flags on each character, with no nesting/work limit or constant-time aggregate state.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `Story::blocks()` evaluates `fields.iter().any()` for every character. Field begin pushes true and separator sets the top flag false. Nesting fields inside enclosing result phases leaves all older flags false, so each subsequent character scans increasingly many frames.

previousFindings.remediation: Maintain an O(1) active-code-frame count, updating it correctly on begin, separator and end while preserving suppression under any code ancestor. Enforce explicit field-nesting and processing-work budgets for balanced and malformed legacy field streams before excessive work.

validation.summary:
Both validated source traces establish public legacy read/CLI conversion -> main_text -> Story::blocks without a field-depth budget. N begin/separator pairs incur O(N²) Boolean visits; balanced closing controls and result text add scans. At depth 100000, roughly 300 KiB of balanced delimiters requires billions of Boolean examinations. The additional native read_document refusal path invokes legacy_doc::read to decide whether to print a DOC conversion hint, so refusal is not an early protection.
Assigned discovery-0008 corroboration: Independently verified Unencrypted DOC -> legacy_doc::read -> main_text -> Story::blocks -> fields.iter().any on each character; BEGIN pushes true, SEPARATOR changes top to false, END pops.
Assigned discovery-0010 Standard corroboration (source validation, not reducer verification): Parent read main_text control decoding and Story::blocks. Each0x13 pushes true;0x14 makes the newest entry false. Repeating this pair leaves all ancestors false and causes scans summing1+2+...+N; balanced0x15 closes also scan before popping. Physical CFB bounds do not constrain this later work.
Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): For [0x13,0x14] repeated N times followed by N 0x15 markers, the stack grows then shrinks while mostly/all false. Sum of traversed depths is quadratic; N=100000 uses 300000 physical text bytes and tens of billions of predicate checks.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration (preserved Standard static assessment, not reducer verification): Verified public read decodes piece-table text to StoryChar values and calls Story::blocks; compressed and UTF-16 decoders preserve field control characters. Each start/separator pair grows an all-false stack, so iter().any scans a progressively larger prefix. No field-depth cap intervenes in the inspected path.
Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed compressed text retains begin/separator/end codes 0x13/0x14/0x15. Repeated begin+separator pairs model nested fields in their result phase; every all-false prefix is rescanned before later input. Public legacy read invokes this function on the complete decoded story.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Verified the character loop and state transitions; no field-depth budget or cached active-code count exists. Early exit for a true outer code flag is avoided by opening each child after the enclosing separator. Closing the fields still produces a supported parser path; no recursion is required for this CPU attack.

rootCause.summary:
The public legacy reader decodes WordDocument and 0Table/1Table pieces into StoryChar, preserving field delimiters, then calls Story::blocks with no field-work/depth budget. blocks retains enclosing code/result states in Vec<bool> and recomputes fields.iter().any for each character, including begin/separator/end controls. Repeated begin+separator sets prior frames false, defeating short-circuiting; balanced ends scan shrinking false stacks and displayed results scan all enclosing frames. No O(1) active-code count is maintained.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: Story::blocks recomputes whether any field is in its code phase by scanning all nested field flags on each character, with no nesting/work limit or constant-time aggregate state.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `Story::blocks()` evaluates `fields.iter().any()` for every character. Field begin pushes true and separator sets the top flag false. Nesting fields inside enclosing result phases leaves all older flags false, so each subsequent character scans increasingly many frames.
Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Story::blocks computes whether any enclosing field is in code by rescanning an unbounded Vec<bool> for each input character, rather than maintaining bounded constant-time state.

previousFindings.remediation: Maintain an O(1) active-code-frame count, updating it correctly on begin, separator and end while preserving suppression under any code ancestor. Enforce explicit field-nesting and processing-work budgets for balanced and malformed legacy field streams before excessive work. Keep legacy diagnostic probes cheap and bounded, or enforce the same field/work budgets before invoking the full reader solely for a refusal hint.

validation.summary:
Both validated source traces establish public legacy read/CLI conversion -> main_text -> Story::blocks without a field-depth budget. N begin/separator pairs incur O(N²) Boolean visits; balanced closing controls and result text add scans. At depth 100000, roughly 300 KiB of balanced delimiters requires billions of Boolean examinations. The additional native read_document refusal path invokes legacy_doc::read to decide whether to print a DOC conversion hint, so refusal is not an early protection.
Assigned discovery-0008 corroboration: Independently verified Unencrypted DOC -> legacy_doc::read -> main_text -> Story::blocks -> fields.iter().any on each character; BEGIN pushes true, SEPARATOR changes top to false, END pops.
Assigned discovery-0010 Standard corroboration (source validation, not reducer verification): Parent read main_text control decoding and Story::blocks. Each0x13 pushes true;0x14 makes the newest entry false. Repeating this pair leaves all ancestors false and causes scans summing1+2+...+N; balanced0x15 closes also scan before popping. Physical CFB bounds do not constrain this later work.
Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): For [0x13,0x14] repeated N times followed by N 0x15 markers, the stack grows then shrinks while mostly/all false. Sum of traversed depths is quadratic; N=100000 uses 300000 physical text bytes and tens of billions of predicate checks.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration (preserved Standard static assessment, not reducer verification): Verified public read decodes piece-table text to StoryChar values and calls Story::blocks; compressed and UTF-16 decoders preserve field control characters. Each start/separator pair grows an all-false stack, so iter().any scans a progressively larger prefix. No field-depth cap intervenes in the inspected path.
Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed compressed text retains begin/separator/end codes 0x13/0x14/0x15. Repeated begin+separator pairs model nested fields in their result phase; every all-false prefix is rescanned before later input. Public legacy read invokes this function on the complete decoded story.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Verified the character loop and state transitions; no field-depth budget or cached active-code count exists. Early exit for a true outer code flag is avoided by opening each child after the enclosing separator. Closing the fields still produces a supported parser path; no recursion is required for this CPU attack.
Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Parent verified that nested field starts and separators can maintain a growing all-false stack; on that state fields.iter().any scans all active levels. Repetition yields cumulative quadratic work even without physical piece reuse. Unclosed nesting is accepted until input end. Public read/conversion and native refusal hints reach this loop.

rootCause.summary:
The public legacy reader decodes WordDocument and 0Table/1Table pieces into StoryChar, preserving field delimiters, then calls Story::blocks with no field-work/depth budget. blocks retains enclosing code/result states in Vec<bool> and recomputes fields.iter().any for each character, including begin/separator/end controls. Repeated begin+separator sets prior frames false, defeating short-circuiting; balanced ends scan shrinking false stacks and displayed results scan all enclosing frames. No O(1) active-code count is maintained.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: Story::blocks recomputes whether any field is in its code phase by scanning all nested field flags on each character, with no nesting/work limit or constant-time aggregate state.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `Story::blocks()` evaluates `fields.iter().any()` for every character. Field begin pushes true and separator sets the top flag false. Nesting fields inside enclosing result phases leaves all older flags false, so each subsequent character scans increasingly many frames.
Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Story::blocks computes whether any enclosing field is in code by rescanning an unbounded Vec<bool> for each input character, rather than maintaining bounded constant-time state.

previousFindings.remediation: Maintain an O(1) active-code-frame count, updating it correctly on begin, separator and end while preserving suppression under any code ancestor. Enforce explicit field-nesting and processing-work budgets for balanced and malformed legacy field streams before excessive work. Keep legacy diagnostic probes cheap and bounded, or enforce the same field/work budgets before invoking the full reader solely for a refusal hint.

validation.summary:
Both validated source traces establish public legacy read/CLI conversion -> main_text -> Story::blocks without a field-depth budget. N begin/separator pairs incur O(N²) Boolean visits; balanced closing controls and result text add scans. At depth 100000, roughly 300 KiB of balanced delimiters requires billions of Boolean examinations. The additional native read_document refusal path invokes legacy_doc::read to decide whether to print a DOC conversion hint, so refusal is not an early protection.
Assigned discovery-0008 corroboration: Independently verified Unencrypted DOC -> legacy_doc::read -> main_text -> Story::blocks -> fields.iter().any on each character; BEGIN pushes true, SEPARATOR changes top to false, END pops.

Each0x13 pushes true;0x14 makes the newest entry false. Repeating this pair leaves all ancestors false and causes scans summing1+2+...+N; balanced0x15 closes also scan before popping. findings.title: Large Chicago numbering values can exhaust memory while reading or rendering a DOCX
findings.summary: An untrusted DOCX can select Chicago numbering with a huge list start/startOverride or section page start. The shared chicago_label formatter repeats a UTF-8 symbol roughly n/4 times without a length bound, allowing gigabyte allocations during list rendering, ordinary section-page processing and Markdown numbered-list views. Authored endnote starts also reach this shared formatter. The supplied u32::MAX framing selects 1073741824 double-daggers, about 3 GiB of UTF-8 label bytes; this is static arithmetic. Additional supplied static framing: start=2147483647 selects 536870912 UTF-8 double-daggers (‡), requesting 1.5 GiB of marker bytes before downstream copies.

severity.rationale: Attacker-selected document numbers directly cause excessive allocations in public document-processing paths. Impact is host-process availability; no remote service is assumed and memory isolation limits wider damage.
severity.changeConditions: Enforce derived resource/output bounds before allocation; process-isolated callers limit blast radius.

confidence.rationale: Independent source tracing confirms unbounded document-selected u32 starts, dispatch to `chicago_label()` and its direct `str::repeat()` expansion, plus the Markdown sibling caller.

rootCause.summary:
List starts/startOverrides and section pgNumType starts retain full u32 values. Numbering::next_marker uses the authored first counter and substitutes format_num output; section_page_label independently dispatches its page counter through format_num. Chicago calls chicago_label, which computes i=n.saturating_sub(1) and MARKS[i%4].repeat(i/4+1) without a bound. Markdown list-label generation uses the same shared formatter. Counter saturation prevents overflow but retains enormous values; ordinary paragraph processing evaluates chapter/page labels even before an empty bookmarks loop.
A level-zero list suffices independently of excessive ilvl iteration; bounding level indices alone does not bound Chicago label length.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): Numbering levels accept an uncapped u32 start and the counter renderer passes it to format_num. The Chicago formatter repeats its selected symbol n/4 times without a label-length budget. Page numbering and the DOCX-to-Markdown list view call the same formatter, so the same missing control affects distinct consumers.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): Numbering start/startOverride values enter u32 counters with only max(1). `Numbering::render()` calls `format_num()`, whose Chicago branch repeats one marker `(n-1)/4+1` times without an output budget.
Endnote numStart/format also reaches the same shared formatter through number_endnote_refs; its generated-label budget must cover that route as well as list, page and agent/MCP read-view consumers.
Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: A shared formatter converts a bounded-width but numerically huge input into output proportional to its magnitude, without checking the resulting label length before String::repeat.

findings.remediation: Bound generated byte/glyph length inside the shared Chicago formatter before repetition, with a documented safe cycle/fallback or typed refusal. Apply that bound to all list, startOverride, section-page and Markdown/direct list_number callers; do not rely on input bytes, counter saturation or later clipping. Include authored endnote numStart/format and MCP agent-view callers in the shared formatter budget.

counterEvidence: Other alphabetic and Roman formats have explicit wrapping maxima, but Chicago has no corresponding bound (convert/mod.rs:6492-6520).
Admission constrains input bytes and depth; it does not constrain generated label length.
Counter saturation prevents integer overflow but preserves enormous values.

Admission restricts input bytes and XML structure, not the expanded label. Sibling alphabetic and Roman formatters explicitly cycle at ALPHA_LABEL_MAX and ROMAN_LABEL_MAX (lines 6491-6514); Chicago lacks an equivalent bound.
Host process resource limits can contain failure but do not bound the allocation request.
Alphabetic labels wrap at ALPHA_LABEL_MAX=780 and Roman labels at 32767; those related claims are rejected.

validation.summary:
The validated traces establish full-u32 list/startOverride propagation and independent section-page and Markdown numbered-list callers. A level with chicago, lvlText %1 and start 4294967295 yields 1073741824 repetitions of a three-byte symbol, requesting 3 GiB before shaping/copying. Section labels are evaluated on ordinary paragraphs even without bookmarks. Alphabetic/Roman siblings cycle at explicit maxima; Chicago does not. Source XML remains small and shallow.
Assigned discovery-0008 corroboration: Independently traced DOCX w:lvl/w:start -> NumLevel.start -> next_marker/render -> format_num(Chicago) -> chicago_label::repeat; Markdown list labels call the shared list_number formatter.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): For n=4294967295, chicago_label computes i=4294967294 and repeats the three-byte double-dagger symbol 1073741824 times, requesting 3221225472 bytes before additional copies. A normal numbered paragraph with numFmt=chicago and lvlText=%1 reaches the list renderer. pgNumType/@start with fmt=chicago reaches the page-label branch, and Markdown list_marker delegates to list_number. ZIP/XML depth/byte bounds do not constrain the numeric expansion.
Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed start 4,294,967,295 at normal ilvl=0 selects the three-byte double-dagger marker repeated 1,073,741,824 times: 3,221,225,472 requested output bytes. This is independent of excessive numbering levels.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Verified initial counter selection, render formatting and repeat arithmetic. A start of 4294967295 selects the double-dagger marker and requests 3,221,225,472 UTF-8 bytes. XML size and depth remain small; source byte limits cannot prevent the allocation.
Assigned discovery-0017 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): For n=2147483647, i=n-1=2147483646; i%4=2 selects the three-byte double dagger, and i/4+1=536870912 produces 1610612736 bytes before copies. List starts, startOverride, reader starts, endnote numStart and page pgNumType.start are parsed without a maximum. Both Numbering::render and the agent reader call the shared formatter. The native read_view adapter calls markdown::read (jubarte-python/src/lib.rs:899-901).
Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Parent verified all reported callers of format_num/chicago_label. Rendering list and startOverride, page numbering and endnote numbering accept attacker u32 values; Markdown passes parsed starts/overrides to the same formatter. This is distinct from oversized list-level iteration: even ordinary level zero reaches it.
