validation.summary:
Parent independently read raster_wmf dispatch/record checks and all three polygon handlers, their file-wide reads and outer offset increment. Repeated eight-byte polygon records with point-count 65535 can repeatedly consume later record bytes as coordinate payload; a 512KiB file supports more than two billion decodes before a late truncation refusal. This is bounded by whole-file bytes rather than record bytes; no memory out-of-bounds access is claimed.
Verified that text counts are u16, checked against the entire buffer, and do not need to fit the declared record. A 14-byte EXTTEXTOUT record can claim 65,535 text bytes beyond its own end. Ten thousand such records with enough trailing bytes imply 655,350,000 source bytes decoded into retained Strings from about 205.6 KB of WMF; UTF-8 conversion and later text handling can add cost.
Additional static proof: a placeable WMF with nonzero mapping bounds and fourteen-byte EXTTEXTOUT records (y/x/count/options, options zero, n=65535, no record-local text) reads following records into retained strings. Tens of thousands of such records in roughly 1 MB imply several GB of overlapping decoded text. This is an estimate from the supplied source, not executed memory measurement; ordinary bounds, nonblank content and sufficient trailing data are prerequisites.
Assigned discovery-0010 Standard corroboration (source validation, not reducer verification): Parent confirmed size3 advances6 bytes, EXTTEXTOUT reads count at payload+4, string at payload+8/16 and checks only data.get(at..at+n). Alternating six-byte EXTTEXTOUT/unknown0xFFFF headers supply count65535 from the next header while allowing repeated advancement. ansi_text collects owned strings retained in texts. TEXTOUT shares the record-local bounds omission.
Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): Verified the record cursor at metafile.rs:684 advances by size2 while handlers at 603-620 read against data. Approximately 65536 14-byte records plus 65535 trailing bytes fit in ~1 MiB yet retain at least ~4 GiB of text. WMF detection checks the placeable magic; bounded canvas dimensions do not bound text. Package admission permits such small binary media.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Parent inspected WMF dispatch, header/canvas setup, complete record loop (445-687), ansi_text (430-442) and wmf_text retention (692-716). Repeated eight-byte TEXTOUT records (4 words) can each declare 65535 bytes, with coordinates and tail inside the overall file and an EOF before unused tail; nonzero extents and nonblank bytes satisfy retention. EXTTEXTOUT and all three point-array opcodes share the boundary failure.
Additional assigned static framing: roughly 100000 eight-byte TEXTOUT records each claiming 65535 bytes plus sufficient trailing bytes (EOF before unused tail) fit in roughly 1 MiB and imply several GiB of overlapping retained strings. Nonzero mapping extents and nonblank decoded text are required. Matching short POLYGON/POLYLINE counts imply billions of point iterations. No payload or measurement was executed.
Assigned discovery-0017 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): An 8-byte TEXTOUT record can specify count65535 while declaring size4 words. String, y and x reads use full-file offsets, not the 8-byte record. Repeating those small records with enough trailing bytes permits each to retain about65535 decoded characters; thousands of records multiply memory far beyond the source. POLYGON, POLYPOLYGON and POLYLINE use the same missing record boundary for counted reads. Whole-file checked access prevents memory unsafety but not overlapping repeated interpretation.

previousFindings.title: WMF record-boundary failures amplify polygon work and retained text
previousFindings.summary: Rendering a DOCX with a crafted placeable WMF lets short declared records consume payload from later records, which the outer parser then revisits. Polygon/polypolygon/polyline records can cause billions of coordinate decodes from roughly 512 KiB; EXTTEXTOUT/TEXTOUT records can retain hundreds of megabytes of overlapping owned strings from roughly 205.6 KB. The common missing record-local boundary bypasses the canvas cap and original package budgets. A further framing uses alternating six-byte EXTTEXTOUT and unknown 0xFFFF record headers to claim 65,535 text bytes from subsequent records, implying several GiB of retained strings from roughly 1 MiB of media; this is a static estimate. A supplied 7-word EXTTEXTOUT framing uses 65536 fourteen-byte records plus a 65535-byte suffix in less than 1 MiB and requests about 4 GiB of decoded characters; nonzero mapping dimensions and nonblank text are required. This is a static estimate.

rootCause.summary:
raster_wmf checks declared size*2 against remaining file bytes but keeps passing the entire data slice to its handlers, then advances only by the declared record size. Polygon, polypolygon and polyline counts therefore cause coordinate reads/allocation/raster work across later records. Independently, META_EXTTEXTOUT/META_TEXTOUT counts slice later bytes as text; wmf_text decodes owned Strings retained in texts and ultimately ImageKind::Metafile. Both subcases repeatedly consume overlapping suffixes because consumed payload extent is not tied to outer advancement. EMF's analogous point helper checks off+size. A mandatory record-limited slice plus record-local field/count checks at this shared WMF dispatch boundary fixes all absorbed handlers; geometry-only count patches leave text retention reachable.
With size=3 the outer cursor advances six bytes. EXTTEXTOUT's count at payload+4 can come from the next unknown-0xFFFF header; options may select a later optional-rectangle string offset. Subsequent header bytes repeatedly supply large whole-file text spans. Both drawing and VML image relationships reach this decoder before the general image crate's default 512 MiB allocation limit, which therefore cannot bound this earlier retention. The supplied alternating-header proof gives options=3, selecting the optional-rectangle branch and a string start at payload+16.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): WMF variable-length record data is read against the whole input rather than the record's declared slice; declared record progression permits overlapping unbounded amplification. A seven-word EXTTEXTOUT record contains its six-byte header and eight-byte fixed fields but can start its 65535-byte text range at the next record, because only whole-file bounds are checked.

previousFindings.remediation: Confine every WMF handler, including field, font, string and geometry reads, to a slice limited to its checked declared record extent. Before allocation validate fixed fields, ring/point counts and coordinate arrays, EXTTEXTOUT options/optional rectangle and text count, and TEXTOUT padded string plus trailing coordinates against that slice using checked arithmetic. Refuse inconsistent records before decoding/rasterization/replay and enforce cumulative decoded-text, record and total geometry/work budgets. Keep the already bounded EMF behavior.

validation.summary:
Parent independently read raster_wmf dispatch/record checks and all three polygon handlers, their file-wide reads and outer offset increment. Repeated eight-byte polygon records with point-count 65535 can repeatedly consume later record bytes as coordinate payload; a 512KiB file supports more than two billion decodes before a late truncation refusal. This is bounded by whole-file bytes rather than record bytes; no memory out-of-bounds access is claimed.
Verified that text counts are u16, checked against the entire buffer, and do not need to fit the declared record. A 14-byte EXTTEXTOUT record can claim 65,535 text bytes beyond its own end. Ten thousand such records with enough trailing bytes imply 655,350,000 source bytes decoded into retained Strings from about 205.6 KB of WMF; UTF-8 conversion and later text handling can add cost.
Additional static proof: a placeable WMF with nonzero mapping bounds and fourteen-byte EXTTEXTOUT records (y/x/count/options, options zero, n=65535, no record-local text) reads following records into retained strings. Tens of thousands of such records in roughly 1 MB imply several GB of overlapping decoded text. This is an estimate from the supplied source, not executed memory measurement; ordinary bounds, nonblank content and sufficient trailing data are prerequisites.
Assigned discovery-0010 Standard corroboration (source validation, not reducer verification): Parent confirmed size3 advances6 bytes, EXTTEXTOUT reads count at payload+4, string at payload+8/16 and checks only data.get(at..at+n). Alternating six-byte EXTTEXTOUT/unknown0xFFFF headers supply count65535 from the next header while allowing repeated advancement. ansi_text collects owned strings retained in texts. TEXTOUT shares the record-local bounds omission.
Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): Verified the record cursor at metafile.rs:684 advances by size2 while handlers at 603-620 read against data. Approximately 65536 14-byte records plus 65535 trailing bytes fit in ~1 MiB yet retain at least ~4 GiB of text. WMF detection checks the placeable magic; bounded canvas dimensions do not bound text. Package admission permits such small binary media.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Parent inspected WMF dispatch, header/canvas setup, complete record loop (445-687), ansi_text (430-442) and wmf_text retention (692-716). Repeated eight-byte TEXTOUT records (4 words) can each declare 65535 bytes, with coordinates and tail inside the overall file and an EOF before unused tail; nonzero extents and nonblank bytes satisfy retention. EXTTEXTOUT and all three point-array opcodes share the boundary failure.
Additional assigned static framing: roughly 100000 eight-byte TEXTOUT records each claiming 65535 bytes plus sufficient trailing bytes (EOF before unused tail) fit in roughly 1 MiB and imply several GiB of overlapping retained strings. Nonzero mapping extents and nonblank decoded text are required. Matching short POLYGON/POLYLINE counts imply billions of point iterations. No payload or measurement was executed.
Assigned discovery-0017 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): An 8-byte TEXTOUT record can specify count65535 while declaring size4 words. String, y and x reads use full-file offsets, not the 8-byte record. Repeating those small records with enough trailing bytes permits each to retain about65535 decoded characters; thousands of records multiply memory far beyond the source. POLYGON, POLYPOLYGON and POLYLINE use the same missing record boundary for counted reads. Whole-file checked access prevents memory unsafety but not overlapping repeated interpretation.

extensions.semanticReductionNotes:
The supplied static proof framing uses repeated eight-byte WMF polygon records with count 65535. In a roughly 512 KiB file, the first roughly 32768 records can each decode following-record bytes as 65535 points, exceeding two billion decodes plus polygon scans before late truncation refusal. META_POLYGON, META_POLYPOLYGON and META_POLYLINE all need record-local bounds; the 384-pixel canvas cap, whole-file safe reads and bounded EMF helper do not enforce those WMF record bounds.
dedup-0003 merges the same shared WMF record-slice violation, rather than a mere media/sink family match. Preserve both proof tuples and all five handlers: eight-byte polygon records with count 65535 in ~512 KiB yield >2 billion point decodes; 10000 fourteen-byte EXTTEXTOUT records claiming 65535 bytes with sufficient nonblank following data yield 655350000 source bytes decoded into retained Strings from ~205.6 KB. Text records need nonblank decoded content and valid ordinary mapping to retain MetaText; EXTTEXTOUT rectangle/options and TEXTOUT padding/coordinate layouts require record-local checks. The text source independently validates its text consequences, while previous validated evidence establishes geometry consequences. Actual failure thresholds remain unmeasured. The common remediation limits the slice at dispatch for every handler; fixing only polygon handlers would not subsume the text source. MAX_SIDE=384, object-count clamps and safe whole-file reads remain useful but do not limit these repeated payloads.
dedup-0005: Same raster_wmf record extent versus whole-file handler access. Mandatory checked record slices across all field/string/font/geometry handlers subsume the assigned text and geometry report; a geometry-only patch would not. The assigned proof uses nonzero placeable bounds, fourteen-byte EXTTEXTOUT y/x/count/options headers with options=0 and n=65535, no local text, and tens of thousands of records in roughly 1 MB to retain several GB of overlapping decoded strings. This supplements, rather than replaces, the prior 10,000-record/~205.6 KB text and ~512 KiB polygon proofs. Preserve nonblank/mapping prerequisites, size>=3 words/advancing cursor, canvas clipping, whole-file memory safety and absent runtime measurements.
dedup-0008: The same WMF dispatch-wide missing record-local boundary; the retained mandatory record slice and field/count checks subsume the six-byte size=3 alternating EXTTEXTOUT/unknown-0xFFFF framing, including VML image callers. Preserve prior polygon, polyline, polypolygon, fourteen-byte text and TEXTOUT proofs, new several-GiB estimate and options/rectangle nuance. Geometry-only or one-text-handler-only repairs are insufficient; no runtime memory measurement or memory-unsafe access is asserted.
dedup-0009: Same placeable-WMF whole-buffer payload/short-record advancement instance. Mandatory declared-record slices with count/field checks and cumulative text/geometry/work budgets subsume this text-only corroboration while preserving the earlier independent polygon and text subcases. Preserve 65,536 fourteen-byte EXTTEXTOUT records plus 65,535 trailing bytes (~1 MiB, >=~4 GiB retained text), nondegenerate mapping and nonblank text preconditions. Existing six-byte/options and TEXTOUT/polygon proofs remain.
dedup-0011: Same WMF declared-record extent versus whole-file payload readers and short advancement. The mandatory shared record slice plus fixed/count/array/string checks subsumes text and geometry handlers; fixing only one handler would not. Preserve eight-byte TEXTOUT records with count 65535 and sufficient trailing coordinates/nonblank text, EOF before unused tail, EXTTEXTOUT rectangle/options, all three point-array opcodes, record-local padding, bounded canvas/EMF countercontrols and pre-image-decoder dispatch.
dedup-0015: Same WMF declared-record extent versus full-buffer variable payload reads and short cursor advance. Mandatory shared record-local slices plus fixed/count/text/point checks and aggregate budgets subsume all text and polygon/polyline/polypolygon variants. Preserve eight-byte TEXTOUT count65535 with sufficient trailing bytes, coordinates and nonblank retained text; whole-file memory safety is not disputed.
dedup-0017: Same WMF dispatch record-extent omission, full-file EXTTEXTOUT/TEXTOUT readers and independent retained Strings. Mandatory record-limited slices plus field/count validation cover text and previously retained geometry cases; retain all distinct record-size constructions.

previousFindings.title: WMF record-boundary failures amplify polygon work and retained text
previousFindings.summary: Rendering a DOCX with a crafted placeable WMF lets short declared records consume payload from later records, which the outer parser then revisits. Polygon/polypolygon/polyline records can cause billions of coordinate decodes from roughly 512 KiB; EXTTEXTOUT/TEXTOUT records can retain hundreds of megabytes of overlapping owned strings from roughly 205.6 KB. The common missing record-local boundary bypasses the canvas cap and original package budgets. A further framing uses alternating six-byte EXTTEXTOUT and unknown 0xFFFF record headers to claim 65,535 text bytes from subsequent records, implying several GiB of retained strings from roughly 1 MiB of media; this is a static estimate. A supplied 7-word EXTTEXTOUT framing uses 65536 fourteen-byte records plus a 65535-byte suffix in less than 1 MiB and requests about 4 GiB of decoded characters; nonzero mapping dimensions and nonblank text are required. This is a static estimate.

severity.rationale: Default document rendering can amplify a small embedded WMF into excessive coordinate/raster work or large retained text allocations, affecting host-process or WASM availability. Shared-host blast radius depends on caller process isolation; no memory-unsafe out-of-bounds read, disclosure or code execution is established.
severity.changeConditions: Mandatory record-local parsing and validated counts across all WMF handlers remove the overlapping-payload amplification; cumulative work/text budgets and isolated workers constrain resource effects.

confidence.rationale: Independent worker and parent verified the concrete input-to-sink control failure statically; exact runtime resource/failure thresholds were not measured.

rootCause.summary:
raster_wmf checks declared size*2 against remaining file bytes but keeps passing the entire data slice to its handlers, then advances only by the declared record size. Polygon, polypolygon and polyline counts therefore cause coordinate reads/allocation/raster work across later records. Independently, META_EXTTEXTOUT/META_TEXTOUT counts slice later bytes as text; wmf_text decodes owned Strings retained in texts and ultimately ImageKind::Metafile. Both subcases repeatedly consume overlapping suffixes because consumed payload extent is not tied to outer advancement. EMF's analogous point helper checks off+size. A mandatory record-limited slice plus record-local field/count checks at this shared WMF dispatch boundary fixes all absorbed handlers; geometry-only count patches leave text retention reachable.
With size=3 the outer cursor advances six bytes. EXTTEXTOUT's count at payload+4 can come from the next unknown-0xFFFF header; options may select a later optional-rectangle string offset. Subsequent header bytes repeatedly supply large whole-file text spans. Both drawing and VML image relationships reach this decoder before the general image crate's default 512 MiB allocation limit, which therefore cannot bound this earlier retention. The supplied alternating-header proof gives options=3, selecting the optional-rectangle branch and a string start at payload+16.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): WMF variable-length record data is read against the whole input rather than the record's declared slice; declared record progression permits overlapping unbounded amplification. A seven-word EXTTEXTOUT record contains its six-byte header and eight-byte fixed fields but can start its 65535-byte text range at the next record, because only whole-file bounds are checked.
Assigned discovery-0016 adds a same-function-header proof: repeated six-byte size=3/0x0A32 headers cause count at off+10 to read the next function (2610), options at off+12 to read size (3), and optional-rectangle text to start at off+22. Nonzero mapping extents, nonblank bytes and sufficient trailing data retain overlapping Strings; roughly 6 MB of records request about 2.6 GB of strings. These are source-derived estimates.

previousFindings.remediation: Confine every WMF handler, including field, font, string and geometry reads, to a slice limited to its checked declared record extent. Before allocation validate fixed fields, ring/point counts and coordinate arrays, EXTTEXTOUT options/optional rectangle and text count, and TEXTOUT padded string plus trailing coordinates against that slice using checked arithmetic. Refuse inconsistent records before decoding/rasterization/replay and enforce cumulative decoded-text, record and total geometry/work budgets. Keep the already bounded EMF behavior.

validation.summary:
Parent independently read raster_wmf dispatch/record checks and all three polygon handlers, their file-wide reads and outer offset increment. Repeated eight-byte polygon records with point-count 65535 can repeatedly consume later record bytes as coordinate payload; a 512KiB file supports more than two billion decodes before a late truncation refusal. This is bounded by whole-file bytes rather than record bytes; no memory out-of-bounds access is claimed.
Verified that text counts are u16, checked against the entire buffer, and do not need to fit the declared record. A 14-byte EXTTEXTOUT record can claim 65,535 text bytes beyond its own end. Ten thousand such records with enough trailing bytes imply 655,350,000 source bytes decoded into retained Strings from about 205.6 KB of WMF; UTF-8 conversion and later text handling can add cost.
Additional static proof: a placeable WMF with nonzero mapping bounds and fourteen-byte EXTTEXTOUT records (y/x/count/options, options zero, n=65535, no record-local text) reads following records into retained strings. Tens of thousands of such records in roughly 1 MB imply several GB of overlapping decoded text. This is an estimate from the supplied source, not executed memory measurement; ordinary bounds, nonblank content and sufficient trailing data are prerequisites.
Assigned discovery-0010 Standard corroboration (source validation, not reducer verification): Parent confirmed size3 advances6 bytes, EXTTEXTOUT reads count at payload+4, string at payload+8/16 and checks only data.get(at..at+n). Alternating six-byte EXTTEXTOUT/unknown0xFFFF headers supply count65535 from the next header while allowing repeated advancement. ansi_text collects owned strings retained in texts. TEXTOUT shares the record-local bounds omission.
Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): Verified the record cursor at metafile.rs:684 advances by size2 while handlers at 603-620 read against data. Approximately 65536 14-byte records plus 65535 trailing bytes fit in ~1 MiB yet retain at least ~4 GiB of text. WMF detection checks the placeable magic; bounded canvas dimensions do not bound text. Package admission permits such small binary media.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Parent inspected WMF dispatch, header/canvas setup, complete record loop (445-687), ansi_text (430-442) and wmf_text retention (692-716). Repeated eight-byte TEXTOUT records (4 words) can each declare 65535 bytes, with coordinates and tail inside the overall file and an EOF before unused tail; nonzero extents and nonblank bytes satisfy retention. EXTTEXTOUT and all three point-array opcodes share the boundary failure.
Additional assigned static framing: roughly 100000 eight-byte TEXTOUT records each claiming 65535 bytes plus sufficient trailing bytes (EOF before unused tail) fit in roughly 1 MiB and imply several GiB of overlapping retained strings. Nonzero mapping extents and nonblank decoded text are required. Matching short POLYGON/POLYLINE counts imply billions of point iterations. No payload or measurement was executed.
Assigned discovery-0017 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): An 8-byte TEXTOUT record can specify count65535 while declaring size4 words. extensions.semanticReductionNotes:
The supplied static proof framing uses repeated eight-byte WMF polygon records with count 65535. In a roughly 512 KiB file, the first roughly 32768 records can each decode following-record bytes as 65535 points, exceeding two billion decodes plus polygon scans before late truncation refusal. META_POLYGON, META_POLYPOLYGON and META_POLYLINE all need record-local bounds; the 384-pixel canvas cap, whole-file safe reads and bounded EMF helper do not enforce those WMF record bounds.
dedup-0003 merges the same shared WMF record-slice violation, rather than a mere media/sink family match. Preserve both proof tuples and all five handlers: eight-byte polygon records with count 65535 in ~512 KiB yield >2 billion point decodes; 10000 fourteen-byte EXTTEXTOUT records claiming 65535 bytes with sufficient nonblank following data yield 655350000 source bytes decoded into retained Strings from ~205.6 KB. Text records need nonblank decoded content and valid ordinary mapping to retain MetaText; EXTTEXTOUT rectangle/options and TEXTOUT padding/coordinate layouts require record-local checks. The text source independently validates its text consequences, while previous validated evidence establishes geometry consequences. Actual failure thresholds remain unmeasured. The common remediation limits the slice at dispatch for every handler; fixing only polygon handlers would not subsume the text source. MAX_SIDE=384, object-count clamps and safe whole-file reads remain useful but do not limit these repeated payloads.
dedup-0005: Same raster_wmf record extent versus whole-file handler access. Mandatory checked record slices across all field/string/font/geometry handlers subsume the assigned text and geometry report; a geometry-only patch would not. This supplements, rather than replaces, the prior 10,000-record/~205.6 KB text and ~512 KiB polygon proofs. dedup-0008: The same WMF dispatch-wide missing record-local boundary; the retained mandatory record slice and field/count checks subsume the six-byte size=3 alternating EXTTEXTOUT/unknown-0xFFFF framing, including VML image callers. findings.title: Aliased legacy DOC pieces expand small physical text into enormous logical stories
findings.summary: Thousands of contiguous logical pieces can all reference the same physical text range. For example, 4095 pieces referencing one common 1 MiB compressed-text range describe nearly 4 GiB of logical characters while requiring only roughly 49 KiB of piece records. main_text materializes metadata for every character, requiring tens of GiB before rendering. A second source-derived framing uses approximately 65,535 pieces reusing 64 KiB, producing over four billion logical characters from a piece table below 1 MiB; expansion precedes later auxiliary-table checks. The assigned 1024-by-65536 framing yields 67108864 logical characters and at least 768 MiB for char/CP/FC fields alone, before modifiers and allocation/output overhead; these are static counts, not measurements. Supplied discovery-0023 additionally gives 4096 contiguous one-million-character pieces sharing a 1 MB physical range (4096000000 logical characters within u32). Public read/conversion and native read_document refusal-hint parsing reach the same expansion before returning a format diagnostic; no runtime resource measurement is claimed.

severity.rationale: An untrusted document supplier can directly induce disproportionate resource use or bypass a resource admission control during normal parsing. Impact is availability of the processing worker/embedding process; no public deployment is assumed.
severity.changeConditions: Enforcing logical-work/selected-directory bounds removes the path; process isolation limits shared-service consequences.

confidence.rationale: Independent investigator and parent traced actual local source and effective controls. Resource counts are statically derived; no runtime reproduction or deployment is asserted.

rootCause.summary:
FIB ccp_text and per-piece CP endpoints are caller-controlled u32 values. pieces assigns each piece an independent physical offset, so many consecutive logical ranges can alias one physical text range. main_text verifies logical continuity and physical read bounds but then pushes one StoryChar per logical CP without a logical/output budget. Physical OLE bounds therefore do not limit retained logical metadata.
The decoder validates logical coverage and physical bounds independently but never limits cumulative decoded characters or charges repeated physical aliases for their full logical expansion. Contiguous increasing CPs may share FC backing; the rejected decreasing/repeated-logical-range variant is unnecessary. Piece count and total decoded work also need explicit accounting.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): `read` accepts the FIB main-story count and piece table, then passes them directly to `main_text`. Piece parsing permits each CP range to select the same physical fc range. The coverage check ensures contiguous increasing logical CPs but does not constrain their total decoded length relative to bytes or a resource limit. The per-character loop rereads the shared physical bytes and pushes a new StoryChar for every logical CP.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `read()` takes a FIB logical length and piece table. `main_text()` checks monotonically covering CP ranges and valid physical reads, but accepts repeated physical FC ranges. It emits all logical characters with no aggregate output budget.
Assigned discovery-0016 gives 1024 one-MiB logical pieces sharing one physical range: 1073741824 logical characters within u32 CP limits, at least 12 GiB for char/CP/FC fields alone before modifiers and allocator capacity. This is a static allocation request, not measured allocation.
Assigned discovery-0023 corroboration: `read` accepts `ccp_text` from the FIB and the piece table's logical CP boundaries and physical offsets. `main_text` establishes logical coverage but never relates total logical length to an output budget. For each piece it recomputes physical offsets relative to that piece, permitting repeated reads from the same valid bytes, and appends records for every logical CP. 4096 pieces of 1,000,000 compressed characters can reuse a 1 MB physical range while declaring 4,096,000,000 logical characters, within u32. Physical file/sector limits therefore do not bound the expanded story.
Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Physical stream bounds are mistaken for decoded-resource bounds; independent piece offsets can reuse source data while contiguous logical CPs drive unbounded StoryChar materialization.

findings.remediation: Introduce configurable legacy physical-input, piece-count, cumulative logical-character, retained-metadata and expansion-work budgets. Check FIB ccp_text and checked cumulative piece lengths before materialization, charge every decoded character including repeated physical aliases, and return typed refusals through read/doc_to_markdown/doc_to_docx and CLI callers. Preserve legitimate fast-save aliases and split UTF-16 surrogate handling within budget. Replace full legacy parsing used only for diagnostic refusal hints with a cheap bounded probe, or apply the same logical/work budgets before that parser runs.

validation.summary:
Parent verified ccp_text parsing, independent piece physical-offset decoding, monotonic/coverage checks and per-CP StoryChar append. 4095 contiguous pieces can reuse a single 1MiB compressed-text range to describe almost 4GiB of logical characters within u32 range, with roughly49KiB of piece records. All physical accesses remain valid while retained metadata grows to tens of GiB.
Parent verified Fib's u32 ccp_text, piece CP/fc parsing, continuity checks, per-character checked offsets and append. Aliases with successive contiguous CPs and a constant in-range fc satisfy both checks while multiplying work. The public read path has no InputLimits admission before main_text.
Additional static proof: 10,000 compressed pieces with consecutive 65,536-character logical CP ranges can share one 64 KiB physical range. ccp_text=655360000 is within u32 and roughly 120 KB of piece records imply 655,360,000 retained StoryChar values. Decreasing/gapped/repeated logical ranges are rejected and are unnecessary; increasing contiguous CP aliases satisfy those controls.
Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): Verified that 4095 consecutive compressed pieces of 1 MiB each, sharing a valid 1 MiB physical range and a matching u32 ccp_text, pass monotonic coverage and physical bounds. The loop attempts about 4.29 billion StoryChar records (at least tens of GiB), before package admission.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Physical stream bounds, checked offset arithmetic and CFB chain limits prevent out-of-bounds reads and chain cycles, but do not limit logical text expansion. For example, 65,535 pieces each reusing a 64KiB compressed-text range describe about 4.29 billion decoded characters with under 1MiB of piece records. Every selected byte remains in bounds; the vector grows far beyond the input size. CLI legacy conversion routes OLE directly to doc_to_docx before DOCX admission.
Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed consecutive pieces may reuse one valid FC range without violating coverage or byte-access checks. Their summed CP lengths may approach the u32 logical ceiling, so physical stream bounds do not prevent billions of logical records. Native legacy conversion directly enters this API.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Verified separate CP/FC parsing, coverage check, unsigned FIB length, bounded CFB traversal, and output loop. 65,535 descriptors each mapping a valid 65,536-byte range can cover 4,294,901,760 logical characters with a piece table under 1 MiB; no memory allocation was attempted. Physical-byte validity does not cap logical expansion.
Assigned discovery-0023 corroboration: Verified FIB count and independent per-piece offsets reach `main_text` before downstream validation. Contiguous, increasing CPs and repeated valid fc offsets satisfy the visible guards while the nested loops grow `out`. Native CLI converts legacy bytes before ordinary DOCX admission. Also validated the shared `read_document` refusal-hint branch: it calls legacy_doc::read on refused input to decide whether to suggest conversion, extending the same exposure beyond convert.
Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Parent verified PCD parsing accepts independent fc values and main_text validates CP coverage rather than physical-range uniqueness or a logical output budget. Reusing a valid physical range across many contiguous pieces keeps all per-byte get checks valid while multiplying decoded allocation. Public conversions and the native CLI refusal hint call the same reader.

finding.title: Reading a small legacy DOC can expand repeated text pieces into billions of characters
finding.summary: A legacy DOC author can reuse the same physical WordDocument text range in many contiguous logical pieces. `main_text` expands every logical character into `StoryChar` without a decoded-character budget, exhausting host memory or CPU.

severity.rationale: Attacker-controlled parser input can deny availability through disproportionate work or allocation in default public paths. Impact is process availability with high likelihood for a crafted input; no remote exposure, confidentiality loss or code execution is assumed.
severity.changeConditions: A disposable process with strict CPU/memory budgets reduces application-level impact; shared long-lived processing increases it.

confidence.rationale: Independent static source trace confirms the input-to-sink control gap and strongest counterevidence; no application or exploit execution was performed.

codeEvidence.label: Physical offsets and logical ranges
codeEvidence.explanation: Attacker CP endpoints and fc offsets become pieces; separate pieces may retain the same physical offset.

codeEvidence.label: Coverage without expansion budget
codeEvidence.explanation: Increasing contiguous logical ranges pass without constraining their total decoded length.

codeEvidence.label: Expand every logical character
codeEvidence.explanation: Each logical CP derives an in-bounds physical offset and is decoded even when earlier pieces already referenced those bytes.

codeEvidence.label: Retain expanded characters

rootCause.summary: `read` accepts the FIB main-story count and piece table, then passes them directly to `main_text`. Piece parsing permits each CP range to select the same physical fc range. The coverage check ensures contiguous increasing logical CPs but does not constrain their total decoded length relative to bytes or a resource limit. The per-character loop rereads the shared physical bytes and pushes a new StoryChar for every logical CP.

finding.remediation: Apply a configurable maximum decoded-character/output-byte budget before expansion and during emission; refuse excessive logical story length even when repeated physical ranges are individually valid.

counterEvidence: CFB sector-chain iteration is bounded by file size and invalid CP coverage is rejected.
No deployment exposure or measured allocation size is assumed; the exact StoryChar layout is platform dependent.
limitations: Static-only validation; no runtime measurement or deployed embedding assessment.
validation.summary: Physical stream bounds, checked offset arithmetic and CFB chain limits prevent out-of-bounds reads and chain cycles, but do not limit logical text expansion. For example, 65,535 pieces each reusing a 64KiB compressed-text range describe about 4.29 billion decoded characters with under 1MiB of piece records. Every selected byte remains in bounds; the vector grows far beyond the input size. CLI legacy conversion routes OLE directly to doc_to_docx before DOCX admission.

rootCause.summary: Piece-table descriptors store logical CP intervals independently from physical FC offsets. `main_text` verifies monotonic contiguous CP coverage and each physical read, but no aggregate logical-size bound. Multiple pieces can therefore reference the same physical bytes while extending CP coverage. The importer loops over the sum of logical lengths and appends a StoryChar per decoded character, before any downstream DOCX admission.

finding.remediation: Pass explicit input, logical-character, allocation and work budgets through legacy import. Preflight the total logical story length before iteration and charge repeated physical-span use against the same budget, returning a recoverable typed refusal.

validation.summary: Confirmed consecutive pieces may reuse one valid FC range without violating coverage or byte-access checks. finding.title: Legacy DOC piece tables amplify reused physical text into enormous logical stories
finding.summary: Legacy DOC parsing checks logical piece continuity and each physical read, but does not cap the total decoded story. Multiple contiguous logical pieces can reuse the same physical WordDocument text range, causing a small OLE file to materialize a much larger StoryChar vector. The native CLI also fully parses legacy input to produce a rejection hint before ordinary DOCX admission.

severity.rationale: A document supplier can exhaust the processing host's memory with a physically small file. Public library and local CLI processing suffice; a shared service is not assumed.
severity.changeConditions: A decoded-character budget applied before expansion removes the amplification; per-request process limits constrain availability impact.

confidence.rationale: Parent verified independent piece offsets, logical continuity checks, per-character push loop, public legacy entrypoints and native CLI conversion/refusal-hint paths. No runtime reproduction was performed.

codeEvidence.explanation: Checks reject backwards/gapped logical CP ranges, but do not limit ccp_text or cumulative decoded allocation relative to physical bytes.

codeEvidence.label: Each logical CP materializes an owned StoryChar
codeEvidence.explanation: A new physical address is calculated relative to each piece's independent fc; reused source bytes are pushed again for every logical piece.

rootCause.summary: Physical stream bounds are mistaken for decoded-resource bounds; independent piece offsets can reuse source data while contiguous logical CPs drive unbounded StoryChar materialization.

finding.remediation: Add a configurable decoded-character/story-memory budget and validate ccp_text and checked cumulative piece lengths before expansion. Charge each decoded output regardless of physical byte reuse. Use a cheap bounded validity probe rather than full legacy parsing for diagnostic hints.

counterEvidence: OLE/FAT chains and physical byte accesses are bounded; the finding concerns logical expansion after those controls.
Decreasing/gapped CPs and physically invalid reads are refused.
Reusing pieces can be valid editing representation, so rejecting all overlap is not required; a decoded budget is the missing control.
limitations: No peak-memory measurement or malicious file execution.
Exact StoryChar memory layout varies by target; impact does not depend on a specific struct size.
validation.summary: Parent verified PCD parsing accepts independent fc values and main_text validates CP coverage rather than physical-range uniqueness or a logical output budget. Reusing a valid physical range across many contiguous pieces keeps all per-byte get checks valid while multiplying decoded allocation. Public conversions and the native CLI refusal hint call the same reader.

rootCause.summary:

Physical OLE bounds therefore do not limit retained logical metadata.
The decoder validates logical coverage and physical bounds independently but never limits cumulative decoded characters or charges repeated physical aliases for their full logical expansion. Contiguous increasing CPs may share FC backing; the rejected decreasing/repeated-logical-range variant is unnecessary. Piece count and total decoded work also need explicit accounting.

rootCause.summary:
FIB ccp_text and per-piece CP endpoints are caller-controlled u32 values. pieces assigns each piece an independent physical offset, so many consecutive logical ranges can alias one physical text range. main_text verifies logical continuity and physical read bounds but then pushes one StoryChar per logical CP without a logical/output budget. Physical OLE bounds therefore do not limit retained logical metadata.
The decoder validates logical coverage and physical bounds independently but never limits cumulative decoded characters or charges repeated physical aliases for their full logical expansion. Contiguous increasing CPs may share FC backing; the rejected decreasing/repeated-logical-range variant is unnecessary. Piece count and total decoded work also need explicit accounting.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): `read` accepts the FIB main-story count and piece table, then passes them directly to `main_text`. Piece parsing permits each CP range to select the same physical fc range. The coverage check ensures contiguous increasing logical CPs but does not constrain their total decoded length relative to bytes or a resource limit. The per-character loop rereads the shared physical bytes and pushes a new StoryChar for every logical CP.

previousFindings.remediation: Introduce configurable legacy physical-input, piece-count, cumulative logical-character, retained-metadata and expansion-work budgets. Check FIB ccp_text and checked cumulative piece lengths before materialization, charge every decoded character including repeated physical aliases, and return typed refusals through read/doc_to_markdown/doc_to_docx and CLI callers. Preserve legitimate fast-save aliases and split UTF-16 surrogate handling within budget.

counterEvidence: Checked arithmetic and word.get/u16_at refuse physical offsets outside WordDocument. Increasing CP validation prevents backwards logical pieces. Neither control bounds repeated physical-range references or total logical expansion. Public legacy APIs have no InputLimits parameter, and CLI parsing happens before resulting DOCX admission.
Compound-file parsing and character addressing use bounds/overflow checks.
main_text rejects decreasing logical CPs, gaps and physical out-of-bounds reads; the repeated in-range aliases satisfy these checks.
No malformed auxiliary table is needed because expansion runs first.
Sector chains are bounded and repeated FAT locations rejected; integer arithmetic and physical byte reads are checked.
Decreasing CPs and gaps are refused, so the rejected repeated 0..N logical-range proposal is not needed. This construction uses increasing contiguous CPs.
The repository recommends host process limits, which constrain damage but do not provide a bounded parser refusal.
Compound-file sector walks and numeric offsets use checked/bounded arithmetic; these bound physical reads, not logical reuse.
Main-story CP coverage must be continuous and increasing; the described pieces satisfy that condition.
Process memory/CPU limits are recommended by SECURITY.md and can contain the host impact.
CFB sector-chain iteration is bounded by file size and invalid CP coverage is rejected.
No deployment exposure or measured allocation size is assumed; the exact StoryChar layout is platform dependent.

validation.summary:
Parent verified ccp_text parsing, independent piece physical-offset decoding, monotonic/coverage checks and per-CP StoryChar append. 4095 contiguous pieces can reuse a single 1MiB compressed-text range to describe almost 4GiB of logical characters within u32 range, with roughly49KiB of piece records. All physical accesses remain valid while retained metadata grows to tens of GiB.
Parent verified Fib's u32 ccp_text, piece CP/fc parsing, continuity checks, per-character checked offsets and append. Aliases with successive contiguous CPs and a constant in-range fc satisfy both checks while multiplying work. The public read path has no InputLimits admission before main_text.
Additional static proof: 10,000 compressed pieces with consecutive 65,536-character logical CP ranges can share one 64 KiB physical range. ccp_text=655360000 is within u32 and roughly 120 KB of piece records imply 655,360,000 retained StoryChar values. Decreasing/gapped/repeated logical ranges are rejected and are unnecessary; increasing contiguous CP aliases satisfy those controls.
Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): Verified that 4095 consecutive compressed pieces of 1 MiB each, sharing a valid 1 MiB physical range and a matching u32 ccp_text, pass monotonic coverage and physical bounds. The loop attempts about 4.29 billion StoryChar records (at least tens of GiB), before package admission.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Physical stream bounds, checked offset arithmetic and CFB chain limits prevent out-of-bounds reads and chain cycles, but do not limit logical text expansion. For example, 65,535 pieces each reusing a 64KiB compressed-text range describe about 4.29 billion decoded characters with under 1MiB of piece records. Every selected byte remains in bounds; the vector grows far beyond the input size. CLI legacy conversion routes OLE directly to doc_to_docx before DOCX admission.

controls: Physical stream bounds remain enforced; they do not bound logical expansion.

rootCause.summary:
FIB ccp_text and per-piece CP endpoints are caller-controlled u32 values. pieces assigns each piece an independent physical offset, so many consecutive logical ranges can alias one physical text range. main_text verifies logical continuity and physical read bounds but then pushes one StoryChar per logical CP without a logical/output budget. Physical OLE bounds therefore do not limit retained logical metadata.
The decoder validates logical coverage and physical bounds independently but never limits cumulative decoded characters or charges repeated physical aliases for their full logical expansion. Contiguous increasing CPs may share FC backing; the rejected decreasing/repeated-logical-range variant is unnecessary. Piece count and total decoded work also need explicit accounting.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): `read` accepts the FIB main-story count and piece table, then passes them directly to `main_text`. Piece parsing permits each CP range to select the same physical fc range. The coverage check ensures contiguous increasing logical CPs but does not constrain their total decoded length relative to bytes or a resource limit. The per-character loop rereads the shared physical bytes and pushes a new StoryChar for every logical CP.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `read()` takes a FIB logical length and piece table. `main_text()` checks monotonically covering CP ranges and valid physical reads, but accepts repeated physical FC ranges. It emits all logical characters with no aggregate output budget.

dataflow.summary: Fib::parse accepts ccp_text directly from the document. pieces accepts contiguous increasing CP ranges with independently controlled physical fc offsets. main_text verifies CP coverage and individual physical reads, then emits one StoryChar for each logical CP without a logical character/output budget. rootCause.summary:
FIB ccp_text and per-piece CP endpoints are caller-controlled u32 values. pieces assigns each piece an independent physical offset, so many consecutive logical ranges can alias one physical text range. main_text verifies logical continuity and physical read bounds but then pushes one StoryChar per logical CP without a logical/output budget. Physical OLE bounds therefore do not limit retained logical metadata.
The decoder validates logical coverage and physical bounds independently but never limits cumulative decoded characters or charges repeated physical aliases for their full logical expansion. Contiguous increasing CPs may share FC backing; the rejected decreasing/repeated-logical-range variant is unnecessary. Piece count and total decoded work also need explicit accounting.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): `read` accepts the FIB main-story count and piece table, then passes them directly to `main_text`. Piece parsing permits each CP range to select the same physical fc range. The coverage check ensures contiguous increasing logical CPs but does not constrain their total decoded length relative to bytes or a resource limit. The per-character loop rereads the shared physical bytes and pushes a new StoryChar for every logical CP.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `read()` takes a FIB logical length and piece table. `main_text()` checks monotonically covering CP ranges and valid physical reads, but accepts repeated physical FC ranges. It emits all logical characters with no aggregate output budget.
Assigned discovery-0016 gives 1024 one-MiB logical pieces sharing one physical range: 1073741824 logical characters within u32 CP limits, at least 12 GiB for char/CP/FC fields alone before modifiers and allocator capacity. This is a static allocation request, not measured allocation.

previousFindings.remediation: Introduce configurable legacy physical-input, piece-count, cumulative logical-character, retained-metadata and expansion-work budgets. Check FIB ccp_text and checked cumulative piece lengths before materialization, charge every decoded character including repeated physical aliases, and return typed refusals through read/doc_to_markdown/doc_to_docx and CLI callers. Preserve legitimate fast-save aliases and split UTF-16 surrogate handling within budget.

validation.summary:
Parent verified ccp_text parsing, independent piece physical-offset decoding, monotonic/coverage checks and per-CP StoryChar append. 4095 contiguous pieces can reuse a single 1MiB compressed-text range to describe almost 4GiB of logical characters within u32 range, with roughly49KiB of piece records. All physical accesses remain valid while retained metadata grows to tens of GiB.
Parent verified Fib's u32 ccp_text, piece CP/fc parsing, continuity checks, per-character checked offsets and append. Aliases with successive contiguous CPs and a constant in-range fc satisfy both checks while multiplying work. The public read path has no InputLimits admission before main_text.
Additional static proof: 10,000 compressed pieces with consecutive 65,536-character logical CP ranges can share one 64 KiB physical range. ccp_text=655360000 is within u32 and roughly 120 KB of piece records imply 655,360,000 retained StoryChar values. Decreasing/gapped/repeated logical ranges are rejected and are unnecessary; increasing contiguous CP aliases satisfy those controls.
Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): Verified that 4095 consecutive compressed pieces of 1 MiB each, sharing a valid 1 MiB physical range and a matching u32 ccp_text, pass monotonic coverage and physical bounds. The loop attempts about 4.29 billion StoryChar records (at least tens of GiB), before package admission.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Physical stream bounds, checked offset arithmetic and CFB chain limits prevent out-of-bounds reads and chain cycles, but do not limit logical text expansion. For example, 65,535 pieces each reusing a 64KiB compressed-text range describe about 4.29 billion decoded characters with under 1MiB of piece records. Every selected byte remains in bounds; the vector grows far beyond the input size. CLI legacy conversion routes OLE directly to doc_to_docx before DOCX admission.
Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed consecutive pieces may reuse one valid FC range without violating coverage or byte-access checks. Their summed CP lengths may approach the u32 logical ceiling, so physical stream bounds do not prevent billions of logical records. Native legacy conversion directly enters this API.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Verified separate CP/FC parsing, coverage check, unsigned FIB length, bounded CFB traversal, and output loop. 65,535 descriptors each mapping a valid 65,536-byte range can cover 4,294,901,760 logical characters with a piece table under 1 MiB; no memory allocation was attempted. Physical-byte validity does not cap logical expansion.

previousFindings.title: Aliased legacy DOC pieces expand small physical text into enormous logical stories
previousFindings.summary: Thousands of contiguous logical pieces can all reference the same physical text range. For example, 4095 pieces referencing one common 1 MiB compressed-text range describe nearly 4 GiB of logical characters while requiring only roughly 49 KiB of piece records. main_text materializes metadata for every character, requiring tens of GiB before rendering. A second source-derived framing uses approximately 65,535 pieces reusing 64 KiB, producing over four billion logical characters from a piece table below 1 MiB; expansion precedes later auxiliary-table checks. The assigned 1024-by-65536 framing yields 67108864 logical characters and at least 768 MiB for char/CP/FC fields alone, before modifiers and allocation/output overhead; these are static counts, not measurements.

severity.changeConditions: Enforcing logical-work/selected-directory bounds removes the path; process isolation limits shared-service consequences.

rootCause.summary:
FIB ccp_text and per-piece CP endpoints are caller-controlled u32 values. pieces assigns each piece an independent physical offset, so many consecutive logical ranges can alias one physical text range. main_text verifies logical continuity and physical read bounds but then pushes one StoryChar per logical CP without a logical/output budget. Physical OLE bounds therefore do not limit retained logical metadata.
The decoder validates logical coverage and physical bounds independently but never limits cumulative decoded characters or charges repeated physical aliases for their full logical expansion. Contiguous increasing CPs may share FC backing; the rejected decreasing/repeated-logical-range variant is unnecessary. Piece count and total decoded work also need explicit accounting.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): `read` accepts the FIB main-story count and piece table, then passes them directly to `main_text`. Piece parsing permits each CP range to select the same physical fc range. The coverage check ensures contiguous increasing logical CPs but does not constrain their total decoded length relative to bytes or a resource limit. The per-character loop rereads the shared physical bytes and pushes a new StoryChar for every logical CP.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `read()` takes a FIB logical length and piece table. `main_text()` checks monotonically covering CP ranges and valid physical reads, but accepts repeated physical FC ranges. It emits all logical characters with no aggregate output budget.
Assigned discovery-0016 gives 1024 one-MiB logical pieces sharing one physical range: 1073741824 logical characters within u32 CP limits, at least 12 GiB for char/CP/FC fields alone before modifiers and allocator capacity. This is a static allocation request, not measured allocation.

previousFindings.remediation: Introduce configurable legacy physical-input, piece-count, cumulative logical-character, retained-metadata and expansion-work budgets. Check FIB ccp_text and checked cumulative piece lengths before materialization, charge every decoded character including repeated physical aliases, and return typed refusals through read/doc_to_markdown/doc_to_docx and CLI callers. Preserve legitimate fast-save aliases and split UTF-16 surrogate handling within budget.

counterEvidence: Checked arithmetic and word.get/u16_at refuse physical offsets outside WordDocument. Increasing CP validation prevents backwards logical pieces. Neither control bounds repeated physical-range references or total logical expansion. Public legacy APIs have no InputLimits parameter, and CLI parsing happens before resulting DOCX admission.

validation.summary:
Parent verified ccp_text parsing, independent piece physical-offset decoding, monotonic/coverage checks and per-CP StoryChar append. 4095 contiguous pieces can reuse a single 1MiB compressed-text range to describe almost 4GiB of logical characters within u32 range, with roughly49KiB of piece records. rootCause.summary:
FIB ccp_text and per-piece CP endpoints are caller-controlled u32 values. pieces assigns each piece an independent physical offset, so many consecutive logical ranges can alias one physical text range. main_text verifies logical continuity and physical read bounds but then pushes one StoryChar per logical CP without a logical/output budget. Physical OLE bounds therefore do not limit retained logical metadata.
The decoder validates logical coverage and physical bounds independently but never limits cumulative decoded characters or charges repeated physical aliases for their full logical expansion. Contiguous increasing CPs may share FC backing; the rejected decreasing/repeated-logical-range variant is unnecessary. Piece count and total decoded work also need explicit accounting.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): `read` accepts the FIB main-story count and piece table, then passes them directly to `main_text`. Piece parsing permits each CP range to select the same physical fc range. The coverage check ensures contiguous increasing logical CPs but does not constrain their total decoded length relative to bytes or a resource limit. The per-character loop rereads the shared physical bytes and pushes a new StoryChar for every logical CP.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `read()` takes a FIB logical length and piece table. `main_text()` checks monotonically covering CP ranges and valid physical reads, but accepts repeated physical FC ranges. It emits all logical characters with no aggregate output budget.
Assigned discovery-0016 gives 1024 one-MiB logical pieces sharing one physical range: 1073741824 logical characters within u32 CP limits, at least 12 GiB for char/CP/FC fields alone before modifiers and allocator capacity. This is a static allocation request, not measured allocation.
Assigned discovery-0023 corroboration: `read` accepts `ccp_text` from the FIB and the piece table's logical CP boundaries and physical offsets. `main_text` establishes logical coverage but never relates total logical length to an output budget. For each piece it recomputes physical offsets relative to that piece, permitting repeated reads from the same valid bytes, and appends records for every logical CP. 4096 pieces of 1,000,000 compressed characters can reuse a 1 MB physical range while declaring 4,096,000,000 logical characters, within u32. Physical file/sector limits therefore do not bound the expanded story.
Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Physical stream bounds are mistaken for decoded-resource bounds; independent piece offsets can reuse source data while contiguous logical CPs drive unbounded StoryChar materialization.

previousFindings.remediation: Introduce configurable legacy physical-input, piece-count, cumulative logical-character, retained-metadata and expansion-work budgets. Check FIB ccp_text and checked cumulative piece lengths before materialization, charge every decoded character including repeated physical aliases, and return typed refusals through read/doc_to_markdown/doc_to_docx and CLI callers. Preserve legitimate fast-save aliases and split UTF-16 surrogate handling within budget. Replace full legacy parsing used only for diagnostic refusal hints with a cheap bounded probe, or apply the same logical/work budgets before that parser runs.

validation.summary:
Parent verified ccp_text parsing, independent piece physical-offset decoding, monotonic/coverage checks and per-CP StoryChar append. 4095 contiguous pieces can reuse a single 1MiB compressed-text range to describe almost 4GiB of logical characters within u32 range, with roughly49KiB of piece records. All physical accesses remain valid while retained metadata grows to tens of GiB.
Parent verified Fib's u32 ccp_text, piece CP/fc parsing, continuity checks, per-character checked offsets and append. Aliases with successive contiguous CPs and a constant in-range fc satisfy both checks while multiplying work. The public read path has no InputLimits admission before main_text.
Additional static proof: 10,000 compressed pieces with consecutive 65,536-character logical CP ranges can share one 64 KiB physical range. ccp_text=655360000 is within u32 and roughly 120 KB of piece records imply 655,360,000 retained StoryChar values. Decreasing/gapped/repeated logical ranges are rejected and are unnecessary; increasing contiguous CP aliases satisfy those controls.
Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): Verified that 4095 consecutive compressed pieces of 1 MiB each, sharing a valid 1 MiB physical range and a matching u32 ccp_text, pass monotonic coverage and physical bounds. The loop attempts about 4.29 billion StoryChar records (at least tens of GiB), before package admission.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Physical stream bounds, checked offset arithmetic and CFB chain limits prevent out-of-bounds reads and chain cycles, but do not limit logical text expansion. For example, 65,535 pieces each reusing a 64KiB compressed-text range describe about 4.29 billion decoded characters with under 1MiB of piece records. Every selected byte remains in bounds; the vector grows far beyond the input size. CLI legacy conversion routes OLE directly to doc_to_docx before DOCX admission.
Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed consecutive pieces may reuse one valid FC range without violating coverage or byte-access checks. Their summed CP lengths may approach the u32 logical ceiling, so physical stream bounds do not prevent billions of logical records. Native legacy conversion directly enters this API.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Verified separate CP/FC parsing, coverage check, unsigned FIB length, bounded CFB traversal, and output loop. 65,535 descriptors each mapping a valid 65,536-byte range can cover 4,294,901,760 logical characters with a piece table under 1 MiB; no memory allocation was attempted. Physical-byte validity does not cap logical expansion.
Assigned discovery-0023 corroboration: Verified FIB count and independent per-piece offsets reach `main_text` before downstream validation. Contiguous, increasing CPs and repeated valid fc offsets satisfy the visible guards while the nested loops grow `out`. Native CLI converts legacy bytes before ordinary DOCX admission. Also validated the shared `read_document` refusal-hint branch: it calls legacy_doc::read on refused input to decide whether to suggest conversion, extending the same exposure beyond convert.
Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Parent verified PCD parsing accepts independent fc values and main_text validates CP coverage rather than physical-range uniqueness or a logical output budget. Reusing a valid physical range across many contiguous pieces keeps all per-byte get checks valid while multiplying decoded allocation. Public conversions and the native CLI refusal hint call the same reader.

rootCause.summary:
FIB ccp_text and per-piece CP endpoints are caller-controlled u32 values. pieces assigns each piece an independent physical offset, so many consecutive logical ranges can alias one physical text range. main_text verifies logical continuity and physical read bounds but then pushes one StoryChar per logical CP without a logical/output budget. Physical OLE bounds therefore do not limit retained logical metadata.
The decoder validates logical coverage and physical bounds independently but never limits cumulative decoded characters or charges repeated physical aliases for their full logical expansion. Contiguous increasing CPs may share FC backing; the rejected decreasing/repeated-logical-range variant is unnecessary. Piece count and total decoded work also need explicit accounting.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): `read` accepts the FIB main-story count and piece table, then passes them directly to `main_text`. Piece parsing permits each CP range to select the same physical fc range. The coverage check ensures contiguous increasing logical CPs but does not constrain their total decoded length relative to bytes or a resource limit. The per-character loop rereads the shared physical bytes and pushes a new StoryChar for every logical CP.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `read()` takes a FIB logical length and piece table. `main_text()` checks monotonically covering CP ranges and valid physical reads, but accepts repeated physical FC ranges. It emits all logical characters with no aggregate output budget.
Assigned discovery-0016 gives 1024 one-MiB logical pieces sharing one physical range: 1073741824 logical characters within u32 CP limits, at least 12 GiB for char/CP/FC fields alone before modifiers and allocator capacity. This is a static allocation request, not measured allocation.
Assigned discovery-0023 corroboration: `read` accepts `ccp_text` from the FIB and the piece table's logical CP boundaries and physical offsets. `main_text` establishes logical coverage but never relates total logical length to an output budget. For each piece it recomputes physical offsets relative to that piece, permitting repeated reads from the same valid bytes, and appends records for every logical CP. 4096 pieces of 1,000,000 compressed characters can reuse a 1 MB physical range while declaring 4,096,000,000 logical characters, within u32. Physical file/sector limits therefore do not bound the expanded story.
Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Physical stream bounds are mistaken for decoded-resource bounds; independent piece offsets can reuse source data while contiguous logical CPs drive unbounded StoryChar materialization.

previousFindings.remediation: Introduce configurable legacy physical-input, piece-count, cumulative logical-character, retained-metadata and expansion-work budgets. Check FIB ccp_text and checked cumulative piece lengths before materialization, charge every decoded character including repeated physical aliases, and return typed refusals through read/doc_to_markdown/doc_to_docx and CLI callers. Preserve legitimate fast-save aliases and split UTF-16 surrogate handling within budget. Replace full legacy parsing used only for diagnostic refusal hints with a cheap bounded probe, or apply the same logical/work budgets before that parser runs.

validation.summary:
Parent verified ccp_text parsing, independent piece physical-offset decoding, monotonic/coverage checks and per-CP StoryChar append. 4095 contiguous pieces can reuse a single 1MiB compressed-text range to describe almost 4GiB of logical characters within u32 range, with roughly49KiB of piece records. All physical accesses remain valid while retained metadata grows to tens of GiB.
Parent verified Fib's u32 ccp_text, piece CP/fc parsing, continuity checks, per-character checked offsets and append. Aliases with successive contiguous CPs and a constant in-range fc satisfy both checks while multiplying work. The public read path has no InputLimits admission before main_text.
Additional static proof: 10,000 compressed pieces with consecutive 65,536-character logical CP ranges can share one 64 KiB physical range. ccp_text=655360000 is within u32 and roughly 120 KB of piece records imply 655,360,000 retained StoryChar values. Decreasing/gapped/repeated logical ranges are rejected and are unnecessary; increasing contiguous CP aliases satisfy those controls.
Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): Verified that 4095 consecutive compressed pieces of 1 MiB each, sharing a valid 1 MiB physical range and a matching u32 ccp_text, pass monotonic coverage and physical bounds. The loop attempts about 4.29 billion StoryChar records (at least tens of GiB), before package admission.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Physical stream bounds, checked offset arithmetic and CFB chain limits prevent out-of-bounds reads and chain cycles, but do not limit logical text expansion. For example, 65,535 pieces each reusing a 64KiB compressed-text range describe about 4.29 billion decoded characters with under 1MiB of piece records. findings.title: ZIP footer and count interpretation mismatch bypasses entry-count admission
findings.summary: The independent preindex footer parser can count a different EOCD or count field from zip 9.0.5. False small-count EOCDs in valid comments can be skipped by zip; a same-footer total=3/on-this-disk=10001 also passes max_entries=10000 while zip indexes 10001. ZIP64 size/offset triggers differ too. Neither admission nor PartFs enforces the actual opened count; duplicate detection also trusts the unrelated declared count. Another supplied false-footer proof uses an EOCD-shaped record inside the real archive comment whose own comment length is impossible; preindex trusts its low count while the ZIP reader rejects it and backtracks.

severity.changeConditions: Enforcing logical-work/selected-directory bounds removes the path; process isolation limits shared-service consequences.

rootCause.summary:
preindex_budget derives max_entries from the last byte signature resembling an EOCD, without validating that candidate's disk/comment/directory fields. The ZIP reader uses validated candidate selection and retries earlier EOCDs when the last one fails. A false zero-count footer in the real comment therefore passes preindex while ZipArchive indexes the earlier real directory. Neither admit nor read_package caps the actual opened archive length, and the collapsed-duplicate comparison also uses the unrelated false count.
The assigned source supplies an alternative invalid-candidate framing: an offset at/past the false EOCD makes zip reject that candidate. Both framings use the same last-signature/validated-selection mismatch. A post-open length check bounds later processing but cannot undo metadata already allocated while indexing.
A separate, incomplete EOCD/ZIP64 parser is treated as authoritative for resource admission even though the delegated ZIP parser chooses its own footer/count semantics. Indexed entries are not reconciled to the active limit.
Assigned discovery-0016 additionally confirms the name-map shortfall inference can be concealed by a low total count: +8=20000/+10=1 causes preindex to see 1 while the reader indexes 20000, and actual<declared is false even after exact-name collapse. Direct raw-duplicate detection or the dependency duplicate indicator is required alongside authoritative preindex counts; case/decoded-name collision checks remain effective.
Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Resource admission and ZIP parsing do not share a validated end-record decision; a one-sided post-open comparison cannot enforce the upper bound against the reader's actual entry index.
Assigned discovery-0025 supplies a fake EOCD with total=0 and central-directory offset=0xFFFFFFFF inside the real comment: preflight accepts its low count, while the source reports zip9.0.5 rejects the impossible offset and retries the earlier real footer. This strengthens the existing candidate-selection proof without changing other count-field/ZIP64 variants.

findings.remediation: Use the delegated reader's authoritative validated EOCD/ZIP64 selection, consistent ZIP32 total/per-disk fields and all ZIP64 total/size/offset triggers. Bound raw central-record traversal/count before index allocation, reject inconsistent unsupported metadata, and retain a post-open active archive.len cap as defense in depth; that later check cannot undo earlier allocation. Reconcile selected raw counts with indexed counts for exact duplicates, including name collapse, comments, ZIP64 and prepended data. Detect raw exact-name duplicates directly or through the reader's duplicate flag rather than relying solely on a count-shortfall inference.

validation.summary:
Parent verified the local preindex parser, post-open checks and PartFs reader, plus locked zip9.0.5 EOCD retry loop and multi-disk mismatch rejection. A trailing false EOCD with zero count and inconsistent disk numbers is skipped by zip but trusted by preindex. The earlier actual directory can exceed max_entries while remaining inside compressed/inflated-byte and structural bounds. No constructed archive was executed.
The additional validated trace uses a small-count fake with an impossible directory offset. Locked zip 9.0.5 rejects offsets at/past the candidate EOCD and retries earlier candidates (format/find_central_directory.rs:100-116,163-166; read/zip_archive.rs:199-235), then reads/indexes that directory (:239-316). No local-header or CRC inconsistency is required. An over-count package need not crash in every embedding: actual resource effects depend on caller limits, metadata size and process isolation.
Parent inspected local zip9.0.5 src/read/mod.rs:53-74, which selects number_of_files_on_this_disk for ZIP32, and src/read/zip_archive.rs:271-299, which collects central records to that count. format/blocks.rs:379-383 selects ZIP64 on total/size/offset sentinels. previousFindings.summary: The independent preindex footer parser can count a different EOCD or count field from zip 9.0.5. False small-count EOCDs in valid comments can be skipped by zip; a same-footer total=3/on-this-disk=10001 also passes max_entries=10000 while zip indexes 10001. ZIP64 size/offset triggers differ too. Neither admission nor PartFs enforces the actual opened count; duplicate detection also trusts the unrelated declared count.

severity.rationale: An untrusted document supplier can directly induce disproportionate resource use or bypass a resource admission control during normal parsing. Impact is availability of the processing worker/embedding process; no public deployment is assumed.
severity.changeConditions: Enforcing logical-work/selected-directory bounds removes the path; process isolation limits shared-service consequences.

confidence.rationale: Independent investigator and parent traced actual local source and effective controls. Resource counts are statically derived; no runtime reproduction or deployment is asserted.

rootCause.summary:
preindex_budget derives max_entries from the last byte signature resembling an EOCD, without validating that candidate's disk/comment/directory fields. The ZIP reader uses validated candidate selection and retries earlier EOCDs when the last one fails. A false zero-count footer in the real comment therefore passes preindex while ZipArchive indexes the earlier real directory. Neither admit nor read_package caps the actual opened archive length, and the collapsed-duplicate comparison also uses the unrelated false count.
The assigned source supplies an alternative invalid-candidate framing: an offset at/past the false EOCD makes zip reject that candidate. Both framings use the same last-signature/validated-selection mismatch. A post-open length check bounds later processing but cannot undo metadata already allocated while indexing.
A separate, incomplete EOCD/ZIP64 parser is treated as authoritative for resource admission even though the delegated ZIP parser chooses its own footer/count semantics. Indexed entries are not reconciled to the active limit.

previousFindings.remediation: Use the delegated reader's authoritative validated EOCD/ZIP64 selection, consistent ZIP32 total/per-disk fields and all ZIP64 total/size/offset triggers. Bound raw central-record traversal/count before index allocation, reject inconsistent unsupported metadata, and retain a post-open active archive.len cap as defense in depth; that later check cannot undo earlier allocation. Reconcile selected raw counts with indexed counts for exact duplicates, including name collapse, comments, ZIP64 and prepended data.

counterEvidence: Compressed-byte and inflated-byte budgets remain effective; this is specifically an entry-count/selected-footer mismatch. ZIP local-header and extent validation runs against the actual opened archive and does not reconcile it with the preindex candidate. This conclusion is source-derived; no archive was constructed or executed.
Byte and inflated-data limits still apply; the bypass specifically concerns entry metadata/count and work.
The existing comparison detects collapsed duplicate names in the smaller-count direction.

A post-open check alone would stop processing but not restore pre-index allocation bounds.
