validation.summary:
Parent verified the local preindex parser, post-open checks and PartFs reader, plus locked zip9.0.5 EOCD retry loop and multi-disk mismatch rejection. A trailing false EOCD with zero count and inconsistent disk numbers is skipped by zip but trusted by preindex. The earlier actual directory can exceed max_entries while remaining inside compressed/inflated-byte and structural bounds. No constructed archive was executed.
The additional validated trace uses a small-count fake with an impossible directory offset. Locked zip 9.0.5 rejects offsets at/past the candidate EOCD and retries earlier candidates (format/find_central_directory.rs:100-116,163-166; read/zip_archive.rs:199-235), then reads/indexes that directory (:239-316). No local-header or CRC inconsistency is required. An over-count package need not crash in every embedding: actual resource effects depend on caller limits, metadata size and process isolation.
Parent inspected local zip9.0.5 src/read/mod.rs:53-74, which selects number_of_files_on_this_disk for ZIP32, and src/read/zip_archive.rs:271-299, which collects central records to that count. format/blocks.rs:379-383 selects ZIP64 on total/size/offset sentinels. Repository precheck instead reads+10 and returns early unless total==FFFF; neither admit nor read_package caps the actual index length. Baseline additionally established false-EOCD candidate selection differences.
Assigned discovery-0010 Standard corroboration (source validation, not reducer verification): Parent confirmed declared_entry_count selects bare last EOCD magic, zip9.0.5 continues past impossible directory offsets, and actual index counts are not bounded by max_entries after selection. A real well-formed directory with unique entries and consistent local headers is unaffected by the other checks.

dataflow.summary:
admit or PartFs::open_within -> preindex_budget -> declared_entry_count chooses the last signature -> open_archive_unchecked -> zip 9.0.5 rejects that candidate and retries an earlier real EOCD -> indexing and processing proceed without an actual-count maximum check.
A false candidate may be invalid through inconsistent disk fields or an impossible directory offset; ZIP legitimately skips either while preindex still trusts its small count.
Attacker EOCD/ZIP64 count/selection fields -> preindex parses smaller total and passes -> zip reader chooses per-disk/ZIP64 count -> central metadata index allocates/loops beyond active max_entries -> admit/PartFs process full indexed entries.
dataflow.source: Supplier-controlled archive comment and central-directory records
dataflow.sink: Archive indexing and per-entry package processing
dataflow.outcome: Entry-count resource budget is bypassed.

impact.why: A false EOCD carrying count zero and inconsistent disk fields can be placed inside the real EOCD comment. The preindex check accepts zero; zip rejects the false candidate and opens the real directory containing more than max_entries. This defeats the advertised entry-count budget and permits excess indexing, structural validation, and per-entry processing. The same mismatch also invalidates admission's declared-count comparison used to detect collapsed exact duplicates.
additionalSourceStatements: Bypass of configured entry limits with excess metadata allocation and CPU processing; compressed-byte budget still bounds physical input.

likelihood.why: The triggering structure and values are document-controlled and not rejected by existing guards.

limitations: Memory-safe reads remain bounded; no arbitrary code execution or confidentiality impact is established.

dedup-0002 merges the same preindex-versus-ZIP candidate-selection root issue. rootCause.summary:
preindex_budget derives max_entries from the last byte signature resembling an EOCD, without validating that candidate's disk/comment/directory fields. The ZIP reader uses validated candidate selection and retries earlier EOCDs when the last one fails. A false zero-count footer in the real comment therefore passes preindex while ZipArchive indexes the earlier real directory. Neither admit nor read_package caps the actual opened archive length, and the collapsed-duplicate comparison also uses the unrelated false count.
The assigned source supplies an alternative invalid-candidate framing: an offset at/past the false EOCD makes zip reject that candidate. Both framings use the same last-signature/validated-selection mismatch. A post-open length check bounds later processing but cannot undo metadata already allocated while indexing.
A separate, incomplete EOCD/ZIP64 parser is treated as authoritative for resource admission even though the delegated ZIP parser chooses its own footer/count semantics. Indexed entries are not reconciled to the active limit.

previousFindings.remediation: Use the delegated reader's authoritative validated EOCD/ZIP64 selection, consistent ZIP32 total/per-disk fields and all ZIP64 total/size/offset triggers. Bound raw central-record traversal/count before index allocation, reject inconsistent unsupported metadata, and retain a post-open active archive.len cap as defense in depth; that later check cannot undo earlier allocation. Reconcile selected raw counts with indexed counts for exact duplicates, including name collapse, comments, ZIP64 and prepended data.

rootCause.summary:
preindex_budget derives max_entries from the last byte signature resembling an EOCD, without validating that candidate's disk/comment/directory fields. The ZIP reader uses validated candidate selection and retries earlier EOCDs when the last one fails. A false zero-count footer in the real comment therefore passes preindex while ZipArchive indexes the earlier real directory. Neither admit nor read_package caps the actual opened archive length, and the collapsed-duplicate comparison also uses the unrelated false count.
The assigned source supplies an alternative invalid-candidate framing: an offset at/past the false EOCD makes zip reject that candidate. Both framings use the same last-signature/validated-selection mismatch. A post-open length check bounds later processing but cannot undo metadata already allocated while indexing.
A separate, incomplete EOCD/ZIP64 parser is treated as authoritative for resource admission even though the delegated ZIP parser chooses its own footer/count semantics. Indexed entries are not reconciled to the active limit.

previousFindings.remediation: Use the delegated reader's authoritative validated EOCD/ZIP64 selection, consistent ZIP32 total/per-disk fields and all ZIP64 total/size/offset triggers. Bound raw central-record traversal/count before index allocation, reject inconsistent unsupported metadata, and retain a post-open active archive.len cap as defense in depth; that later check cannot undo earlier allocation. Reconcile selected raw counts with indexed counts for exact duplicates, including name collapse, comments, ZIP64 and prepended data.

A trailing false EOCD with zero count and inconsistent disk numbers is skipped by zip but trusted by preindex. The earlier actual directory can exceed max_entries while remaining inside compressed/inflated-byte and structural bounds. No constructed archive was executed.
The additional validated trace uses a small-count fake with an impossible directory offset. Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed the nonempty ZIP32 reader selects on-disk count and parses that many central headers. impact.why: A false EOCD carrying count zero and inconsistent disk fields can be placed inside the real EOCD comment. preindex_budget derives max_entries from the last byte signature resembling an EOCD, without validating that candidate's disk/comment/directory fields. The ZIP reader uses validated candidate selection and retries earlier EOCDs when the last one fails. A false zero-count footer in the real comment therefore passes preindex while ZipArchive indexes the earlier real directory. Neither admit nor read_package caps the actual opened archive length, and the collapsed-duplicate comparison also uses the unrelated false count.
The assigned source supplies an alternative invalid-candidate framing: an offset at/past the false EOCD makes zip reject that candidate. Both framings use the same last-signature/validated-selection mismatch. A post-open length check bounds later processing but cannot undo metadata already allocated while indexing.
A separate, incomplete EOCD/ZIP64 parser is treated as authoritative for resource admission even though the delegated ZIP parser chooses its own footer/count semantics. Indexed entries are not reconciled to the active limit.
Assigned discovery-0016 additionally confirms the name-map shortfall inference can be concealed by a low total count: +8=20000/+10=1 causes preindex to see 1 while the reader indexes 20000, and actual<declared is false even after exact-name collapse. Direct raw-duplicate detection or the dependency duplicate indicator is required alongside authoritative preindex counts; case/decoded-name collision checks remain effective.

previousFindings.remediation: Use the delegated reader's authoritative validated EOCD/ZIP64 selection, consistent ZIP32 total/per-disk fields and all ZIP64 total/size/offset triggers. Bound raw central-record traversal/count before index allocation, reject inconsistent unsupported metadata, and retain a post-open active archive.len cap as defense in depth; that later check cannot undo earlier allocation. Reconcile selected raw counts with indexed counts for exact duplicates, including name collapse, comments, ZIP64 and prepended data. Detect raw exact-name duplicates directly or through the reader's duplicate flag rather than relying solely on a count-shortfall inference.

validation.summary:
Parent verified the local preindex parser, post-open checks and PartFs reader, plus locked zip9.0.5 EOCD retry loop and multi-disk mismatch rejection. A trailing false EOCD with zero count and inconsistent disk numbers is skipped by zip but trusted by preindex. The earlier actual directory can exceed max_entries while remaining inside compressed/inflated-byte and structural bounds. No constructed archive was executed.
The additional validated trace uses a small-count fake with an impossible directory offset. Locked zip 9.0.5 rejects offsets at/past the candidate EOCD and retries earlier candidates (format/find_central_directory.rs:100-116,163-166; read/zip_archive.rs:199-235), then reads/indexes that directory (:239-316). No local-header or CRC inconsistency is required. An over-count package need not crash in every embedding: actual resource effects depend on caller limits, metadata size and process isolation.
Parent inspected local zip9.0.5 src/read/mod.rs:53-74, which selects number_of_files_on_this_disk for ZIP32, and src/read/zip_archive.rs:271-299, which collects central records to that count. format/blocks.rs:379-383 selects ZIP64 on total/size/offset sentinels. Repository precheck instead reads+10 and returns early unless total==FFFF; neither admit nor read_package caps the actual index length. Baseline additionally established false-EOCD candidate selection differences.
Assigned discovery-0010 Standard corroboration (source validation, not reducer verification): Parent confirmed declared_entry_count selects bare last EOCD magic, zip9.0.5 continues past impossible directory offsets, and actual index counts are not bounded by max_entries after selection. A real well-formed directory with unique entries and consistent local headers is unaffected by the other checks.
Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): A footer with disk numbers zero, per-disk count 60000 and total count 1 passes preindex max10000. Cached zip9.0.5/src/read/mod.rs:69-74 uses per-disk count; read/zip_archive.rs:253-326 checks disk-number agreement and indexes exactly that count. All distinct entries can have valid names/headers/CRCs and small payloads. Existing byte budgets need not be exceeded.
Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed the nonempty ZIP32 reader selects on-disk count and parses that many central headers. Header consistency/extent checks operate on the resulting archive and do not reconcile the footer count fields. Using a positive low total avoids the distinct empty-archive shortcut.
Assigned discovery-0017 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): A false 22-byte EOCD at the end of the real archive's comment can declare count 0 and directory offset 0xffffffff. The precheck returns 0 immediately. The matching zip 9.0.5 source rejects an empty footer whose central offset exceeds its position and continues searching; its archive metadata loop retries candidates. The real archive's unique, safe empty entries can then pass header/extent/CRC checks while actual count exceeds max_entries. `admit` checks only actual<declared, and read_package has no actual-count rejection.

impact.why: A false EOCD carrying count zero and inconsistent disk fields can be placed inside the real EOCD comment. The same mismatch also invalidates admission's declared-count comparison used to detect collapsed exact duplicates.

rootCause.summary:
preindex_budget derives max_entries from the last byte signature resembling an EOCD, without validating that candidate's disk/comment/directory fields. The ZIP reader uses validated candidate selection and retries earlier EOCDs when the last one fails. A false zero-count footer in the real comment therefore passes preindex while ZipArchive indexes the earlier real directory. Neither admit nor read_package caps the actual opened archive length, and the collapsed-duplicate comparison also uses the unrelated false count.
The assigned source supplies an alternative invalid-candidate framing: an offset at/past the false EOCD makes zip reject that candidate. Both framings use the same last-signature/validated-selection mismatch. A post-open length check bounds later processing but cannot undo metadata already allocated while indexing.
A separate, incomplete EOCD/ZIP64 parser is treated as authoritative for resource admission even though the delegated ZIP parser chooses its own footer/count semantics. Indexed entries are not reconciled to the active limit.
Assigned discovery-0016 additionally confirms the name-map shortfall inference can be concealed by a low total count: +8=20000/+10=1 causes preindex to see 1 while the reader indexes 20000, and actual<declared is false even after exact-name collapse. Direct raw-duplicate detection or the dependency duplicate indicator is required alongside authoritative preindex counts; case/decoded-name collision checks remain effective.
Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Resource admission and ZIP parsing do not share a validated end-record decision; a one-sided post-open comparison cannot enforce the upper bound against the reader's actual entry index.

previousFindings.remediation: Use the delegated reader's authoritative validated EOCD/ZIP64 selection, consistent ZIP32 total/per-disk fields and all ZIP64 total/size/offset triggers. Bound raw central-record traversal/count before index allocation, reject inconsistent unsupported metadata, and retain a post-open active archive.len cap as defense in depth; that later check cannot undo earlier allocation. Reconcile selected raw counts with indexed counts for exact duplicates, including name collapse, comments, ZIP64 and prepended data. Detect raw exact-name duplicates directly or through the reader's duplicate flag rather than relying solely on a count-shortfall inference.

validation.summary:
Parent verified the local preindex parser, post-open checks and PartFs reader, plus locked zip9.0.5 EOCD retry loop and multi-disk mismatch rejection. A trailing false EOCD with zero count and inconsistent disk numbers is skipped by zip but trusted by preindex. The earlier actual directory can exceed max_entries while remaining inside compressed/inflated-byte and structural bounds. No constructed archive was executed.
The additional validated trace uses a small-count fake with an impossible directory offset. Locked zip 9.0.5 rejects offsets at/past the candidate EOCD and retries earlier candidates (format/find_central_directory.rs:100-116,163-166; read/zip_archive.rs:199-235), then reads/indexes that directory (:239-316). No local-header or CRC inconsistency is required. An over-count package need not crash in every embedding: actual resource effects depend on caller limits, metadata size and process isolation.
Parent inspected local zip9.0.5 src/read/mod.rs:53-74, which selects number_of_files_on_this_disk for ZIP32, and src/read/zip_archive.rs:271-299, which collects central records to that count. format/blocks.rs:379-383 selects ZIP64 on total/size/offset sentinels. Repository precheck instead reads+10 and returns early unless total==FFFF; neither admit nor read_package caps the actual index length. Baseline additionally established false-EOCD candidate selection differences.
Assigned discovery-0010 Standard corroboration (source validation, not reducer verification): Parent confirmed declared_entry_count selects bare last EOCD magic, zip9.0.5 continues past impossible directory offsets, and actual index counts are not bounded by max_entries after selection. A real well-formed directory with unique entries and consistent local headers is unaffected by the other checks.
Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): A footer with disk numbers zero, per-disk count 60000 and total count 1 passes preindex max10000. Cached zip9.0.5/src/read/mod.rs:69-74 uses per-disk count; read/zip_archive.rs:253-326 checks disk-number agreement and indexes exactly that count. All distinct entries can have valid names/headers/CRCs and small payloads. Existing byte budgets need not be exceeded.
Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed the nonempty ZIP32 reader selects on-disk count and parses that many central headers. Header consistency/extent checks operate on the resulting archive and do not reconcile the footer count fields. Using a positive low total avoids the distinct empty-archive shortcut.
Assigned discovery-0017 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): A false 22-byte EOCD at the end of the real archive's comment can declare count 0 and directory offset 0xffffffff. The precheck returns 0 immediately. The matching zip 9.0.5 source rejects an empty footer whose central offset exceeds its position and continues searching; its archive metadata loop retries candidates. The real archive's unique, safe empty entries can then pass header/extent/CRC checks while actual count exceeds max_entries. `admit` checks only actual<declared, and read_package has no actual-count rejection.
Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Parent inspected pinned zip 9.0.5 source: src/read/zip_archive.rs:178-237 loops through end-record candidates and continues after CentralDirectoryInfo/read_central_header errors. It explicitly rejects inconsistent multidisk metadata at 253-257. Jubarte's precheck instead selects the last signature and returns its low count; admission only refuses actual<declared and OPC does not recheck actual>max_entries. This source-backed parser differential establishes the missing budget control without runtime reproduction.

impact.rationale: Bypass of configured resource limits and excess indexing/processing memory/CPU.
impact.why: A false EOCD carrying count zero and inconsistent disk fields can be placed inside the real EOCD comment. The preindex check accepts zero; zip rejects the false candidate and opens the real directory containing more than max_entries. This defeats the advertised entry-count budget and permits excess indexing, structural validation, and per-entry processing. The same mismatch also invalidates admission's declared-count comparison used to detect collapsed exact duplicates.

previousFindings.title: ZIP footer and count interpretation mismatch bypasses entry-count admission
previousFindings.summary: The independent preindex footer parser can count a different EOCD or count field from zip 9.0.5. False small-count EOCDs in valid comments can be skipped by zip; a same-footer total=3/on-this-disk=10001 also passes max_entries=10000 while zip indexes 10001. ZIP64 size/offset triggers differ too. Neither admission nor PartFs enforces the actual opened count; duplicate detection also trusts the unrelated declared count. Another supplied false-footer proof uses an EOCD-shaped record inside the real archive comment whose own comment length is impossible; preindex trusts its low count while the ZIP reader rejects it and backtracks.

severity.rationale: An untrusted document supplier can directly induce disproportionate resource use or bypass a resource admission control during normal parsing. Impact is availability of the processing worker/embedding process; no public deployment is assumed.
severity.changeConditions: Enforcing logical-work/selected-directory bounds removes the path; process isolation limits shared-service consequences.

confidence.rationale: Independent investigator and parent traced actual local source and effective controls. Resource counts are statically derived; no runtime reproduction or deployment is asserted.

rootCause.summary:
preindex_budget derives max_entries from the last byte signature resembling an EOCD, without validating that candidate's disk/comment/directory fields. The ZIP reader uses validated candidate selection and retries earlier EOCDs when the last one fails. A false zero-count footer in the real comment therefore passes preindex while ZipArchive indexes the earlier real directory. Neither admit nor read_package caps the actual opened archive length, and the collapsed-duplicate comparison also uses the unrelated false count.
The assigned source supplies an alternative invalid-candidate framing: an offset at/past the false EOCD makes zip reject that candidate. Both framings use the same last-signature/validated-selection mismatch. A post-open length check bounds later processing but cannot undo metadata already allocated while indexing.
A separate, incomplete EOCD/ZIP64 parser is treated as authoritative for resource admission even though the delegated ZIP parser chooses its own footer/count semantics. Indexed entries are not reconciled to the active limit.
Assigned discovery-0016 additionally confirms the name-map shortfall inference can be concealed by a low total count: +8=20000/+10=1 causes preindex to see 1 while the reader indexes 20000, and actual<declared is false even after exact-name collapse. Direct raw-duplicate detection or the dependency duplicate indicator is required alongside authoritative preindex counts; case/decoded-name collision checks remain effective.
Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Resource admission and ZIP parsing do not share a validated end-record decision; a one-sided post-open comparison cannot enforce the upper bound against the reader's actual entry index.

previousFindings.remediation: Use the delegated reader's authoritative validated EOCD/ZIP64 selection, consistent ZIP32 total/per-disk fields and all ZIP64 total/size/offset triggers. Bound raw central-record traversal/count before index allocation, reject inconsistent unsupported metadata, and retain a post-open active archive.len cap as defense in depth; that later check cannot undo earlier allocation. Reconcile selected raw counts with indexed counts for exact duplicates, including name collapse, comments, ZIP64 and prepended data. Detect raw exact-name duplicates directly or through the reader's duplicate flag rather than relying solely on a count-shortfall inference.

validation.summary:
Parent verified the local preindex parser, post-open checks and PartFs reader, plus locked zip9.0.5 EOCD retry loop and multi-disk mismatch rejection. A trailing false EOCD with zero count and inconsistent disk numbers is skipped by zip but trusted by preindex. The earlier actual directory can exceed max_entries while remaining inside compressed/inflated-byte and structural bounds. No constructed archive was executed.
The additional validated trace uses a small-count fake with an impossible directory offset. Locked zip 9.0.5 rejects offsets at/past the candidate EOCD and retries earlier candidates (format/find_central_directory.rs:100-116,163-166; read/zip_archive.rs:199-235), then reads/indexes that directory (:239-316). No local-header or CRC inconsistency is required. An over-count package need not crash in every embedding: actual resource effects depend on caller limits, metadata size and process isolation.
Parent inspected local zip9.0.5 src/read/mod.rs:53-74, which selects number_of_files_on_this_disk for ZIP32, and src/read/zip_archive.rs:271-299, which collects central records to that count. format/blocks.rs:379-383 selects ZIP64 on total/size/offset sentinels. Repository precheck instead reads+10 and returns early unless total==FFFF; neither admit nor read_package caps the actual index length. Baseline additionally established false-EOCD candidate selection differences.
Assigned discovery-0010 Standard corroboration (source validation, not reducer verification): Parent confirmed declared_entry_count selects bare last EOCD magic, zip9.0.5 continues past impossible directory offsets, and actual index counts are not bounded by max_entries after selection. A real well-formed directory with unique entries and consistent local headers is unaffected by the other checks.
Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): A footer with disk numbers zero, per-disk count 60000 and total count 1 passes preindex max10000. Cached zip9.0.5/src/read/mod.rs:69-74 uses per-disk count; read/zip_archive.rs:253-326 checks disk-number agreement and indexes exactly that count. All distinct entries can have valid names/headers/CRCs and small payloads. Existing byte budgets need not be exceeded.
Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed the nonempty ZIP32 reader selects on-disk count and parses that many central headers. Header consistency/extent checks operate on the resulting archive and do not reconcile the footer count fields. Using a positive low total avoids the distinct empty-archive shortcut.
Assigned discovery-0017 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): A false 22-byte EOCD at the end of the real archive's comment can declare count 0 and directory offset 0xffffffff. The precheck returns 0 immediately. The matching zip 9.0.5 source rejects an empty footer whose central offset exceeds its position and continues searching; its archive metadata loop retries candidates. The real archive's unique, safe empty entries can then pass header/extent/CRC checks while actual count exceeds max_entries. `admit` checks only actual<declared, and read_package has no actual-count rejection.
Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Parent inspected pinned zip 9.0.5 source: src/read/zip_archive.rs:178-237 loops through end-record candidates and continues after CentralDirectoryInfo/read_central_header errors. It explicitly rejects inconsistent multidisk metadata at 253-257. Jubarte's precheck instead selects the last signature and returns its low count; admission only refuses actual<declared and OPC does not recheck actual>max_entries. This source-backed parser differential establishes the missing budget control without runtime reproduction.

impact.rationale: Bypass of configured resource limits and excess indexing/processing memory/CPU.
impact.why: A false EOCD carrying count zero and inconsistent disk fields can be placed inside the real EOCD comment. The preindex check accepts zero; zip rejects the false candidate and opens the real directory containing more than max_entries. This defeats the advertised entry-count budget and permits excess indexing, structural validation, and per-entry processing. The same mismatch also invalidates admission's declared-count comparison used to detect collapsed exact duplicates.

rootCause.summary:
DocxOptions.reference is copied into a template and opened by PartFs, which enforces ZIP budgets but does not admit ordinary document XML. assemble reads the selected main part and passes it to frame/final_section. final_section calls the trusted-only parse_xdocument on those bytes, reaching unguarded recursive parse_element. Native/Python/WASM wrappers forward reference bytes without adding that missing XML gate; native CLI read_document only sniffs the container.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: The reference-template path treats PartFs::open's ZIP/inflation bounds as sufficient and invokes Dom::parse_xdocument on unchecked reference XML, contrary to that API's requirement for prior XML policy enforcement.

findings.remediation: Admit every supplied reference DOCX under explicit active InputLimits before metadata, style, scholar, frame or other reference XML consumers parse it, or consistently use checked parsing at every main and preserved auxiliary XML boundary. Propagate limits and typed refusals across Rust/Python/WASM/CLI paths.

returnedFinding.title: Markdown reference documents reach recursive XML parsing without depth admission
returnedFinding.body: A caller-supplied reference DOCX is opened with PartFs::open and its main XML is passed into frame/final_section without package admission or checked XML parsing. PartFs bounds ZIP sizes and entry counts but does not enforce XML depth on document parts. final_section calls the explicitly unchecked Dom::parse_xdocument, whose parse_element recursively descends for every nested element without a depth limit. rootCause.summary: `apply_sect_pr()` accepts unbounded f32 page dimensions and margins. A text-relative border starts at that margin. Dotted-border painting clamps on/off intervals to0.5 each, then repeatedly adds1 to the f32 position. At a large finite coordinate this addition cannot change the value; the while condition remains true and each iteration pushes another FillRect.

findings.remediation: Validate finite, reasonable page/margin/border geometry before layout. Use a bounded integer segment count instead of open-ended float accumulation, enforce a maximum border-operation budget, and explicitly refuse any step that cannot advance.

counterEvidence: All trigger numbers are finite; a NaN/infinity-only check would not fix the problem.

findings.title: Redaction succeeds while UTF-16 XML retains the removed text
findings.summary: The redact operation can return successful clean and redline documents while a supported BOM-marked UTF-16LE/BE auxiliary XML part still contains the same confidential text. Its XML leak branch uses lossy UTF-8 and misses the retained copy, which a recipient can recover after sharing. Even the scanner's no-root fallback searches the already lossily decoded string, so it cannot recover a multi-character value split by UTF-16 NUL bytes.

severity.rationale: An outgoing document can disclose text the user explicitly asked to remove. A supplier can place a duplicate in supported customXml and the user performs ordinary redaction; successful checking makes the confidentiality failure likely when that document is shared.
severity.changeConditions: Impact depends on sensitivity and subsequent sharing. Consistent BOM-aware decoding and fail-closed scanning remove the bypass.

confidence.rationale: Parent verified UTF16 admission, raw part retention/output, XML-only lossy UTF8 branch and success gate. Baseline validation allows unchanged auxiliary issues. No product execution was performed.

rootCause.summary:
Admission deliberately transcodes BOM-marked UTF16 XML for validation, but PartFs preserves its raw bytes. After visible body redaction, `leaks_within()` routes every .xml/.rels part into `String::from_utf8_lossy()` and semantic scanning. Its UTF16 byte search exists only for non-XML parts. Thus NUL-interleaved UTF16 copies are invisible; `check_redactions()` sees no hits and permits output with those unchanged bytes. The standalone leaks API and both prepared artifacts use this same branch; ordinary Transitional input does not require Strict normalization to rewrite the untouched auxiliary part.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `check_redactions()` relies on `scrub::leaks()` to detect retained text in both output packages. The scanner chooses its XML branch by suffix and lossy-decodes as UTF-8; its UTF-16LE raw-byte search runs only for non-XML. BOM-prefixed UTF-16 XML is accepted by admission but its NUL-separated characters evade the scan. The no-root fallback returns xml.contains(needle) after incompatible decoding rather than searching the original bytes; non-XML UTF-16LE test coverage exercises a different branch.

findings.remediation: Decode every XML part with the same BOM-aware policy as admission before semantic leak scanning. Fail closed on unsupported/undecodable representations and retain raw UTF8 and both UTF16 byte-order checks as defense in depth. Use the same decoding across leak checks and package validation.

Assigned discovery-0017 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): BOM UTF16LE/BE XML is supported by admission. rootCause.summary: Admission decodes BOM-marked UTF-16LE/BE XML for validation, so a `customXml/item1.xml` holding the target text is supported input. Redaction rewrites the body and touched stories, preserving untouched part bytes in the clean DOCX. `check_redactions()` scans generated outputs through `scrub::leaks()`, but its XML branch passes lossy UTF-8 to `xml_holds()` instead of decoding the XML encoding. Interleaved UTF-16 NULs prevent semantic or fallback matching; the raw UTF-16 needle check is available only to non-XML parts. An empty match set permits successful return with the sensitive bytes still present.

finding.remediation: Reuse a BOM/encoding-aware XML decoder before leak scanning, handling UTF-16LE and UTF-16BE, and fail closed when an XML part cannot be decoded or scanned completely.

Custom XML is outside the edited story, so a copied secret can remain while visible text is redacted and check_redactions returns success.

rootCause.summary:
Admission deliberately transcodes BOM-marked UTF16 XML for validation, but PartFs preserves its raw bytes. After visible body redaction, `leaks_within()` routes every .xml/.rels part into `String::from_utf8_lossy()` and semantic scanning. Its UTF16 byte search exists only for non-XML parts. Thus NUL-interleaved UTF16 copies are invisible; `check_redactions()` sees no hits and permits output with those unchanged bytes. The standalone leaks API and both prepared artifacts use this same branch; ordinary Transitional input does not require Strict normalization to rewrite the untouched auxiliary part.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `check_redactions()` relies on `scrub::leaks()` to detect retained text in both output packages. The scanner chooses its XML branch by suffix and lossy-decodes as UTF-8; its UTF-16LE raw-byte search runs only for non-XML. BOM-prefixed UTF-16 XML is accepted by admission but its NUL-separated characters evade the scan.

previousFindings.remediation: Decode every XML part with the same BOM-aware policy as admission before semantic leak scanning. Fail closed on unsupported/undecodable representations and retain raw UTF8 and both UTF16 byte-order checks as defense in depth. Use the same decoding across leak checks and package validation.

findings.title: Metadata scrub leaves property parts under alternate names
findings.summary: With docprops enabled, scrub removes metadata only from three conventional filenames. A document using alternate package relationship targets can retain creators, editors, dates, company/manager or custom properties while scrub returns success. The custom-properties branch additionally skips relationship/content-type removal when docProps/custom.xml is absent, leaving an active relationship to a relocated target such as metadata/private.xml.

severity.rationale: The user invokes a privacy operation before sharing, yet identifying or confidential property data remains. A supplier controls package names/relationships; no host privilege is needed. The selected scrub deterministically misses alternate targets.
severity.changeConditions: Impact depends on metadata sensitivity and sharing. Resolving selected metadata through relationships/content types and verifying removal closes the gap.

confidence.rationale: Parent confirmed fixed path constants, exact-path loads, conditional custom cleanup, arbitrary package relationship preservation and validation-based success. No Word or application execution performed.

rootCause.summary:
`scrub()` invokes `scrub_properties()` when docprops is selected. That routine resolves only docProps/core.xml, docProps/app.xml and docProps/custom.xml constants, rather than actual property relationship targets. If custom properties use another part name, even relationship cleanup is skipped. PartFs preserves arbitrary ordinary parts and their relationships; output serialization retains untouched metadata. Validation compares newly introduced issues rather than the requested privacy postcondition. The assigned trace additionally follows public README sharing guidance, authoritative package-level relationships and preservation of every surviving output part. Admission and structural validation do not mandate conventional metadata filenames or enforce anonymization.
Privacy sanitization selects conventional filenames instead of all relationship/content-type-selected property parts and does not verify requested removal postconditions.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): Sensitive metadata is selected by physical conventional filenames rather than its authoritative package relationships/content type. Structural before/after validation checks only newly introduced findings; it does not certify that selected privacy fields were removed. The assigned remediation includes supported Strict relationship variants and coexistence of conventional and relocated targets.

findings.remediation: Resolve all core, extended and custom property parts through authoritative package relationships and content types, sanitize every applicable internal target according to docprops selection, and remove corresponding custom-property parts/relationships/content-type records coherently. Verify the selected privacy postcondition; refuse unsupported or ambiguous layouts rather than returning a successfully scrubbed copy. Preserve intentional title/subject/application and revision-date retention. Missing/invalid selected targets require explicit refusal or documented safe handling; default public and CLI callers must enforce the same postcondition. Include supported Strict property relationship variants and regression cases containing both conventional and relocated targets; every active property target must satisfy the requested postcondition.

validation.summary:
A package relationship can point to an alternate valid properties part. Loading preserves that relationship and its raw bytes. None of the three fixed-path branches loads the alternate part, and a valid unchanged metadata part introduces no validation finding, allowing scrub to return output with the private fields intact.
Verified the scrub call chain, all three fixed-path branches, and preservation of surviving parts/package relationships. Admission checks supported main document type and XML structure, not conventional metadata filenames; validation compares structural findings rather than enforcing anonymization. The finding is narrowed to docprops; author-alias traversal outside word/ was not independently validated as a separate issue.
Parent verified default docprops=true, fixed core/app/custom handling, unchanged-part serialization and Ok(out) after only introduced-finding checks. Python Document.scrub promises the same defaults. Recipient byte inspection establishes disclosure without requiring Word UI behavior.
Additional validated trace gives a bounded well-formed metadata/core.xml selected by a root relationship and appropriate content type; absent conventional docProps/core.xml skips removal. Default public/CLI docprops scrub returns unchanged private bytes because general validation only rejects newly introduced findings, not failed privacy postconditions.
Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): Independently inspected root relationship loading and raw-part preservation in opc/mod.rs365-376, property removal357-384 and scrub's before/after validation. For docprops-only scrub with an absent conventional CUSTOM file, no custom relationship/content removal occurs; unchanged retained metadata introduces no new validation finding and therefore returns successfully. This is a supported package-loader path, not a claim about an observed Word deployment.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Parent verified scrub contract (5-24), default docprops (68-75), public pipeline (109-150), fixed constants (39-47), complete scrub_properties (357-385) and relationship-aware custom_props_part (document_comparer.rs:6180-6188). Alternate related metadata remains unchanged; before/after validation only rejects newly introduced structural findings.
Assigned discovery-0017 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Scrub accepts packages by main document existence and returns the serialized output if validation introduced no new findings. Metadata processing loads only CORE, APP and CUSTOM constants. No alternative-target lookup occurs, and PartFs serializes every remaining raw part and package relationship. Consequently an alternate core/app target keeps its selected fields, while an alternate custom target also keeps its relationship.

finding.title: Property scrubbing leaves metadata stored at alternate part names
finding.summary: Scrubbing a DOCX whose metadata relationships point to nonstandard part names leaves creator/editor/company fields and custom properties unchanged. The command returns a package even with document-property scrubbing enabled, so a recipient can recover identifying metadata the sender intended to remove.

severity.rationale: The direct impact is retained identifying document metadata. The source does not establish exposure of credentials or high-sensitivity data, and sharing the result is an additional user workflow step.
severity.changeConditions: Evidence that high-sensitivity custom-property values are routinely scrubbed and shared would increase impact; resolving all metadata by relationship/content type removes the bypass.

confidence.rationale: The scrubber only loads three constants and preserves other parts/relationships; it does not resolve metadata targets despite package support for arbitrary relationship paths.

rootCause.summary: scrub_properties assumes metadata lives at conventional filenames rather than following package metadata relationships or content types. A core/extended/custom relationship can target a different in-package part; that data is untouched. The custom-properties relationship is only removed when the conventional custom part is present.

finding.remediation: Discover all internal core, extended and custom metadata parts through package relationships/content types, scrub or remove each one, and verify the requested metadata-removal postcondition before returning.

counterEvidence: Conventional metadata names are correctly scrubbed.
Validation compares newly introduced findings; it does not verify scrub confidentiality postconditions.

limitations: No package crafted or scrub command executed.
validation.summary: Scrub accepts packages by main document existence and returns the serialized output if validation introduced no new findings. Metadata processing loads only CORE, APP and CUSTOM constants. No alternative-target lookup occurs, and PartFs serializes every remaining raw part and package relationship. Consequently an alternate core/app target keeps its selected fields, while an alternate custom target also keeps its relationship.

rootCause.summary: `scrub()` invokes `scrub_properties()` when docprops is selected. That routine resolves only docProps/core.xml, docProps/app.xml and docProps/custom.xml constants, rather than actual property relationship targets. If custom properties use another part name, even relationship cleanup is skipped. PartFs preserves arbitrary ordinary parts and their relationships; output serialization retains untouched metadata. Validation compares newly introduced issues rather than the requested privacy postcondition.

previousFindings.remediation: Discover core, extended and custom property parts through package relationship types and resolved targets, with content-type-aware handling where needed. Remove every selected part/field and all corresponding relationships/content-type records, and verify the privacy postcondition rather than silently skipping unsupported representations.

counterEvidence: Conventional property files are scrubbed and conventional custom properties get part/relationship/content-type cleanup.

Actual confidentiality impact depends on retained values and subsequent document distribution.

validation.summary: A package relationship can point to an alternate valid properties part. Loading preserves that relationship and its raw bytes. codeEvidence.label: scrub guarantee
codeEvidence.code:
Removes who touched a document before it goes out: author names (as one
alias, `--author-alias NAME`), rsids, the people and dates in the document

rootCause.summary:
`scrub()` invokes `scrub_properties()` when docprops is selected. That routine resolves only docProps/core.xml, docProps/app.xml and docProps/custom.xml constants, rather than actual property relationship targets. If custom properties use another part name, even relationship cleanup is skipped. PartFs preserves arbitrary ordinary parts and their relationships; output serialization retains untouched metadata. Validation compares newly introduced issues rather than the requested privacy postcondition. The assigned trace additionally follows public README sharing guidance, authoritative package-level relationships and preservation of every surviving output part. Admission and structural validation do not mandate conventional metadata filenames or enforce anonymization.
Privacy sanitization selects conventional filenames instead of all relationship/content-type-selected property parts and does not verify requested removal postconditions.

previousFindings.remediation: Resolve all core, extended and custom property parts through authoritative package relationships and content types, sanitize every applicable internal target according to docprops selection, and remove corresponding custom-property parts/relationships/content-type records coherently. Verify the selected privacy postcondition; refuse unsupported or ambiguous layouts rather than returning a successfully scrubbed copy. Preserve intentional title/subject/application and revision-date retention. Missing/invalid selected targets require explicit refusal or documented safe handling; default public and CLI callers must enforce the same postcondition.

validation.summary:
A package relationship can point to an alternate valid properties part. Loading preserves that relationship and its raw bytes. None of the three fixed-path branches loads the alternate part, and a valid unchanged metadata part introduces no validation finding, allowing scrub to return output with the private fields intact.
Verified the scrub call chain, all three fixed-path branches, and preservation of surviving parts/package relationships. Admission checks supported main document type and XML structure, not conventional metadata filenames; validation compares structural findings rather than enforcing anonymization. The finding is narrowed to docprops; author-alias traversal outside word/ was not independently validated as a separate issue.
Parent verified default docprops=true, fixed core/app/custom handling, unchanged-part serialization and Ok(out) after only introduced-finding checks. Python Document.scrub promises the same defaults. Recipient byte inspection establishes disclosure without requiring Word UI behavior.
Additional validated trace gives a bounded well-formed metadata/core.xml selected by a root relationship and appropriate content type; absent conventional docProps/core.xml skips removal. Default public/CLI docprops scrub returns unchanged private bytes because general validation only rejects newly introduced findings, not failed privacy postconditions.
Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): Independently inspected root relationship loading and raw-part preservation in opc/mod.rs365-376, property removal357-384 and scrub's before/after validation. For docprops-only scrub with an absent conventional CUSTOM file, no custom relationship/content removal occurs; unchanged retained metadata introduces no new validation finding and therefore returns successfully. This is a supported package-loader path, not a claim about an observed Word deployment.

rootCause.summary:
`scrub()` invokes `scrub_properties()` when docprops is selected. That routine resolves only docProps/core.xml, docProps/app.xml and docProps/custom.xml constants, rather than actual property relationship targets. If custom properties use another part name, even relationship cleanup is skipped. PartFs preserves arbitrary ordinary parts and their relationships; output serialization retains untouched metadata. Validation compares newly introduced issues rather than the requested privacy postcondition. The assigned trace additionally follows public README sharing guidance, authoritative package-level relationships and preservation of every surviving output part. Admission and structural validation do not mandate conventional metadata filenames or enforce anonymization.
Privacy sanitization selects conventional filenames instead of all relationship/content-type-selected property parts and does not verify requested removal postconditions.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): Sensitive metadata is selected by physical conventional filenames rather than its authoritative package relationships/content type.

previousFindings.remediation: Resolve all core, extended and custom property parts through authoritative package relationships and content types, sanitize every applicable internal target according to docprops selection, and remove corresponding custom-property parts/relationships/content-type records coherently. Verify the selected privacy postcondition; refuse unsupported or ambiguous layouts rather than returning a successfully scrubbed copy. Preserve intentional title/subject/application and revision-date retention. Missing/invalid selected targets require explicit refusal or documented safe handling; default public and CLI callers must enforce the same postcondition.

validation.summary:
A package relationship can point to an alternate valid properties part. Loading preserves that relationship and its raw bytes. None of the three fixed-path branches loads the alternate part, and a valid unchanged metadata part introduces no validation finding, allowing scrub to return output with the private fields intact.
Verified the scrub call chain, all three fixed-path branches, and preservation of surviving parts/package relationships. Admission checks supported main document type and XML structure, not conventional metadata filenames; validation compares structural findings rather than enforcing anonymization. The finding is narrowed to docprops; author-alias traversal outside word/ was not independently validated as a separate issue.
Parent verified default docprops=true, fixed core/app/custom handling, unchanged-part serialization and Ok(out) after only introduced-finding checks. Python Document.scrub promises the same defaults. Recipient byte inspection establishes disclosure without requiring Word UI behavior.
Additional validated trace gives a bounded well-formed metadata/core.xml selected by a root relationship and appropriate content type; absent conventional docProps/core.xml skips removal. Default public/CLI docprops scrub returns unchanged private bytes because general validation only rejects newly introduced findings, not failed privacy postconditions.
Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): Independently inspected root relationship loading and raw-part preservation in opc/mod.rs365-376, property removal357-384 and scrub's before/after validation. For docprops-only scrub with an absent conventional CUSTOM file, no custom relationship/content removal occurs; unchanged retained metadata introduces no new validation finding and therefore returns successfully. This is a supported package-loader path, not a claim about an observed Word deployment.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Parent verified scrub contract (5-24), default docprops (68-75), public pipeline (109-150), fixed constants (39-47), complete scrub_properties (357-385) and relationship-aware custom_props_part (document_comparer.rs:6180-6188). Alternate related metadata remains unchanged; before/after validation only rejects newly introduced structural findings.
Assigned discovery-0017 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Scrub accepts packages by main document existence and returns the serialized output if validation introduced no new findings. Metadata processing loads only CORE, APP and CUSTOM constants. No alternative-target lookup occurs, and PartFs serializes every remaining raw part and package relationship. Consequently an alternate core/app target keeps its selected fields, while an alternate custom target also keeps its relationship.

findings.title: Opaque DTD and top-level CDATA bypass package XML depth checks
findings.summary:
Package admission ignores opaque DTD and top-level CDATA events, while the permissive DOM handles top-level <! constructs by skipping only to the first '>'. A delimiter within a quoted entity or CDATA body exposes deeply nested literal markup as recursive elements, bypassing admission depth and potentially exhausting the host stack. Rendering and lazy WmlDocument main-part access are preserved affected entrypoints.
An internal-subset comment with a literal > supplies an additional hidden-tag framing at the same declaration boundary. The assigned corroboration additionally identifies get_revisions main-document parsing after ordinary admission.

severity.rationale: A small ordinary-named document part can cause process stack exhaustion through public document processing. Impact is availability without privileged configuration; no external entity fetch or code execution is asserted.
severity.changeConditions: Rejecting DTD declarations at package admission and enforcing parser depth makes the representations agree. Isolated workers reduce shared-host impact.

confidence.rationale: Independent parent traced both parser interpretations and checked the locked quick-xml0.42 DTD parser's quote-sensitive skip. No runtime stack exhaustion was executed; the exact crash depth depends on runtime stack size.

rootCause.summary:
`check_xml_depth()` counts Start/Empty events and ignores DocType. The streaming reader correctly consumes the complete internal subset, including quoted element-like text. `parse_document()` instead skips any declaration only to the first closing angle bracket, even inside that literal, then treats the remaining literal markup as actual elements. Its recursive element parser has no independent depth guard. The checked XML API's explicit DTD rejection is absent from package admission. WmlDocument::from_bytes admits/stores parts and main_document later parses the same main bytes unchecked. A single quoted internal entity value with nested literal tags is sufficient; the earlier two-entity illustration is not a prerequisite.
The package gate and permissive DOM disagree on lexical boundaries of DTD/top-level CDATA. Admission ignores opaque tokens while the DOM's first-> skip reinterprets their remaining bytes as recursively nested markup.
The additional legal internal-subset-comment framing uses a literal > before nested-looking tags, exposing comment content through the same first-delimiter skip; it needs no entity expansion.
The rendering corroboration also retains quoted ENTITY/ATTLIST internal-subset handling in quick-xml 0.42 (parser/dtd.rs:28-60,122-144,196-205; reader/state.rs:163-173). A Transitional main part without altChunk or strict namespace rewriting remains unchanged before unchecked with_layout parsing; main-part existence/content-type checks are not declaration safety checks.
Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration: get_revisions (src/document_comparer.rs:6299-6308) shares the admitted-main unchecked DOM route. Checked inspect/edit parse_part_within rejects DTDs and is excluded from this specific declaration path.

findings.remediation: Align admission and DOM lexical/structural semantics for every opaque <! construct. Reject unsupported DTD and CDATA/text outside the root consistently with checked XML validation, and enforce active depth during DOM construction or use the checked API before every untrusted consumer. If opaque constructs are supported, consume their complete grammar rather than the first '>'. A DTD-only refusal does not fix the top-level CDATA subcase; retain valid in-root CDATA. Include get_revisions main-document parsing in the mandatory lexical/depth boundary while preserving existing checked-consumer distinctions.

validation.summary:
A valid internal entity declaration can contain a long literal with nested tag text without using the entity. quick-xml0.42 consumes the entire declaration as DocType (cached src/parser/dtd.rs:28-59,194-200,262-265), so package depth remains shallow. The DOM skip ends at the literal's first tag terminator and immediately enters recursion over the remaining literal. Normal rendering parses before it can reject the phantom root. This is independent of non-XML filenames.
Verified current quick-xml 0.42.0 parser/dtd.rs:28-30,124-135,194-199 preserves quoted entity values while scanning the internal subset, and reader/state.rs:163-173 emits the entire declaration as DocType. Admission ignores that event. The raw parser uses its first-'>' search regardless of quotation and resumes element parsing, so sufficiently deep literal tags can exceed the admitted depth.
Parent verified admission event match, DOM top-level skip and recursion plus WmlDocument admission/lazy parse. Current direct dependency quick-xml0.42.0 (Cargo.toml) treats quoted ENTITY content as one DTD and emits one DocType; local parser/dtd.rs:194-202,262-265 and reader/state.rs:163-174 confirm it. A quoted literal containing many opening/closing tags can remain below physical byte budgets but exceed DOM stack depth. Top-level CDATA is a sibling opaque-token path.
Assigned discovery-0008 corroboration: Independently verified DOCX main part with internal-subset comment -> admission quick-xml DocType ignored -> WmlDocument::main_document -> parse_document first-> skip -> hidden <a> strings -> recursive parse_element.
Assigned discovery-0009 corroboration (preserved offline Standard validation): Verified admission.rs:798-821 has no DocType refusal, parse.rs:539-547 stops at the first delimiter, and parse.rs:660-663 recurses. Installed quick-xml 0.42 source parser/dtd.rs:28-60,122-144,196-205 and reader/state.rs:163-173 show that quoted ENTITY/ATTLIST content is returned within one DocType event. Main-part metadata checks inspect existence/content type rather than XML declaration safety. with_layout then parses the unchanged Transitional main XML.
Assigned discovery-0010 Standard corroboration (source validation, not reducer verification): Parent read admission's event match, installed quick-xml0.42 quote-sensitive DTD state, WmlDocument constructor/main parse, and DOM declaration/recursive branches. A quoted replacement beginning with > then nested markup is not counted as elements by admission but is consumed by DOM recursion. Checked raw-XML validation rejects DTDs and is not the affected entry.
Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Verified unreferenced quoted DTD content is excluded from admission's depth events but can be treated as recursive markup by the DOM. The package path invokes admission yet never calls the checked DTD-rejecting validator before these consumers.

finding.title: A DTD literal bypasses package XML depth checks

rootCause.summary: `check_xml_depth()` counts Start/Empty events and ignores DocType. The streaming reader correctly consumes the complete internal subset, including quoted element-like text. `parse_document()` instead skips any declaration only to the first closing angle bracket, even inside that literal, then treats the remaining literal markup as actual elements. Its recursive element parser has no independent depth guard. The checked XML API's explicit DTD rejection is absent from package admission.

finding.remediation: Reject DocType events in package admission consistently with validate_xml, and enforce depth within DOM parsing or use the checked API with active limits before every consumer. If declarations must be tolerated, parse their full quoted/internal-subset grammar instead of stopping at the first `>`.

finding.title: Loading an admitted document can recurse into markup hidden inside its DTD
finding.summary: A conventionally named DOCX main XML part can put deeply nested literal markup inside a quoted DTD entity value. Admission treats the entire DTD as one ignored event, while the downstream raw DOM parser stops skipping at its first `>` and interprets the remaining embedded tags recursively. This bypasses configured XML depth limits and can terminate the native host or trap WASM.

severity.rationale: An untrusted document supplier controls ordinary main-part bytes, and the public admitted-document API reaches the recursive parser without privileged options. The supported impact is process/instance availability loss, constrained by recommended external process isolation; no XXE, file access or code execution is claimed.
severity.changeConditions: Mandatory DTD rejection during admission or checked parsing before DOM construction removes this path; a shared unsandboxed document service would increase impact.

confidence.rationale: Parent verified both repository parser implementations and cached locked quick-xml 0.42.0 DTD scanner behavior. No application code or crafted input was executed.

finalWorkerFinding.attacker: A party supplying an untrusted DOCX main-document XML part.
finalWorkerFinding.violated_security_invariant: The admission scanner must not hide markup from its depth accounting that the downstream DOM parser subsequently interprets recursively.
finalWorkerFinding.source_to_sink: Package admission ignores DocType events. quick-xml 0.42 consumes an entire DOCTYPE internal subset, including quoted entity values, as one DocType event. The downstream permissive DOM parser instead skips a '<!' construct only through the first '>' character. Deeply nested '<a>' markup inside a quoted entity value therefore remains hidden from admission but becomes recursive DOM-parser input after the first embedded '>'.
finalWorkerFinding.impact: An attacker can cause native stack exhaustion and process termination, or a WASM trap, using a conventionally named document.xml whose real document element is shallow and whose package fits the input budgets.

rootCause.summary:
`check_xml_depth()` counts Start/Empty events and ignores DocType. The streaming reader correctly consumes the complete internal subset, including quoted element-like text. `parse_document()` instead skips any declaration only to the first closing angle bracket, even inside that literal, then treats the remaining literal markup as actual elements. Its recursive element parser has no independent depth guard. The checked XML API's explicit DTD rejection is absent from package admission. WmlDocument::from_bytes admits/stores parts and main_document later parses the same main bytes unchecked. A single quoted internal entity value with nested literal tags is sufficient; the earlier two-entity illustration is not a prerequisite.
The package gate and permissive DOM disagree on lexical boundaries of DTD/top-level CDATA. Admission ignores opaque tokens while the DOM's first-> skip reinterprets their remaining bytes as recursively nested markup.
The additional legal internal-subset-comment framing uses a literal > before nested-looking tags, exposing comment content through the same first-delimiter skip; it needs no entity expansion.
The rendering corroboration also retains quoted ENTITY/ATTLIST internal-subset handling in quick-xml 0.42 (parser/dtd.rs:28-60,122-144,196-205; reader/state.rs:163-173). A Transitional main part without altChunk or strict namespace rewriting remains unchanged before unchecked with_layout parsing; main-part existence/content-type checks are not declaration safety checks.
Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration: get_revisions (src/document_comparer.rs:6299-6308) shares the admitted-main unchecked DOM route. Checked inspect/edit parse_part_within rejects DTDs and is excluded from this specific declaration path.

previousFindings.remediation: Align admission and DOM lexical/structural semantics for every opaque <! construct. Reject unsupported DTD and CDATA/text outside the root consistently with checked XML validation, and enforce active depth during DOM construction or use the checked API before every untrusted consumer. If opaque constructs are supported, consume their complete grammar rather than the first '>'. A DTD-only refusal does not fix the top-level CDATA subcase; retain valid in-root CDATA. Include get_revisions main-document parsing in the mandatory lexical/depth boundary while preserving existing checked-consumer distinctions.

findings.title: npm plan recording follows a predictable staging symlink
findings.summary: When recording plan operations, the npm CLI writes to a basename/PID staging path without exclusive creation. A local attacker who can create entries in that directory can redirect the write to an unrelated file writable by the CLI user.

severity.rationale: This is a local, conditional file-integrity failure: exploitation needs attacker write access to the plan directory and prediction/observation of the CLI PID. The target must be writable by the victim. These constrained prerequisites lower likelihood.
severity.changeConditions: A workflow routinely recording plans in a directory writable by less-trusted users increases likelihood. An exclusive regular staging file in a private unpredictable directory removes the link-following path.

confidence.rationale: Source directly constructs predictable partial name, calls default fs.writeFileSync and only then renames. No exclusive/no-follow protection applies; no runtime filesystem manipulation was performed.

rootCause.summary: `runEdit()` routes plan-plus-operation flags to `recordPlan()`. It derives the temporary pathname solely from target basename and process PID and calls `fs.writeFileSync()` with default truncating write semantics. A preexisting symlink at that pathname is followed, modifying its referent before `renameSync()` can publish the plan. Resolving the intended plan target does not validate the separate staging entry. The assigned source separately confirms that engine preview checks plan contents but does not reserve staging; npm consume-path O_NOFOLLOW/identity checks do not protect this recordPlan write.

findings.remediation: Create an unpredictable private staging directory next to the plan and open the staged regular file exclusively. Write through its held descriptor and rename only that file. At minimum refuse every preexisting staging entry using exclusive creation rather than default truncating writes.

rootCause.summary:
`font_index_path()` accepts JUBARTE_FONT_INDEX or derives the cache beside the font directory. On an uncached/stale font lookup, `indexed_faces()` records and saves entries. `FontIndex::save()` replaces the extension with tsv.PID.tmp, writes using fs::write without exclusive creation/no-follow, then renames. An existing symlink in a shared configured parent redirects the truncating write before rename.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: Persistent font-cache updates use PID-only staging names opened with a nonexclusive truncating write rather than exclusive private staging. The assigned native rendering trace shows index recording can trigger a save after an uncached or stale lookup even if no matching face is found; empty/off JUBARTE_FONT_INDEX disables saving.

Atomically rename only that file; refuse preexisting staging entries and document/private-parent expectations for shared configurations.

findings.title: Repeated HTML chunk references bypass conversion memory budgets
findings.summary: A DOCX can repeatedly reference one modest HTML part. The renderer admits the small original package, then copies and converts that chunk separately for every reference and concatenates all generated XML. The resulting allocation and work can exceed package budgets by orders of magnitude. For example, 10,000 short references to one 1 MiB ordinary HTML paragraph can imply roughly 10 GiB of generated XML; this is a static estimate, not a runtime measurement. The assigned source also supplies nested HTML tables as a depth variant of this post-admission expansion boundary: generated WML enters unchecked DOM and recursive table layout. Complete repair must enforce both cumulative size/work and generated depth; the earlier dedicated depth record remains cross-referenced.

severity.rationale: An untrusted document supplier can choose many tiny references and one ordinary HTML part that fit original byte/depth/entry limits. The direct outcome is memory/CPU exhaustion in the embedding process or WASM instance. No service deployment is assumed; process isolation limits collateral impact.
severity.changeConditions: Shared unsandboxed upload processing increases impact; a cumulative expanded-byte/node budget enforced before append removes this path.

findings.title: Python CLI output/plan and npm direct-output symlinks can overwrite unrelated files
findings.summary: Python and npm ordinary-output helpers check pathname existence separately from truncating writes; a local writer of the selected directory can replace an output name and redirect generated bytes to a victim-writable file. Python plan recording additionally uses a predictable basename/PID partial pathname without exclusive creation. The assigned report also corroborates npm plan staging, which is represented by the separately retained symlink-following.plan-staging finding. Without --force, a stable symlink to an existing referent is refused; post-preflight substitution bypasses that refusal, and a dangling link can pass the existence test. Filesystem/OS protections and shared-directory authority remain prerequisites. The shared writers also publish read/compare/revision results, document/PDF/PNG and font/render products, edit/visual-diff bundles, field-update reports, and repair outputs. Assigned Python and npm diff/bundle traces explicitly include dangling destination links permitting unintended file creation without --force, and forced existing-member links redirecting bundle/report writes; stable existing referents are refused in the ordinary nonracing no-force case.

severity.rationale: Medium integrity impact with medium likelihood: this is a local shared-directory attack requiring victim CLI execution in an attacker-writable directory, plus successful name replacement or prediction/observation of the PID-based staging name. No remote exposure or privileged execution is established.
severity.changeConditions: Higher impact requires a victim with greater filesystem privileges and an exploitable writable target; private non-writable output directories remove the attacker prerequisite.

confidence.rationale: Source directly shows nonexclusive, symlink-following writes after preflight and predictable plan staging in both adapters; platform behavior was assessed statically, with no exploit executed.

rootCause.summary:
Python/npm direct-output authorization is a non-atomic exists check followed by a symlink-following truncating write. Python plan recording separately derives a predictable PID partial and opens it without exclusive/no-follow semantics. Intentional resolution of the caller-selected plan target does not authorize an attacker-planted partial entry. The separate npm plan-staging instance is cross-referenced rather than absorbed.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: No-overwrite authorization is implemented as exists()/existsSync() preflight, while final writes follow and truncate the current destination. The final open is neither exclusive nor bound to a staged file/held destination parent.

findings.remediation: Publish Python/Node ordinary outputs, bundles and reports through held-directory authority and exclusive private staging. Atomically install without replacement when --force is false, or atomically replace the authorized destination entry when true; never truncate through a mutable final pathname. Apply exclusive unpredictable regular-file staging beside the authorized target to Python plan recording. Node recordPlan staging retains its separately established repair and identity. Expose/reuse native publication for Python CLI outputs with overwrite authorization passed into the commit operation; Node host publication must provide equivalent exclusive staging and atomic no-clobber/replacement.

counterEvidence: The local attacker must have write access to the actual selected directory. Ordinary authorized --force behavior alone is not a vulnerability.
recordPlan/_record intentionally resolve an explicitly selected plan symlink; the independently attacker-planted partial symlink is the vulnerability.

finding.title: Python and npm CLIs can overwrite unrelated files through output and staging symlinks
finding.summary: Both filesystem CLI adapters check whether an output exists, then open its pathname for a truncating write. def cmd_diff(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    """Text only, as in the native CLI: the patch, a text view, or (two
    Markdown documents) CriticMarkup, on stdout or in -o's file."""
    from . import _native
    from .document import _decode_diff

    output = args.output
    # An existing output is refused before any work.
    if output is not None:
        _ensure_writable(output, args.force)
    old = _read_side(args.old, args.old_format)
    new = _read_side(args.new, args.new_format)
    if args.format in ("github", "word", "normal", "context", "side-by-side"):
        text = _native.diff_view(old, new, format=args.format, old_name=_spelled(args, "old"), new_name=_spelled(args, "new"),
                                 context=args.context, accept_changes=args.accept_changes, full_lines=args.full_lines)
    else:
        critic = args.format == "critic"
        if critic and not (isinstance(old, str) and isinstance(new, str)):
            raise CliError("--format critic needs both documents in Markdown; "
                           "`jubarte compare OLD NEW` prints their redline as the agent view")
        # The shared parser dated the run (D17).
        text = _decode_diff(_native.diff_json(old, new, old_name=_spelled(args, "old"), new_name=_spelled(args, "new"),
                                              author=args.author, date=args.datetime, columns=args.columns, critic=critic)).text
    if output is None:
        sys.stdout.write(text)
        return EXIT_OK
    size = _write(output, text)

codeEvidence.label: Diff output argument reaches publication
codeEvidence.code:
def cmd_diff(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    """Text only, as in the native CLI: the patch, a text view, or (two
    Markdown documents) CriticMarkup, on stdout or in -o's file."""
    from . import _native
    from .document import _decode_diff

    output = args.output
    # An existing output is refused before any work.
    if output is not None:
        _ensure_writable(output, args.force)
    old = _read_side(args.old, args.old_format)
    new = _read_side(args.new, args.new_format)
    if args.format in ("github", "word", "normal", "context", "side-by-side"):
        text = _native.diff_view(old, new, format=args.format, old_name=_spelled(args, "old"), new_name=_spelled(args, "new"),
                                 context=args.context, accept_changes=args.accept_changes, full_lines=args.full_lines)
    else:
        critic = args.format == "critic"
        if critic and not (isinstance(old, str) and isinstance(new, str)):
            raise CliError("--format critic needs both documents in Markdown; "
                           "`jubarte compare OLD NEW` prints their redline as the agent view")
        # The shared parser dated the run (D17).
        text = _decode_diff(_native.diff_json(old, new, old_name=_spelled(args, "old"), new_name=_spelled(args, "new"),
                                              author=args.author, date=args.datetime, columns=args.columns, critic=critic)).text
    if output is None:
        sys.stdout.write(text)
        return EXIT_OK
    size = _write(output, text)
