rootCause.summary:
Python/npm direct-output authorization is a non-atomic exists check followed by a symlink-following truncating write. Python plan recording separately derives a predictable PID partial and opens it without exclusive/no-follow semantics. Intentional resolution of the caller-selected plan target does not authorize an attacker-planted partial entry. The separate npm plan-staging instance is cross-referenced rather than absorbed.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: No-overwrite authorization is implemented as exists()/existsSync() preflight, while final writes follow and truncate the current destination. The final open is neither exclusive nor bound to a staged file/held destination parent.

previousFindings.remediation: Publish Python/Node ordinary outputs, bundles and reports through held-directory authority and exclusive private staging. Atomically install without replacement when --force is false, or atomically replace the authorized destination entry when true; never truncate through a mutable final pathname. Apply exclusive unpredictable regular-file staging beside the authorized target to Python plan recording. Node recordPlan staging retains its separately established repair and identity.

counterEvidence: The local attacker must have write access to the actual selected directory. Ordinary authorized --force behavior alone is not a vulnerability.
recordPlan/_record intentionally resolve an explicitly selected plan symlink; the independently attacker-planted partial symlink is the vulnerability.

Assigned parent verified both ordinary output helpers and Python plan staging. Preview validates the edit, not the filesystem object opened. Native Rust publication and MCP use separate hardened capability/staging controls. The same assigned source also verifies npm recordPlan, whose exact staging tuple is retained under symlink-following.plan-staging.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration (preserved Standard static assessment, not reducer verification): Confirmed Python cmd_diff checks before input processing and later calls _write, whose Path.write_bytes follows current symlinks; Node ensureWritable/write implements the same split. Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed diff routes check the output before reading inputs and computing results, then call the unguarded common writer. The affected writer also serves comparison, conversion, PNG/report/font-report products, revision results, edit/visual-diff bundles, field-update reports and repair outputs.
Assigned discovery-0017 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Python checks output at lines 740-741, renders at 742, then calls its pathname writer at 757; Node performs the same sequence at 149-152. Neither writer receives or enforces the force policy. Existing symlinks to files are usually caught before rendering, but this does not protect against replacement afterwards. A same-directory attacker's ability to replace an entry does not imply permission to modify the symlink's external referent.

findings.title: Cyclic Markdown drawing dependencies terminate conversion through unbounded recursion
findings.summary: A drawing: image destination in ordinary Markdown is base64-decoded and deserialized into a dependency graph without validation. Package materialization recursively follows each dep.rels.part before writing the dependent part and has no active-node or completed-node map. A one-node self-reference causes indefinite recursion and stack exhaustion, even with default Markdown conversion options and no image loader. Header/footer drawing payloads also reach this same materializer through view_stories::story_part. Capture memoizes a part before descending, so even capture-produced envelopes can encode a cycle; capture count/byte limits do not establish an acyclic imported graph.

severity.rationale: Medium process-availability impact with high likelihood when an application processes attacker-controlled document bytes. No remote service or host-wide compromise is assumed.
severity.changeConditions: Shared in-process deployments may suffer broader availability loss; external process resource limits contain host impact but still permit worker termination.

confidence.rationale: Independent parent source tracing confirms the entrypoint, attacker-controlled dataflow, ineffective control and sensitive operation. No application code or exploit was executed.

rootCause.summary:
Imported integer-indexed dependency graphs are recursively materialized without cycle detection, node memoization or depth limits. Capture-side limits and index memoization are not enforced on imported graphs. A self-cycle uses flat JSON integer indexes and is not constrained by serde nesting. Equality/deduplication occurs after recursion; a graph traversal state must precede it.
The corroborating source makes the output-name countercontrol explicit: name_for stops after 998 alternatives and still returns a name, so it does not stop a self-edge; package byte-equality reuse at drawing.rs:1998 is after recursive children. Out-of-range dependency indices return None, whereas an in-range cycle passes.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: Imported drawing graphs are accepted by serde deserialization without validating acyclicity, and dep_part recurses before recording completed materialization or checking visiting state/depth.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): The deserialization boundary accepts arbitrary graph edges, while materialization assumes acyclic capture output and tracks names rather than graph traversal state.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): The writer accepts `drawing:` destinations and stores the decoded Drawing. `decode` validates base64/JSON syntax but not dependency edges or graph budgets. `materialize` dispatches top-level part indices to `dep_part`, which recursively traverses every in-range dependency without a visiting set, depth guard or memoized reconstruction. Capture-side MAX_DEPS/MAX_DEP_RELS/MAX_DEP_BYTES do not validate decoded Markdown.
Assigned discovery-0023 corroboration: `picture` recognizes a caller-authored `drawing:` destination and `decode` base64-decodes it into serde graph structs. Package assembly invokes `materialize`, which follows a root `part` index into `deps`. `dep_part` reserves a fresh name and clones XML, then follows every dependent `part` index by calling itself before writing or memoizing the current part. A root pointing to dependency 0 whose own relationship points to 0 repeats indefinitely. Capture's 64-part limits are not validated by decode and would not rule out a one-node cycle anyway.

findings.remediation: Validate dependency indices, count/byte/depth limits and graph shape at import. Materialize with an active/completed traversal state and index-to-output map, rejecting cycles or reserving identities to support cycles without recursive expansion. Memoize shared subgraphs. Enforce explicit dependency-edge and traversal-work budgets before assembly; when rejecting active-node revisits return a typed conversion refusal. Apply the same graph validation and traversal state to header/footer drawing materialization, not only body drawings.

validation.summary:
Parent verified Drawing/PayRel/Dep deserialization shapes, direct image import, public markdown_to_docx -> package assembly -> materialize and recursive dep_part. A top rel to dependency0 and dependency0 rel to itself never reaches the post-traversal write/return. name_for's collision loop still returns a name and does not terminate graph traversal.
The additional validated source explicitly represents the self-cycle as flat integer references, so serde JSON nesting limits do not help. The root and child both select dependency zero; recursion precedes XML/base64 output, package equality or part deduplication.
Assigned discovery-0009 corroboration (preserved offline Standard validation): Verified write.rs:86/108 and :4189-4197, xml.rs:2058-2083, package.rs:1703-1712 and drawing.rs:1397-1408/1889-2007. A one-node in-range cycle passes JSON shape checks and recursively revisits the same index indefinitely. The output-name loop terminates after 998 alternatives and still recurses, so name allocation is no cycle guard.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration (preserved Standard static assessment, not reducer verification): Independently verified drawing JSON structs accept index relationships, decode has no graph validation, picture stores the drawing, package assembly calls materialize, and dep_part recursively follows in-range indices. A one-node self-reference always passes the index guard. Output-name collision handling does not stop recursion.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Parent verified Drawing/PayRel serde defaults (73-135), decode (1397-1408), writer image dispatch (4183-4201), package dispatch (1697-1712), materialize (1881-1905) and dep_part (1956-2007). A top-level rel.part=0 and deps[0].rels[0].part=0 enters the same index indefinitely before writing. The graph is flat JSON, not deep JSON nesting.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): A flat JSON graph containing one dependency with rel.part=0, reached by a top-level rel.part=0, passes index checks and immediately recurses on the same node forever. Serde's JSON nesting limit does not bound cycles represented as integer indices. `used` tracks output names, not visited dependency indices; late byte deduplication occurs only after recursive descent.
Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed a graph with one dependency and a self-referencing part index is accepted by decode and recursively revisited without a terminating condition. Public conversion assembles the package before any post-conversion revision processing. No test or triggering input was run.
Assigned discovery-0023 corroboration: Confirmed markdown_to_docx -> read/picture -> package::assemble/drawing -> materialize -> dep_part. Bounds checks prove indices exist but do not establish acyclicity. `used` is a name-collision set rather than a graph-visit set. serde recursion limits concern nested JSON, not integer graph cycles.

finding.summary: A Markdown image with a `drawing:` payload can provide a self-referential dependency index. `markdown_to_docx()` accepts the decoded graph and `dep_part()` recurses without cycle or depth checks, exhausting the process stack before returning an error.

severity.rationale: A document supplier can reliably deny availability of the conversion process through the public default parser boundary. No privileges, network exposure or deployment were assumed; impact is process availability rather than code execution or disclosure.

codeEvidence.label: Capture memoizes before recursion
codeEvidence.explanation: The DOCX capture side tracks indexes, unlike the inverse materializer; its count cap does not make the graph acyclic.

rootCause.summary: `picture()` accepts the image destination as an encoded `Drawing`; `decode()` performs only base64/JSON decoding, preserving arbitrary `rels[].part` indexes. Package assembly calls `materialize()`, which enters `dep_part()` for any in-range root index. Each dependent relation invokes `dep_part()` again for any in-range child index without an in-progress set or depth bound. A child pointing back to index zero therefore recurses forever; the `used` set only renames parts and cannot break the cycle.

finding.remediation: Validate the decoded dependency graph before materialization; track in-progress and completed dependency indexes, reject cycles and enforce depth/work budgets, and memoize each completed part for shared DAGs.

counterEvidence: Capture uses a memoized index and caps dependent parts/relations, but decode/materialize do not enforce acyclicity; a one-node graph fits all count limits.
Package part equality is checked only after recursive traversal; it cannot stop self-reference.
limitations: No application execution or crash reproduction; no remote service deployment established.
validation.summary: A flat JSON envelope with one root relation to dependency zero and dependency zero relating to itself passes the only index bounds checks. Recursive descent occurs before base64/XML output or deduplication, so even a small input reaches nonterminating recursion. Capture limits and serde JSON nesting limits do not constrain a cycle represented as flat integer indexes.

rootCause.summary: `markdown_to_docx()` reads image destinations and accepts a caller-supplied `drawing:` envelope. `decode()` deserializes its flat dependency vector and `part` indices without graph validation. Package assembly invokes `materialize()`, which follows a top-level index into `dep_part()`. Each nested in-range index recursively invokes `dep_part()` again. The `used` set tracks renamed package files, so it neither detects an active index nor memoizes completed graph nodes; a self-edge never reaches the later byte comparison or package write.

finding.remediation: Validate dependency graphs and budgets at drawing decode/materialization. Reject active-node revisits with a typed conversion error, memoize completed dependency indices, and enforce total dependency, edge, byte and traversal budgets before output assembly.

counterEvidence: Out-of-range indices return None.
MAX_DEPS/MAX_DEP_RELS bound capture from DOCX, but are not applied by decode and do not prevent even a single-node cycle.
The package byte-equality reuse check at drawing.rs:1998 runs after recursive children and is unreachable for cycles.
limitations: No application execution, crash probe or tests.
validation.summary: Verified write.rs:86/108 and :4189-4197, xml.rs:2058-2083, package.rs:1703-1712 and drawing.rs:1397-1408/1889-2007. finding.title: A cyclic Markdown drawing payload causes unbounded dependency recursion
finding.summary: A Markdown author can supply a `drawing:` image payload with a dependency pointing back to itself. Base64/JSON decoding accepts the graph and package reconstruction recursively follows it without cycle detection, exhausting the stack and host resources.

severity.rationale: Attacker-controlled parser input can deny availability through disproportionate work or allocation in default public paths. Impact is process availability with high likelihood for a crafted input; no remote exposure, confidentiality loss or code execution is assumed.
severity.changeConditions: A disposable process with strict CPU/memory budgets reduces application-level impact; shared long-lived processing increases it.

confidence.rationale: Independent static source trace confirms the input-to-sink control gap and strongest counterevidence; no application or exploit execution was performed.

codeEvidence.label: Markdown accepts drawing destination
codeEvidence.explanation: A caller-supplied drawing URL decodes to stored content instead of ordinary alt text.

codeEvidence.label: Syntax-only Drawing decoding
codeEvidence.explanation: Base64 is parsed as a Drawing without validating graph topology or graph budgets.

codeEvidence.label: Package reconstruction materializes graph
codeEvidence.explanation: Stored attacker Drawing reaches materialize during DOCX emission.

codeEvidence.label: Top-level part index starts traversal
codeEvidence.explanation: An in-range index dispatches directly to dep_part; no traversal state is established.

codeEvidence.label: Recursive dependency traversal
codeEvidence.explanation: Each in-range inner index recurses, including an edge to its own currently active node.

codeEvidence.label: Capture-side bounds
codeEvidence.explanation: Constants describe bounded capture, but decode does not apply them to attacker-crafted graphs.

rootCause.summary: The writer accepts `drawing:` destinations and stores the decoded Drawing. `decode` validates base64/JSON syntax but not dependency edges or graph budgets. `materialize` dispatches top-level part indices to `dep_part`, which recursively traverses every in-range dependency without a visiting set, depth guard or memoized reconstruction. Capture-side MAX_DEPS/MAX_DEP_RELS/MAX_DEP_BYTES do not validate decoded Markdown.

finding.remediation: Validate decoded graph size, edge indices, aggregate bytes and cycles before materialization; use bounded traversal with visiting/visited states and memoize completed dependency materialization.

counterEvidence: Invalid base64/JSON becomes alt text, but a well-formed flat graph is accepted.
Capture from DOCX has bounds, which do not apply to crafted decoding. No external relationships or code execution are needed.
limitations: Static-only validation; no runtime measurement or deployed embedding assessment.
validation.summary: A flat JSON graph containing one dependency with rel.part=0, reached by a top-level rel.part=0, passes index checks and immediately recurses on the same node forever. Serde's JSON nesting limit does not bound cycles represented as integer indices. `used` tracks output names, not visited dependency indices; late byte deduplication occurs only after recursive descent.

finding.title: Converting a Markdown drawing with cyclic dependencies aborts the process
finding.summary: An attacker who supplies Markdown to `markdown_to_docx` can encode a `drawing:` payload whose internal part relationship points back to itself. Materialization recursively follows the index without a visiting set or depth bound, exhausting the stack and terminating the conversion host.

severity.rationale: A small attacker-controlled input reliably reaches an unbounded recursive parser operation. The supported impact is availability loss of the conversion process; a shared long-lived host must accept untrusted Markdown for cross-user disruption.
severity.changeConditions: A one-shot isolated CLI worker limits the impact; a shared long-lived conversion service increases it. No remote deployment is assumed.

confidence.rationale: The public input, base64/JSON decoding, package materialization and unconditional recursive edge are directly source-established; no runtime payload was executed.

codeEvidence.label: Public Markdown conversion input
codeEvidence.explanation: A library caller supplies the Markdown string, so input from a lower-trust document producer can reach this boundary without filesystem privileges.

codeEvidence.label: Drawing destinations deserialize without graph validation
codeEvidence.explanation: The destination controls deserialized Drawing.rels and Drawing.deps, including numeric part indexes. JSON nesting protection cannot detect a cycle expressed by indexes.

codeEvidence.label: Accepted drawing is stored for package output
codeEvidence.explanation: Successfully decoded input becomes a Content::Drawing item; it is not restricted to payloads previously generated by the product.

codeEvidence.label: Internal index starts recursive materialization
codeEvidence.explanation: A top-level relationship with part=0 and no external URL reaches the first attacker-controlled dependency.

codeEvidence.label: Dependency index is recursively followed without a cycle guard
codeEvidence.explanation: A dependency whose relationship also has part=0 repeatedly invokes the same index. The used set tracks output names and never checks active dependency indexes. No bytes are written or duplicate-part reuse checked until recursion returns.

codeEvidence.label: Header/footer drawing materialization shares the vulnerable graph traversal
codeEvidence.explanation: Header/footer scalars can also look up drawing payloads and invoke the same materialize/dep_part graph traversal, so body-only fixes would miss this entrypoint.

rootCause.summary: `Drawing` deserialization accepts internal relationship indexes from a Markdown destination. `Writer::picture` stores the graph and `PartRelate::drawing` calls `materialize`. Each internal edge invokes `dep_part`, which reserves a name and follows further indexes before storing the part. It lacks an active-index set, memoization or recursion budget, so a self-edge never reaches the later byte-deduplication check.

finding.remediation: Validate decoded dependency graphs and materialize with a visiting/complete state per dependency index. Reject cycles with a recoverable MarkdownError and enforce depth, part-count and aggregate-byte budgets before traversal.

counterEvidence: MAX_DEPS, MAX_DEP_RELS and MAX_DEP_BYTES bound DOCX-to-Markdown capture, not Drawing decode or materialization.
The output-name used set and later byte deduplication do not detect active graph cycles.
The repository recommends process limits; those constrain the failure to a process but do not turn stack exhaustion into a recoverable conversion error.
limitations: Static validation only; no shared service deployment or exploit runtime was assumed.
validation.summary: Confirmed a graph with one dependency and a self-referencing part index is accepted by decode and recursively revisited without a terminating condition. Public conversion assembles the package before any post-conversion revision processing. No test or triggering input was run.

dataflow.summary: Markdown string -> Writer::picture -> drawing::decode -> Content::Drawing -> package assembly -> PartRelate::drawing -> materialize -> dep_part -> same dep_part index indefinitely.

impact.why: Denial of service to the conversion process.

likelihood.why: A single small graph cycle deterministically reaches the recursive edge without a depth or cycle guard.

reachability.summary: Reachable through the public Markdown-to-DOCX library/parser boundary. The attacker needs control of converted Markdown, not server configuration or output paths. Header/footer drawing payloads also reach the same materializer through view_stories::story_part.
reachability.outcome: Stack exhaustion and process termination.
preconditions: A host converts Markdown supplied by an attacker.

attackPath.summary: Supply a Markdown image with a base64 JSON drawing envelope that points to dependency 0, whose own relationship also points to 0, then request Markdown-to-DOCX conversion.

remediationTests: Reject a one-node self-cycle and a two-node cycle without aborting the process.
Preserve shared acyclic dependencies and reject over-budget dependency graphs.

rootCause.summary:
Imported integer-indexed dependency graphs are recursively materialized without cycle detection, node memoization or depth limits. Capture-side limits and index memoization are not enforced on imported graphs. A self-cycle uses flat JSON integer indexes and is not constrained by serde nesting. Equality/deduplication occurs after recursion; a graph traversal state must precede it.
The corroborating source makes the output-name countercontrol explicit: name_for stops after 998 alternatives and still returns a name, so it does not stop a self-edge; package byte-equality reuse at drawing.rs:1998 is after recursive children. Out-of-range dependency indices return None, whereas an in-range cycle passes.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: Imported drawing graphs are accepted by serde deserialization without validating acyclicity, and dep_part recurses before recording completed materialization or checking visiting state/depth.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): The deserialization boundary accepts arbitrary graph edges, while materialization assumes acyclic capture output and tracks names rather than graph traversal state.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): The writer accepts `drawing:` destinations and stores the decoded Drawing. `decode` validates base64/JSON syntax but not dependency edges or graph budgets. `materialize` dispatches top-level part indices to `dep_part`, which recursively traverses every in-range dependency without a visiting set, depth guard or memoized reconstruction. Capture-side MAX_DEPS/MAX_DEP_RELS/MAX_DEP_BYTES do not validate decoded Markdown.

Enforce explicit dependency-edge and traversal-work budgets before assembly; when rejecting active-node revisits return a typed conversion refusal.

validation.summary:
Parent verified Drawing/PayRel/Dep deserialization shapes, direct image import, public markdown_to_docx -> package assembly -> materialize and recursive dep_part. A top rel to dependency0 and dependency0 rel to itself never reaches the post-traversal write/return. name_for's collision loop still returns a name and does not terminate graph traversal.
The additional validated source explicitly represents the self-cycle as flat integer references, so serde JSON nesting limits do not help. The root and child both select dependency zero; recursion precedes XML/base64 output, package equality or part deduplication.
Assigned discovery-0009 corroboration (preserved offline Standard validation): Verified write.rs:86/108 and :4189-4197, xml.rs:2058-2083, package.rs:1703-1712 and drawing.rs:1397-1408/1889-2007. A one-node in-range cycle passes JSON shape checks and recursively revisits the same index indefinitely. The output-name loop terminates after 998 alternatives and still recurses, so name allocation is no cycle guard.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration (preserved Standard static assessment, not reducer verification): Independently verified drawing JSON structs accept index relationships, decode has no graph validation, picture stores the drawing, package assembly calls materialize, and dep_part recursively follows in-range indices. A one-node self-reference always passes the index guard. Output-name collision handling does not stop recursion.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Parent verified Drawing/PayRel serde defaults (73-135), decode (1397-1408), writer image dispatch (4183-4201), package dispatch (1697-1712), materialize (1881-1905) and dep_part (1956-2007). A top-level rel.part=0 and deps[0].rels[0].part=0 enters the same index indefinitely before writing. The graph is flat JSON, not deep JSON nesting.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): A flat JSON graph containing one dependency with rel.part=0, reached by a top-level rel.part=0, passes index checks and immediately recurses on the same node forever. Serde's JSON nesting limit does not bound cycles represented as integer indices. `used` tracks output names, not visited dependency indices; late byte deduplication occurs only after recursive descent.

rootCause.summary:
Imported integer-indexed dependency graphs are recursively materialized without cycle detection, node memoization or depth limits. Capture-side limits and index memoization are not enforced on imported graphs. A self-cycle uses flat JSON integer indexes and is not constrained by serde nesting. Equality/deduplication occurs after recursion; a graph traversal state must precede it.
The corroborating source makes the output-name countercontrol explicit: name_for stops after 998 alternatives and still returns a name, so it does not stop a self-edge; package byte-equality reuse at drawing.rs:1998 is after recursive children. Out-of-range dependency indices return None, whereas an in-range cycle passes.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: Imported drawing graphs are accepted by serde deserialization without validating acyclicity, and dep_part recurses before recording completed materialization or checking visiting state/depth.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): The deserialization boundary accepts arbitrary graph edges, while materialization assumes acyclic capture output and tracks names rather than graph traversal state.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): The writer accepts `drawing:` destinations and stores the decoded Drawing. `decode` validates base64/JSON syntax but not dependency edges or graph budgets. `materialize` dispatches top-level part indices to `dep_part`, which recursively traverses every in-range dependency without a visiting set, depth guard or memoized reconstruction. Capture-side MAX_DEPS/MAX_DEP_RELS/MAX_DEP_BYTES do not validate decoded Markdown.

previousFindings.remediation: Validate dependency indices, count/byte/depth limits and graph shape at import. Materialize with an active/completed traversal state and index-to-output map, rejecting cycles or reserving identities to support cycles without recursive expansion. Memoize shared subgraphs. Enforce explicit dependency-edge and traversal-work budgets before assembly; when rejecting active-node revisits return a typed conversion refusal. Apply the same graph validation and traversal state to header/footer drawing materialization, not only body drawings.

validation.summary:
Parent verified Drawing/PayRel/Dep deserialization shapes, direct image import, public markdown_to_docx -> package assembly -> materialize and recursive dep_part. A top rel to dependency0 and dependency0 rel to itself never reaches the post-traversal write/return. name_for's collision loop still returns a name and does not terminate graph traversal.
The additional validated source explicitly represents the self-cycle as flat integer references, so serde JSON nesting limits do not help. The root and child both select dependency zero; recursion precedes XML/base64 output, package equality or part deduplication.
Assigned discovery-0009 corroboration (preserved offline Standard validation): Verified write.rs:86/108 and :4189-4197, xml.rs:2058-2083, package.rs:1703-1712 and drawing.rs:1397-1408/1889-2007. A one-node in-range cycle passes JSON shape checks and recursively revisits the same index indefinitely. The output-name loop terminates after 998 alternatives and still recurses, so name allocation is no cycle guard.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration (preserved Standard static assessment, not reducer verification): Independently verified drawing JSON structs accept index relationships, decode has no graph validation, picture stores the drawing, package assembly calls materialize, and dep_part recursively follows in-range indices. A one-node self-reference always passes the index guard. Output-name collision handling does not stop recursion.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Parent verified Drawing/PayRel serde defaults (73-135), decode (1397-1408), writer image dispatch (4183-4201), package dispatch (1697-1712), materialize (1881-1905) and dep_part (1956-2007). A top-level rel.part=0 and deps[0].rels[0].part=0 enters the same index indefinitely before writing. The graph is flat JSON, not deep JSON nesting.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): A flat JSON graph containing one dependency with rel.part=0, reached by a top-level rel.part=0, passes index checks and immediately recurses on the same node forever. Serde's JSON nesting limit does not bound cycles represented as integer indices. `used` tracks output names, not visited dependency indices; late byte deduplication occurs only after recursive descent.
Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed a graph with one dependency and a self-referencing part index is accepted by decode and recursively revisited without a terminating condition. Public conversion assembles the package before any post-conversion revision processing. No test or triggering input was run.

findings.title: Public Strict-format probe inflates unbounded document headers
findings.summary: The public main_part_is_strict helper reads word/document.xml without admission or an inflation/preamble cap. A compressible oversized/unfinished root opening tag or long XML comment keeps the last '<' at offset zero; the full growing head remains retained and is repeatedly scanned until the root tag completes or EOF, allowing memory/CPU exhaustion for direct library consumers. rootCause.summary:
Public ZIP-reading sibling bypasses admission and assumes bytes since the last '<' remain small, without bounding an individual opening tag. The same accumulating buffer is unbounded during comments as well as a root opening tag: rposition('<') remains zero, drain(..0) drops nothing, and root_open scans the entire retained preamble after every 16 KiB read.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): A boolean format probe bypasses package resource admission and assumes retaining bytes since the last < bounds state; a long comment invalidates that assumption.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `main_part_is_strict()` opens word/document.xml directly. It appends decompressed chunks to `head` until finding `>`, then retains from the last `<`. With an unfinished root tag followed by a long whitespace run, that position remains zero and no bytes are discarded.
Assigned discovery-0023 corroboration: `main_part_is_strict` opens the ZIP and `word/document.xml` directly, then reads the part in chunks into `head`. While an opening tag contains only its initial '<' and no '>', draining before the last '<' removes nothing. Each read therefore increases retained decompressed bytes and repeats delimiter scans across the accumulated tag. A highly compressible long run of spaces within the root tag reaches both unbounded memory growth and superlinear scanning before a boolean is returned.

findings.remediation: Apply bounded admission before indexing/inflation and explicit cumulative inflated-byte/preamble/work limits to this public helper. Use a streaming lexical probe with bounded retained state for comments, declarations and chunk-spanning root tags; refuse excessive probes with a checked/limited API and safe default limits.

rootCause.summary: `main_part_is_strict` opens the ZIP and `word/document.xml` directly, then reads the part in chunks into `head`. rootCause.summary:
`parse_font_table_xml()` stores attacker-selected distinct names and embedded relationship IDs. After physical package admission, `with_layout()` calls `load_embedded_fonts()` for every table row. Each unknown alias resolves the same part, calls `deobfuscate_odttf()` which immediately copies all bytes, then stores a new allocation keyed by alias/style. No resolved-part cache or aggregate decoded-font budget shares or bounds repeated copies.
Fonts::for_document subsequently visits every retained alias; its later u16 face-index conversion does not prevent already retained per-alias payload copies.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): A physical resource charged once by package admission is decoded and cloned into independent Arc allocations per attacker-chosen family/style alias without aggregate accounting.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `with_layout()` loads the whole font table before collecting used names. For every unknown family/style, `load_embedded_fonts()` resolves the part, copies/deobfuscates its entire bytes, validates it and inserts a new retained allocation. Aliases sharing a target have no deduplication or aggregate byte cap.

findings.remediation:
Cache decoded font buffers by resolved package part and effective obfuscation key, share Arc values across aliases, and enforce an aggregate decoded-font allocation/work budget before copying.
Enforce face-count limits before decoding/retention and load only used faces where possible; cover all four style slots and different effective keys.

validation.method: Preserve supplied already-validated Standard evidence and source-specific assessments. Serial artifact-only semantic remediation-subsumption reduction; no new repository/dependency inspection, validation, execution or attack-path analysis.
validation.summary:
A valid ordinary font can be referenced by thousands of differently named `w:font` rows using the same `r:id`. The names need not occur in runs. Unknown family names bypass the installed-catalogue optimization and valid font parsing succeeds for every copy. Ten thousand aliases of an approximately 320 KB font request roughly 3.2 GB of retained payload bytes while archive admission charges the original part once.
Assigned discovery-0008 corroboration: Independently traced DOCX fontTable unique names sharing embed r:id/key -> load_embedded_fonts loops every entry -> deobfuscate_odttf bytes.to_vec -> new Arc per alias -> retained EmbeddedFonts -> Fonts::for_document.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Parent read font table parse (76-129), plain/deobfuscation cloning (179-193), full embedded loader (205-232) and with_layout ordering (806-809). Names are not required to match internal font family or be used in document text. One ~1MiB valid font with 10000 distinct names can request ~10GiB retained bytes while physical input remains a few MiB.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Verified catalogue-known families are skipped but arbitrary distinct unknown names are accepted, plain sfnt data is allowed, and every alias can reference the same valid part. Unique keys retain all copies; the later extra-face index cap occurs after loading. Admission counts the physical part once, not aliases times font size.
Assigned discovery-0017 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Distinct family names produce distinct table entries. Non-catalogue aliases can share a single valid TTF relationship; plain sfnt input is still cloned by deobfuscate_odttf. Face::parse validates format, then data.into() transfers each separate Vec into the retained map. Rendering loads that map unconditionally and borrows it through Fonts::for_document. Native installed-font lookup does not retroactively bound allocations already retained.

rootCause.summary: `parse_font_table_xml()` stores attacker-selected distinct names and embedded relationship IDs. rootCause.summary:
`parse_font_table_xml()` stores attacker-selected distinct names and embedded relationship IDs. After physical package admission, `with_layout()` calls `load_embedded_fonts()` for every table row. Each unknown alias resolves the same part, calls `deobfuscate_odttf()` which immediately copies all bytes, then stores a new allocation keyed by alias/style. No resolved-part cache or aggregate decoded-font budget shares or bounds repeated copies.
Fonts::for_document subsequently visits every retained alias; its later u16 face-index conversion does not prevent already retained per-alias payload copies.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): A physical resource charged once by package admission is decoded and cloned into independent Arc allocations per attacker-chosen family/style alias without aggregate accounting.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `with_layout()` loads the whole font table before collecting used names. For every unknown family/style, `load_embedded_fonts()` resolves the part, copies/deobfuscates its entire bytes, validates it and inserts a new retained allocation. Aliases sharing a target have no deduplication or aggregate byte cap.

previousFindings.remediation:
Cache decoded font buffers by resolved package part and effective obfuscation key, share Arc values across aliases, and enforce an aggregate decoded-font allocation/work budget before copying.
Enforce face-count limits before decoding/retention and load only used faces where possible; cover all four style slots and different effective keys.

validation.summary:
A valid ordinary font can be referenced by thousands of differently named `w:font` rows using the same `r:id`. The names need not occur in runs. Unknown family names bypass the installed-catalogue optimization and valid font parsing succeeds for every copy. Ten thousand aliases of an approximately 320 KB font request roughly 3.2 GB of retained payload bytes while archive admission charges the original part once.
Assigned discovery-0008 corroboration: Independently traced DOCX fontTable unique names sharing embed r:id/key -> load_embedded_fonts loops every entry -> deobfuscate_odttf bytes.to_vec -> new Arc per alias -> retained EmbeddedFonts -> Fonts::for_document.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Parent read font table parse (76-129), plain/deobfuscation cloning (179-193), full embedded loader (205-232) and with_layout ordering (806-809). Names are not required to match internal font family or be used in document text. One ~1MiB valid font with 10000 distinct names can request ~10GiB retained bytes while physical input remains a few MiB.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Verified catalogue-known families are skipped but arbitrary distinct unknown names are accepted, plain sfnt data is allowed, and every alias can reference the same valid part. Unique keys retain all copies; the later extra-face index cap occurs after loading. Admission counts the physical part once, not aliases times font size.
Assigned discovery-0017 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Distinct family names produce distinct table entries. Non-catalogue aliases can share a single valid TTF relationship; plain sfnt input is still cloned by deobfuscate_odttf. Face::parse validates format, then data.into() transfers each separate Vec into the retained map. Rendering loads that map unconditionally and borrows it through Fonts::for_document. Native installed-font lookup does not retroactively bound allocations already retained.

findings.title: Redacting a numeric identifier can leave its custom XML attribute intact
findings.summary: The final redaction leak scan exempts numeric-looking attributes by local name alone. A sensitive value such as a customer or account identifier in custom XML `id` is ignored, allowing visible redaction to succeed while the value remains recoverable in the returned DOCX.

rootCause.summary: Admission explicitly transcodes UTF-16LE/BE with a BOM, so bounded valid property XML is accepted. The metadata scrubber's `Part::load()` instead calls `part_string()`, which interprets original bytes as UTF-8 lossily. A UTF-16 BOM becomes replacement characters, not the Unicode BOM stripped by `parse_xdocument()`. The permissive parser stops before creating a root; `Part::load()` returns `None` and `scrub_properties()` silently skips the core/app fields. Unchanged raw bytes serialize back out, while the final general-validation comparison rejects only increased findings rather than failed privacy removal.

findings.remediation: Use a shared encoding-aware XML decoder for selected metadata parts, and fail closed when a selected part cannot be parsed or requested identifying values remain. Handle both UTF-16 endiannesses consistently with admission.

counterEvidence: Valid UTF-8 property XML follows the intended removal path.
Conventional custom.xml is removed by raw existence and is not affected by this encoding-specific path.
Admission still enforces XML limits; the problem is inconsistent decoding between admission and the privacy operation.

Even if the general validator reports a preexisting parsing finding, unchanged finding counts do not refuse `scrub()`.

rootCause.summary: Admission explicitly transcodes UTF-16LE/BE with a BOM, so bounded valid property XML is accepted. The metadata scrubber's `Part::load()` instead calls `part_string()`, which interprets original bytes as UTF-8 lossily. A UTF-16 BOM becomes replacement characters, not the Unicode BOM stripped by `parse_xdocument()`. The permissive parser stops before creating a root; `Part::load()` returns `None` and `scrub_properties()` silently skips the core/app fields. Unchanged raw bytes serialize back out, while the final general-validation comparison rejects only increased findings rather than failed privacy removal.

finding.remediation: Use a shared encoding-aware XML decoder for selected metadata parts, and fail closed when a selected part cannot be parsed or requested identifying values remain. Handle both UTF-16 endiannesses consistently with admission.

findings.title: Tiny Markdown table metadata can trigger unbounded cell allocation
findings.summary: A caller-controlled cells paragraph range is converted into an unbounded count and used to append padding cells. A tiny Markdown table with a range such as p0-p1000000000 causes roughly a billion padding entries to be allocated before DOCX assembly, exhausting CPU and memory in Rust, Python, or WASM conversion hosts. The new corroboration explicitly matches two metadata ranges to a header and data row without breaks; MOST_GRID=64 and arithmetic overflow checks do not bound these valid row counts.

severity.rationale: A small untrusted Markdown input can exhaust or terminate its processing host. Reachability is direct through public byte/string APIs; remote or multi-user service exposure is conditional, and there is no confidentiality or integrity compromise.
severity.changeConditions: Process memory/CPU limits and worker isolation constrain impact; a shared remotely exposed conversion service would increase operational impact.

confidence.rationale: Static source tracing establishes the unchecked numeric count, default public conversion path, and count-driven Vec growth; runtime exhaustion was deliberately not executed.

rootCause.summary:
DOCX gridSpan and imported HTML colspan are trusted as output column cardinalities with only a lower bound. Both document-table paths lack a shared grid/output budget before generation and allocation.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): The renderer accepts cell spans and row skips as unbounded machine integers and expands sparse semantic counts into dense vectors without checked cumulative arithmetic or an allocation budget. The sibling HTML importer lacks the same column budget and performs span-sized XML emission.
Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: The renderer treats document-controlled span counts as allocation sizes without a maximum semantic table width or checked aggregate occupancy. The HTML table importer likewise accepts unbounded colspan and materializes a grid proportional to it before DOM parsing.

findings.remediation: Enforce practical per-cell span/row-skip and checked cumulative table/grid/output budgets across direct OOXML gridSpan/gridBefore/gridAfter and HTML/MHT colspan. Neither importer-only nor later layout-only checking is sufficient. Use fallible allocation/reservation within those bounds so capacity failures become typed refusals. Carry the caller-configurable column/occupancy budget through every table source and enforce a generated-XML/output ceiling before altChunk materialization.

finding.title: Untrusted table spans cause unbounded renderer allocations
finding.summary: A small DOCX table can set w:gridSpan, w:gridBefore or w:gridAfter to a large usize. The shared PDF/PNG layout pipeline admits the package, derives column occupancy from these values, and allocates column and merge vectors at that size without a semantic budget. This can exhaust worker memory or panic before returning a normal conversion error. The HTML altChunk importer also accepts unbounded colspan and emits one gridCol per logical column.

severity.rationale: A document supplier can deterministically deny service to a process rendering the supplied file with very small input. Impact is availability of that process; no remote service or broader compromise is assumed, and process resource limits constrain host-wide impact.

confidence.rationale: Direct source trace from public conversion entry points through admission and uncapped attribute parsing to Vec allocation; no runtime exploit was executed.

taxonomy.category: Uncontrolled resource allocation from untrusted document metadata

codeEvidence.explanation: The return type (usize, VMerge) makes the parsed span an attacker-controlled usize; max(1) sets only a minimum.

codeEvidence.explanation: The same missing semantic-column budget affects HTML colspans before table DOM construction.

codeEvidence.label: One XML element emitted per logical column
codeEvidence.explanation: end_table computes cols as maximum sum of cell.span (469-475) and emits unchecked attacker-sized output.

rootCause.summary: The renderer accepts cell spans and row skips as unbounded machine integers and expands sparse semantic counts into dense vectors without checked cumulative arithmetic or an allocation budget. The sibling HTML importer lacks the same column budget and performs span-sized XML emission.

finding.remediation: Apply a conservative semantic maximum to cell spans, row skips and cumulative grid columns before creating RawCell or allocating vectors. Use checked cumulative arithmetic and return a typed resource-limit error before any span-derived loop/allocation. Enforce the same budget in every shared layout path. Apply this semantic maximum during HTML colspan parsing and table emission as well.

counterEvidence: Package admission enforces byte, ZIP entry, XML depth and attribute limits before layout; those checks accept short decimal span attributes.
stretch_stale_spans returns early when used spans exceed existing columns (14172-14177); it does not cap spans.
SECURITY.md recommends process CPU/memory isolation; that mitigates host impact but does not prevent termination of a rendering worker.
limitations: No application code executed; no claim of a deployed remotely accessible renderer.
validation.summary: Validated by reading the public PDF/render entry points (422-460,592-645), with_layout admission (769-799), table_block callers (8619,9178,17184,20598), span propagation (13200-13216,13466,13530-13536), allocation (13600-13619) and merge tracking (14600-14644). InputLimits fields (src/admission.rs:42-60) cover byte/entry/XML structural limits, not grid counts. Parent additionally validated HTML colspan parsing (altchunk.rs:562-566), sum (469-475) and 0..cols emission (489-490).

finding.title: DOCX and HTML table spans cause unbounded renderer expansion
finding.summary: A small DOCX can set w:gridSpan, w:gridBefore or w:gridAfter to an enormous positive integer. Rendering expands the table column vector to the attacker-provided occupancy without a semantic column budget, causing excessive allocation or a process-terminating allocation failure. ZIP size and XML nesting admission do not bound these numeric values. Internal HTML altChunk colspan values independently expand into one generated w:gridCol per requested column before the generated XML is parsed, bypassing the original package's byte budgets.

severity.rationale: An attacker who can supply a document to a rendering caller can reliably request allocations disproportionate to input size and terminate or exhaust that process. No authentication bypass, code execution, remote service deployment or host-wide outage is established.
severity.changeConditions: Process memory/CPU limits and per-request process isolation confine impact; a shared long-lived renderer increases availability impact.

confidence.rationale: Direct source traces the unbounded usize from XML through RawCell.colspan and occupancy into vec!/resize after admission. No runtime reproduction was performed.

codeEvidence.label: Unbounded table span from document XML
codeEvidence.explanation: The return type is usize; positive values have no upper bound.

codeEvidence.label: Row grid skip uses the same unchecked span
codeEvidence.explanation: Both gridBefore and gridAfter become RawCell.colspan at line 14379 and reach the same occupancy allocator.

codeEvidence.label: Occupancy directly sizes column storage
codeEvidence.explanation: A single span of 1,000,000,000 requests at least four billion bytes of f32 columns before later per-column allocations.

codeEvidence.label: Public rendering uses admission before table construction
codeEvidence.explanation: Ordinary valid small table XML is reachable through public PDF/PNG/render-report APIs; archive/XML admission does not cap table column values.

codeEvidence.label: HTML spans generate proportional XML without a budget
codeEvidence.explanation: The maximum row span sum drives generated XML size. The HTML parser accepts positive usize colspan without a maximum at lines 562-566; expansion is called after original package admission at convert/mod.rs:789-798.

rootCause.summary: The renderer treats document-controlled span counts as allocation sizes without a maximum semantic table width or checked aggregate occupancy. The HTML table importer likewise accepts unbounded colspan and materializes a grid proportional to it before DOM parsing.

finding.remediation: Introduce a configurable maximum table-column/occupancy budget, validate gridSpan/gridBefore/gridAfter before constructing cells, use checked_add for aggregate spans, and reject excessive values with a typed conversion error before allocating. Apply the same budget to all table sources. Enforce the same maximum during HTML altChunk parsing and checked row-span accumulation, and cap generated XML/output before materialization.

counterEvidence: Package admission runs first and rejects malformed/over-budget ZIP/XML; a tiny valid numeric span is within those checks.
SECURITY.md recommends process memory/CPU limits; these constrain blast radius but do not prevent request-triggered renderer termination.
limitations: No application execution, exploit input creation, or runtime memory measurement.
Actual shared-service deployment and isolation are unknown.
validation.summary: Parent verified the positive usize parser, row skip sibling, RawCell propagation, occupancy allocator and public with_layout entry path. Admission limits are byte/entry/depth/attribute budgets (src/admission.rs:42-99), not table-column bounds. Parent also verified altchunk::expand -> html_to_wml -> end_table, its positive usize colspan parser and unbounded gridCol generation. Both paths require the same semantic table-column budget; original package admission precedes HTML expansion.

dataflow.summary: DOCX bytes -> with_layout admission/normalization -> DOM body table -> table_block -> cell_span or row_grid_skip -> RawCell.colspan -> occupancy -> cols vec!/resize. Alternate path: internal altChunk relationship -> package HTML bytes -> html_to_wml colspan -> end_table gridCol loop -> generated XML -> DOM/layout.

rootCause.summary:
Duplicate reporting uses repaired.contains on a growing Vec even though first-occurrence lookup already uses a HashMap. Root and every part relationship set invoke this repair. N distinct IDs each duplicated identically require N(N-1)/2 prior-ID string comparisons despite first-occurrence hashing; byte/depth/attribute checks do not limit this product.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): An ordered report vector is also used as a membership set, so the first duplicate of each new ID scans all preceding repaired IDs.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): `read_relationships` preserves the record list and `PartFs::open_within` invokes `drop_repeated_relationships`. Its `seen` map finds duplicates efficiently, but each duplicate then uses `repaired.contains` over all previously repaired IDs. Repeating each of N distinct IDs twice requires roughly N(N-1)/2 string comparisons.
Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: The duplicate-repair result is used as a linear membership set inside an attacker-sized loop, producing quadratic work over valid identical-duplicate relationship records.

Optionally cap relationship-record/work totals before repair; test many distinct identical duplicate pairs while preserving deterministic repaired-ID order and conflicting-duplicate refusals. Apply an active relationship-record/work budget at metadata admission in addition to making duplicate membership near-linear.

finding.title: Identical relationship duplicate repair performs quadratic ID searches
finding.summary: OPC loading retains relationship records for duplicate repair. For each distinct duplicated ID, drop_repeated_relationships scans the entire growing repaired-ID vector even though a hash map already tracks original IDs. A modest relationship part with many identical duplicate pairs therefore triggers quadratic string comparisons before ordinary processing.

severity.rationale: An untrusted DOCX can impose billions of string comparisons within normal XML/ZIP byte limits, denying availability to its processing host.

rootCause.summary:
Duplicate reporting uses repaired.contains on a growing Vec even though first-occurrence lookup already uses a HashMap. Root and every part relationship set invoke this repair. N distinct IDs each duplicated identically require N(N-1)/2 prior-ID string comparisons despite first-occurrence hashing; byte/depth/attribute checks do not limit this product.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): An ordered report vector is also used as a membership set, so the first duplicate of each new ID scans all preceding repaired IDs.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): `read_relationships` preserves the record list and `PartFs::open_within` invokes `drop_repeated_relationships`. Its `seen` map finds duplicates efficiently, but each duplicate then uses `repaired.contains` over all previously repaired IDs. Repeating each of N distinct IDs twice requires roughly N(N-1)/2 string comparisons.

previousFindings.remediation: Track already-reported duplicate IDs in a HashSet or alongside seen-map state, retaining a Vec only for deterministic reporting order. Optionally cap relationship-record/work totals before repair; test many distinct identical duplicate pairs while preserving deterministic repaired-ID order and conflicting-duplicate refusals.

rootCause.summary:
Duplicate reporting uses repaired.contains on a growing Vec even though first-occurrence lookup already uses a HashMap. Root and every part relationship set invoke this repair. N distinct IDs each duplicated identically require N(N-1)/2 prior-ID string comparisons despite first-occurrence hashing; byte/depth/attribute checks do not limit this product.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): An ordered report vector is also used as a membership set, so the first duplicate of each new ID scans all preceding repaired IDs.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): `read_relationships` preserves the record list and `PartFs::open_within` invokes `drop_repeated_relationships`. Its `seen` map finds duplicates efficiently, but each duplicate then uses `repaired.contains` over all previously repaired IDs. Repeating each of N distinct IDs twice requires roughly N(N-1)/2 string comparisons.
Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: The duplicate-repair result is used as a linear membership set inside an attacker-sized loop, producing quadratic work over valid identical-duplicate relationship records.

previousFindings.remediation: Track already-reported duplicate IDs in a HashSet or alongside seen-map state, retaining a Vec only for deterministic reporting order. Optionally cap relationship-record/work totals before repair; test many distinct identical duplicate pairs while preserving deterministic repaired-ID order and conflicting-duplicate refusals. Apply an active relationship-record/work budget at metadata admission in addition to making duplicate membership near-linear.

finding.title: Unbounded numbering levels exhaust renderer CPU and memory
finding.summary: A DOCX paragraph may specify any u32 numbering level. Resolving an undefined large level searches every lower integer; defining that large level instead initializes a counter for every lower level and later scans each placeholder level. A tiny document can therefore trigger billions of iterations or counter entries after normal package admission.

severity.rationale: A document author can cause severe per-process availability loss through ordinary rendering. A shared remotely reachable service is not assumed.
severity.changeConditions: Per-request CPU/memory limits and process isolation bound the outage; shared rendering hosts increase availability impact.

confidence.rationale: Direct static source shows uncapped u32 input driving integer ranges and map allocation. The caller chain is list_marker -> next_revised -> next_marker/resolve_ilvl. Runtime reproduction was not performed.

codeEvidence.label: Unbounded document level
codeEvidence.explanation: No semantic maximum is enforced before callers resolve or iterate over the level.

codeEvidence.label: Integer-range fallback search
codeEvidence.code:

            .rev()
            .find(|i| lvls.contains_key(i))
            .unwrap_or(ilvl)
codeEvidence.explanation: With only level zero defined and ilvl 4294967295, this attempts roughly 4.3 billion lookups.

codeEvidence.label: Counters materialized for every lower integer
codeEvidence.explanation: Defining the attacker-selected large level avoids fallback but reaches this proportional map expansion.

rootCause.summary: Numbering metadata is accepted as arbitrary u32 and used as the extent of dense scans and counter materialization, without validating the supported level range.

finding.remediation: Validate numbering levels at every paragraph/style/abstract/override parse against the supported bounded range. Select existing lower levels by bounded/sparse map lookup rather than walking arbitrary integer ranges, and materialize only necessary bounded counters; return a typed error for unsupported metadata.

counterEvidence: Admission bounds compressed/inflated bytes and XML shape but not ilvl values.
An undefined list instance returns early; the attacker can include a normal matching num/abstractNum relationship.
Process isolation recommended in SECURITY.md can bound impact.
limitations: No runtime timing or allocation measurement; actual hosting deployment unknown.

validation.summary:
Independently traced DOCX paragraph w:numPr/w:ilvl -> num_pr -> numbering lookup -> resolve_ilvl reverse integer scan; defined high levels -> next_marker lower-level counter insertion and render loop.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration (preserved Standard static assessment, not reducer verification): Verified num_pr -> list_marker -> next_revised/next_marker -> resolve_ilvl. Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed a paragraph level 4,000,000,000 with only level zero defined causes about four billion parent-level probes. Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Traced paragraph numPr through list_marker/next_revised/next_marker to resolve_ilvl. A normal abstract list defining only level zero and a huge undefined requested level avoids the exact-key fast path and forces the reverse-range scan.
Assigned discovery-0017 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Paragraph numbering and style inheritance use num_pr without an ilvl cap (src/convert/mod.rs:12683-12718,12834-12879). An undefined u32-max paragraph level reaches resolve_ilvl's reverse scan with an ordinary level-zero parent. A defined high level bypasses that search but reaches the counters loop. Abstract levels and full overrides have no upper-bound check, so both paths remain reachable after admission.

findings.title: Entity decoding repeatedly scans the input suffix
findings.summary: HTML altChunk text with bare ampersands and the public XML entity decoder repeatedly search the remaining suffix for ';', yielding quadratic CPU work. A valid admitted .rels Target containing repeated & is normalized upstream and redundantly decoded by PartFs, reaching the same XML sink during rendering, inspection, revision processing or comparison even when the target part does not exist. An additional admitted-main-XML route uses an unquoted value whose first character never reappears: the DOM consumes through EOF and decodes a bare-ampersand comment as an attribute, reaching the same quadratic XML decoder. Ordinary bare-ampersand text is rejected upstream and is not this proof.

rootCause.summary:
Each unrecognized ampersand restarts an unbounded delimiter search; the HTML ten-character filter is applied after scanning the full suffix.
oxml-opc 0.14.2 returns normalized Target attributes using quick-xml 0.41; PartFs::resolve_rel_target assumes raw attributes and calls unescape_xml_text again. Repeated & in valid XML thus becomes consecutive bare ampersands before the second decoder. Target existence checks occur after resolution. Around one million decoded ampersands from roughly five MB of encoded input imply about 500 billion character inspections, a static operation estimate rather than a benchmark.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: unescape_xml_text rescans the remaining input for every unresolved ampersand, and the relationship adapter redundantly invokes it on values already decoded by its current OPC parser.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): The relationship consumer assumes raw attributes although its parser stores decoded values; its fallback entity scanner repeatedly scans the same suffix.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `Builder::text()` sends HTML text to `decode_entities()`. For every `&`, the decoder calls `tail.find(';')` on the remaining suffix and only then rejects positions over ten. Repeated ampersands without semicolons therefore cause quadratic scans. The assigned current-tree relationship round-trip assertion corroborates normalized targets independently of dependency-version assumptions, and the established internal story renderer resolves the target before checking whether the selected part exists.
Assigned discovery-0023 corroboration: `read_relationships` loads each record through oxml-opc, whose `parse_relationship` applies `decoded_and_normalized_value` before storing Target. Internal consumers pass that decoded string to `PartFs::resolve_rel_target`, which invokes `unescape_xml_text` again. For N escaped ampersands in source, the second pass sees N literal ampersands and no semicolons. Each failed semicolon search revisits the suffix, then advances by one, yielding N(N-1)/2 comparisons. Attribute count, XML depth and package byte limits do not bound this quadratic work adequately.
Assigned discovery-0022 adds tolerant HTML-style attribute boundaries versus DOM first-character-as-quote parsing: comment ampersands can become one large decoded attribute. This is an additional source path to the retained XML suffix-search root; no relationship resolution is required.

findings.remediation: Scan entities once without revisiting suffixes. In HTML, bound the search to the supported entity-length window before looking for ';'; give XML decoding a monotonic parser or bounded entity grammar. Remove PartFs's redundant relationship decoding when upstream supplies normalized attributes; retain the linear XML-helper repair for its other callers and the separate bounded HTML-helper repair. Preserve canonical literal '&' part names and one-time entity normalization through round trips. Preserve the standalone XML helper's documented permissive output for unsupported or unterminated references while making its work linear. Apply practical relationship-target length/work bounds as defense in depth, preserving exactly one normalization pass and the standalone helper's linear permissive behavior. Align admission/DOM attribute token boundaries or reject unsupported unquoted syntax as defense in depth. Preserve the linear XML decoder fix for this comment-to-attribute route; removing only the redundant relationship decode does not cover it.

PartFs::resolve_rel_target nevertheless passes that already-decoded target through unescape_xml_text again. A small compressed document can stall its processing worker.

severity.rationale: A document supplier can reach the decoder during normal rendering through internal header/footer/note relationships; no privileged options are required. severity.changeConditions: A shared processing service without worker CPU deadlines increases operational impact; eliminating the second decode or using a linear scanner removes the amplification.

confidence.rationale: Repository parser and round-trip tests establish that relationship targets are already XML-decoded. Current callers feed these decoded targets into the wrapper, and the decoder's nested suffix scans establish quadratic complexity. No runtime timing test was executed.

rootCause.summary:
Each unrecognized ampersand restarts an unbounded delimiter search; the HTML ten-character filter is applied after scanning the full suffix.
oxml-opc 0.14.2 returns normalized Target attributes using quick-xml 0.41; PartFs::resolve_rel_target assumes raw attributes and calls unescape_xml_text again. Repeated & in valid XML thus becomes consecutive bare ampersands before the second decoder. Target existence checks occur after resolution. Around one million decoded ampersands from roughly five MB of encoded input imply about 500 billion character inspections, a static operation estimate rather than a benchmark.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: unescape_xml_text rescans the remaining input for every unresolved ampersand, and the relationship adapter redundantly invokes it on values already decoded by its current OPC parser.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): The relationship consumer assumes raw attributes although its parser stores decoded values; its fallback entity scanner repeatedly scans the same suffix.

previousFindings.remediation: Scan entities once without revisiting suffixes. In HTML, bound the search to the supported entity-length window before looking for ';'; give XML decoding a monotonic parser or bounded entity grammar. Remove PartFs's redundant relationship decoding when upstream supplies normalized attributes; retain the linear XML-helper repair for its other callers and the separate bounded HTML-helper repair. Preserve canonical literal '&' part names and one-time entity normalization through round trips.

rootCause.summary:
Each unrecognized ampersand restarts an unbounded delimiter search; the HTML ten-character filter is applied after scanning the full suffix.
oxml-opc 0.14.2 returns normalized Target attributes using quick-xml 0.41; PartFs::resolve_rel_target assumes raw attributes and calls unescape_xml_text again. Repeated & in valid XML thus becomes consecutive bare ampersands before the second decoder. Target existence checks occur after resolution. Around one million decoded ampersands from roughly five MB of encoded input imply about 500 billion character inspections, a static operation estimate rather than a benchmark.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: unescape_xml_text rescans the remaining input for every unresolved ampersand, and the relationship adapter redundantly invokes it on values already decoded by its current OPC parser.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): The relationship consumer assumes raw attributes although its parser stores decoded values; its fallback entity scanner repeatedly scans the same suffix.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `Builder::text()` sends HTML text to `decode_entities()`. For every `&`, the decoder calls `tail.find(';')` on the remaining suffix and only then rejects positions over ten. Repeated ampersands without semicolons therefore cause quadratic scans.

previousFindings.remediation: Scan entities once without revisiting suffixes. In HTML, bound the search to the supported entity-length window before looking for ';'; give XML decoding a monotonic parser or bounded entity grammar. Remove PartFs's redundant relationship decoding when upstream supplies normalized attributes; retain the linear XML-helper repair for its other callers and the separate bounded HTML-helper repair. Preserve canonical literal '&' part names and one-time entity normalization through round trips.

rootCause.summary:
Each unrecognized ampersand restarts an unbounded delimiter search; the HTML ten-character filter is applied after scanning the full suffix.
oxml-opc 0.14.2 returns normalized Target attributes using quick-xml 0.41; PartFs::resolve_rel_target assumes raw attributes and calls unescape_xml_text again. Repeated & in valid XML thus becomes consecutive bare ampersands before the second decoder. Target existence checks occur after resolution. Around one million decoded ampersands from roughly five MB of encoded input imply about 500 billion character inspections, a static operation estimate rather than a benchmark.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: unescape_xml_text rescans the remaining input for every unresolved ampersand, and the relationship adapter redundantly invokes it on values already decoded by its current OPC parser.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): The relationship consumer assumes raw attributes although its parser stores decoded values; its fallback entity scanner repeatedly scans the same suffix.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `Builder::text()` sends HTML text to `decode_entities()`. For every `&`, the decoder calls `tail.find(';')` on the remaining suffix and only then rejects positions over ten. Repeated ampersands without semicolons therefore cause quadratic scans.

previousFindings.remediation: Scan entities once without revisiting suffixes. In HTML, bound the search to the supported entity-length window before looking for ';'; give XML decoding a monotonic parser or bounded entity grammar. Remove PartFs's redundant relationship decoding when upstream supplies normalized attributes; retain the linear XML-helper repair for its other callers and the separate bounded HTML-helper repair. Preserve canonical literal '&' part names and one-time entity normalization through round trips.

rootCause.summary:
Each unrecognized ampersand restarts an unbounded delimiter search; the HTML ten-character filter is applied after scanning the full suffix.
oxml-opc 0.14.2 returns normalized Target attributes using quick-xml 0.41; PartFs::resolve_rel_target assumes raw attributes and calls unescape_xml_text again. Repeated & in valid XML thus becomes consecutive bare ampersands before the second decoder. Target existence checks occur after resolution. Around one million decoded ampersands from roughly five MB of encoded input imply about 500 billion character inspections, a static operation estimate rather than a benchmark.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: unescape_xml_text rescans the remaining input for every unresolved ampersand, and the relationship adapter redundantly invokes it on values already decoded by its current OPC parser.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): The relationship consumer assumes raw attributes although its parser stores decoded values; its fallback entity scanner repeatedly scans the same suffix.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `Builder::text()` sends HTML text to `decode_entities()`. For every `&`, the decoder calls `tail.find(';')` on the remaining suffix and only then rejects positions over ten. Repeated ampersands without semicolons therefore cause quadratic scans. The assigned current-tree relationship round-trip assertion corroborates normalized targets independently of dependency-version assumptions, and the established internal story renderer resolves the target before checking whether the selected part exists.

previousFindings.remediation: Scan entities once without revisiting suffixes. In HTML, bound the search to the supported entity-length window before looking for ';'; give XML decoding a monotonic parser or bounded entity grammar. Remove PartFs's redundant relationship decoding when upstream supplies normalized attributes; retain the linear XML-helper repair for its other callers and the separate bounded HTML-helper repair. Preserve canonical literal '&' part names and one-time entity normalization through round trips. Preserve the standalone XML helper's documented permissive output for unsupported or unterminated references while making its work linear.

dataflow.summary: Builder::text passes imported HTML text to decode_entities. For each ampersand, the decoder scans the complete remaining suffix for a semicolon and only then filters the result to a maximum entity length of ten. If decoding fails it advances by one byte. A run of ampersands without semicolons therefore repeatedly scans overlapping suffixes.

dataflow.summary: The current oxml-opc reader decodes XML attribute entities when constructing Relationship.target. PartFs::resolve_rel_target nevertheless passes that already-decoded target through unescape_xml_text again. That helper searches the entire remaining character suffix for a semicolon on every ampersand. A valid Target attribute containing many & references consequently becomes a raw ampersand run before the second decoder and causes quadratic work.

impact.rationale: A shallow .rels part with a fontTable relationship whose Target is '&' repeated 100,000 times is roughly 500 KB. Rendering resolves this target through main_rel_part even if no corresponding package part exists. The second decoder performs approximately five billion character comparisons. The attack also reaches inspect/edit related-part resolution; malformed XML or an altChunk is unnecessary.
